5.62.d: ऋतेन ऋतमपिहितं ध्रुवं वां सूर्यस्य यत्र विमुचन्त्यश्वान् । दश शता सह तस्थुस्तदेकं देवानां श्रेष्ठं वपुषामपश्यम् ॥
5.62.e: BY your high Law firm order is established there where they loose for travel Sūrya's horses.  Ten hundred stood together: there I looked on this the most marvellous Deities' one chief glory.

5.62.d: तत्सु वां मित्रावरुणा महित्वमीर्मा तस्थुषीरहभिर्दुदुह्रे । विश्वाः पिन्वथः स्वसरस्य धेना अनु वामेकः पविरा ववर्त ॥
5.62.e: This, Mitra-Varuṇa, is your special greatness: floods that stood there they with the days attracted.  Ye cause to flow all voices of the cowpen: your single chariotfelly hath rolled hither.

5.62.d: अधारयतं पृथिवीमुत द्यां मित्रराजाना वरुणा महोभिः । वर्धयतमोषधीः पिन्वतं गा अव वृष्टिं सृजतं जीरदानू ॥
5.62.e: O Mitra-Varuṇa, ye by your greatness, both Kings, have firmly stablished earth and heaven,  Ye caused the cows to stream, the plants to flourish, and, scattering swift drops, sent down the rain-flood.

5.62.d: आ वामश्वासः सुयुजो वहन्तु यतरश्मय उप यन्त्वर्वाक् । घृतस्य निर्णिगनु वर्तते वामुप सिन्धवः प्रदिवि क्षरन्ति ॥
5.62.e: Let your well-harnessed horses bear you hither: hitherward let them come with reins drawn tightly.  A covering cloud of sacred oil attends you, and your streams flow to us from days aforetime.

5.62.d: अनु श्रुताममतिं वर्धदुर्वीं बर्हिरिव यजुषा रक्षमाणा । नमस्वन्ता धृतदक्षाधि गर्ते मित्रासाथे वरुणेळास्वन्तः ॥
5.62.e: To make the lustre wider and more famous, guarding the sacred grass with veneration,  Ye, Mitra-Varuṇa, firm, strong, awe-inspiring, are seated on a throne amid oblations.

5.62.d: अक्रविहस्ता सुकृते परस्पा यं त्रासाथे वरुणेळास्वन्तः । राजाना क्षत्रमहृणीयमाना सहस्रस्थूणं बिभृथः सह द्वौ ॥
5.62.e: With hands that shed no blood, guarding the pious, whom, Varuni3, ye save amid oblations.  Ye Twain, together, Kings of willing spirit, uphold dominion based on thousand pillars.

5.62.d: हिरण्यनिर्णिगयो अस्य स्थूणा वि भ्राजते दिव्य१श्वाजनीव । भद्रे क्षेत्रे निमिता तिल्विले वा सनेम मध्वो अधिगर्त्यस्य ॥
5.62.e: Adorned with gold, its columns are of iron. in heaven it glitters like a whip for horses;  Or stablished on a field deep-spoiled and fruitful. So may we share the meath that loads your car-seat.

5.62.d: हिरण्यरूपमुषसो व्युष्टावयःस्थूणमुदिता सूर्यस्य । आ रोहथो वरुण मित्र गर्तमतश्चक्षाथे अदितिं दितिं च ॥
5.62.e: Ye mount your car gold-hued at break of morning, and iron-pillared when the Sun is setting,  And from that place, O Varuṇa and Mitra, behold infinity and limit~tion.

5.62.d: यद्बंहिष्ठं नातिविधे सुदानू अच्छिद्रं शर्म भुवनस्य गोपा । तेन नो मित्रावरुणावविष्टं सिषासन्तो जिगीवांसः स्याम ॥
5.62.e: Bountiful guardians of the world! the shelter that is impenetrable, strongest, flawless,  Aid us with that, O Varuṇa and Mitra, and when we long to win may we be victors.

5.63.d: ऋतस्य गोपावधि तिष्ठथो रथं सत्यधर्माणा परमे व्योमनि । यमत्र मित्रावरुणावथो युवं तस्मै वृष्टिर्मधुमत्पिन्वते दिवः ॥
5.63.e: GUARDIANS of Order, ye whose Laws are ever true, in the sublimest heaven your chariot ye ascend.  O Mitra-Varuṇa whomsoe’er ye: favour, here, to him the rain with sweetness streameth down from heaven.

5.63.d: सम्राजावस्य भुवनस्य राजथो मित्रावरुणा विदथे स्वर्दृशा । वृष्टिं वां राधो अमृतत्वमीमहे द्यावापृथिवी वि चरन्ति तन्यवः ॥
5.63.e: This world's imperial Kings, O Mitra-Varuṇa, ye rule in holy synod, looking on the light.  We pray for rain, your boon, and immortality. Through heaven and over earth the thunderers take their way.

5.63.d: सम्राजा उग्रा वृषभा दिवस्पती पृथिव्या मित्रावरुणा विचर्षणी । चित्रेभिरभ्रैरुप तिष्ठथो रवं द्यां वर्षयथो असुरस्य मायया ॥
5.63.e: Imperial Kings, strong, Heroes, Lords of earth and heaven, Mitra and Varuṇa, ye ever active Ones,  Ye wait on thunder with the many-tinted clouds, and by the Asura's magic power cause Heaven to rain.

5.63.d: माया वां मित्रावरुणा दिवि श्रिता सूर्यो ज्योतिश्चरति चित्रमायुधम् । तमभ्रेण वृष्ट्या गूहथो दिवि पर्जन्य द्रप्सा मधुमन्त ईरते ॥
5.63.e: Your magic, Mitra-Varuṇa, resteth in the heaven. The Sun, the wondrous weapon, cometh forth as light.  Ye hide him in the sky with cloud and flood of rain, and water-drops, Parjanya! full of sweetness flow.

5.63.d: रथं युञ्जते मरुतः शुभे सुखं शूरो न मित्रावरुणा गविष्टिषु । रजांसि चित्रा वि चरन्ति तन्यवो दिवः सम्राजा पयसा न उक्षतम् ॥
5.63.e: The Maruts yoke their easy car for victory, O Mitra-Varuṇa, as a hero in the wars.  The thunderers roam through regions varied in their hues. Imperial Kings, bedew us with the milk of heaven.

5.63.d: वाचं सु मित्रावरुणाविरावतीं पर्जन्यश्चित्रां वदति त्विषीमतीम् । अभ्रा वसत मरुतः सु मायया द्यां वर्षयतमरुणामरेपसम् ॥
5.63.e: Refreshing is your voice, O Mitra-Varuṇa: Parjanya sendeth out a wondrous mighty voice.  With magic power the Maruts clothe them with the clouds. Ye Two cause Heaven to rain, the red, the spotless One.

5.63.d: धर्मणा मित्रावरुणा विपश्चिता व्रता रक्षेथे असुरस्य मायया । ऋतेन विश्वं भुवनं वि राजथः सूर्यमा धत्थो दिवि चित्र्यं रथम् ॥
5.63.e: Wise, with your Law and through the Asura's magic power ye guard the ordinances, Mitra-Varuṇa.  Ye by eternal Order govern all the world. Ye set the Sun in heaven as a refulgent car.

5.64.d: वरुणं वो रिशादसमृचा मित्रं हवामहे । परि व्रजेव बाह्वोर्जगन्वांसा स्वर्णरम् ॥
5.64.e: You, foeman-slaying Varuṇa and Mitra, we invoke with song,  Who, as with penfold of your arms, encompass round the realm of light.

5.64.d: ता बाहवा सुचेतुना प्र यन्तमस्मा अर्चते । शेवं हि जार्यं वां विश्वासु क्षासु जोगुवे ॥
5.64.e: Stretch out your arms with favouring love unto this man who singeth hymns,  For in all places is sung forth your evergracious friendliness.

5.64.d: यन्नूनमश्यां गतिं मित्रस्य यायां पथा । अस्य प्रियस्य शर्मण्यहिंसानस्य सश्चिरे ॥
5.64.e: That I may gain a refuge now, may my steps be on Mitra's path.  Men go protected in the charge of this dear Friend who harms us not.

5.64.d: युवाभ्यां मित्रावरुणोपमं धेयामृचा । यद्ध क्षये मघोनां स्तोतॄणां च स्पूर्धसे ॥
5.64.e: Mitra and Varuṇa, from you may I, by song, win noblest meed.  That shall stir envy in the homes of wealthy chiefs and those who praise.

5.64.d: आ नो मित्र सुदीतिभिर्वरुणश्च सधस्थ आ । स्वे क्षये मघोनां सखीनां च वृधसे ॥
5.64.e: With your fair splendours, Varuṇa and Mitra, to our gathering come,  That in their homes the wealthy chiefs and they who are your friends may thrive.

5.64.d: युवं नो येषु वरुण क्षत्रं बृहच्च बिभृथः । उरु णो वाजसातये कृतं राये स्वस्तये ॥
5.64.e: With those, moreover, among whom ye hold your high supremacy,  Vouchsafe us room that we may win strength for prosperity and wealth.

5.64.d: उच्छन्त्यां मे यजता देवक्षत्रे रुशद्गवि । सुतं सोमं न हस्तिभिरा पड्भिर्धावतं नरा बिभ्रतावर्चनानसम् ॥
5.64.e: When morning flushes, Holy Ones! in the Gods’ realm where white Cows shine,  Supporting Arcananas, speed, ye Heroes, with your active feet hither to my pressed Soma juice.

5.65.d: यश्चिकेत स सुक्रतुर्देवत्रा स ब्रवीतु नः । वरुणो यस्य दर्शतो मित्रो वा वनते गिरः ॥
5.65.e: FULL wise is he who hath discerned: let him speak to us of the Gods,—  The man whose praise-songs Varuṇa the beautiful, or Mitra, loves.

5.65.d: ता हि श्रेष्ठवर्चसा राजाना दीर्घश्रुत्तमा । ता सत्पती ऋतावृध ऋतावाना जनेजने ॥
5.65.e: For they are Kings of noblest might, of glorious fame most widely spread;  Lords of the brave, who strengthen Law, the Holy Ones with every race.

5.65.d: ता वामियानोऽवसे पूर्वा उप ब्रुवे सचा । स्वश्वासः सु चेतुना वाजाँ अभि प्र दावने ॥
5.65.e: Approaching you with prayer for aid, together I address you first  We who have good steeds call on you, Most Sage, to give us strength besides.

5.65.d: मित्रो अंहोश्चिदादुरु क्षयाय गातुं वनते । मित्रस्य हि प्रतूर्वतः सुमतिरस्ति विधतः ॥
5.65.e: E’en out of misery Mitra gives a way to dwelling at our case,  For he who worships hath the grace of Mitra, fighter in the van. '

5.65.d: वयं मित्रस्यावसि स्याम सप्रथस्तमे । अनेहसस्त्वोतयः सत्रा वरुणशेषसः ॥
5.65.e: In Mitra's shelter that extends to utmost distance may we dwell,  Unmenaced, guarded by the care, ever as sons of Varuṇa.

5.65.d: युवं मित्रेमं जनं यतथः सं च नयथः । मा मघोनः परि ख्यतं मो अस्माकमृषीणां गोपीथे न उरुष्यतम् ॥
5.65.e: Ye, Mitra, urge this people on, and to one end direct their ways.  Neglect not ye the wealthy chiefs, neglect not us the Ṛṣis: be our guardians when ye quaff the milk.

5.66.d: आ चिकितान सुक्रतू देवौ मर्त रिशादसा । वरुणाय ऋतपेशसे दधीत प्रयसे महे ॥
5.66.e: O SAPIENT man, call the Two Gods, the very wise, who slay the foe.  For Varuṇa, whose form is Law, place offerings for his great delight.

5.66.d: ता हि क्षत्रमविह्रुतं सम्यगसुर्य१माशाते । अध व्रतेव मानुषं स्व१र्ण धायि दर्शतम् ॥
5.66.e: For they have won unbroken sway in full perfection, power divine.  And, like high laws, the world of man hath been made beautiful as light.

5.66.d: ता वामेषे रथानामुर्वीं गव्यूतिमेषाम् । रातहव्यस्य सुष्टुतिं दधृक्स्तोमैर्मनामहे ॥
5.66.e: Therefore we praise you that your cars may travel far in front of ours-  You who accept the eulogy of Ratahavya with his hymns.

5.66.d: अधा हि काव्या युवं दक्षस्य पूर्भिरद्भुता । नि केतुना जनानां चिकेथे पूतदक्षसा ॥
5.66.e: And ye show wMom, Wondrous Gods with fulness of intellIgence.  By men's discernment are Ve marked, O ye whose might is purified.

5.66.d: तदृतं पृथिवि बृहच्छ्रवएष ऋषीणाम् । ज्रयसानावरं पृथ्वति क्षरन्ति यामभिः ॥
5.66.e: This is the Law sublime, O Earth: to aid the Ṛṣis’ toil for fame  The Two, wide-spreading, are prepared. They come with ample overflow.

5.66.d: आ यद्वामीयचक्षसा मित्र वयं च सूरयः । व्यचिष्ठे बहुपाय्ये यतेमहि स्वराज्ये ॥
5.66.e: Mitra, ye Gods with wandering eyes, would that the worshippers and we  Might strive to reach the realm ye rule, most spacious and protected well,

5.67.d: बळित्था देव निष्कृतमादित्या यजतं बृहत् । वरुण मित्रार्यमन्वर्षिष्ठं क्षत्रमाशाथे ॥
5.67.e: YE Gods, Ādityas, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Mitra, verily  Have here obtained supremest sway, high, holy, set apart for you.

5.67.d: आ यद्योनिं हिरण्ययं वरुण मित्र सदथः । धर्तारा चर्षणीनां यन्तं सुम्नं रिशादसा ॥
5.67.e: When, Varuṇa and Mitra, ye sit in your golden dwelling-place,  Ye Twain, supporters of mankind, foeslayers, give felicity.

5.67.d: विश्वे हि विश्ववेदसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा । व्रता पदेव सश्चिरे पान्ति मर्त्यं रिषः ॥
5.67.e: All these, possessors of all wealth, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman,  Follow their ways, as if with feet, and guard from injury mortal man.

5.67.d: ते हि सत्या ऋतस्पृश ऋतावानो जनेजने । सुनीथासः सुदानवोंऽहोश्चिदुरुचक्रयः ॥
5.67.e: For they are true, they cleave to Law, held holy among every race,  Good leaders, bounteous in their gifts, deliverers even from distress.

5.67.d: को नु वां मित्रास्तुतो वरुणो वा तनूनाम् । तत्सु वामेषते मतिरत्रिभ्य एषते मतिः ॥
5.67.e: Which of your persons, Varuṇa or Mitra, merits not our praise?  Therefore our thought is turned to you, the Atris' thought is turned to you.

5.68.d: प्र वो मित्राय गायत वरुणाय विपा गिरा । महिक्षत्रावृतं बृहत् ॥
5.68.e: SING forth unto your Varuṇa and Mitra with a song inspired.  They, Mighty Lords, are lofty Law

5.68.d: सम्राजा या घृतयोनी मित्रश्चोभा वरुणश्च । देवा देवेषु प्रशस्ता ॥
5.68.e: Full springs of fatness, Sovran Kings, Mitra. and Varuṇa, the Twain,  Gods glorified among the Gods.

5.68.d: ता नः शक्तं पार्थिवस्य महो रायो दिव्यस्य । महि वां क्षत्रं देवेषु ॥
5.68.e: So help ye us to riches, great terrestrial and celestial wealth:  Vast is your sway among the Gods.

5.68.d: ऋतमृतेन सपन्तेषिरं दक्षमाशाते । अद्रुहा देवौ वर्धेते ॥
5.68.e: Carefully tending Law with Law they have attained their vigorous might.  The two Gods wax devoid of guile.
With rainy skies and streaming floods, Lords of the strength that bringeth gifts,  A lofty seat have they attained.

5.69.d: त्री रोचना वरुण त्रीँरुत द्यून्त्रीणि मित्र धारयथो रजांसि । वावृधानावमतिं क्षत्रियस्यानु व्रतं रक्षमाणावजुर्यम् ॥
5.69.e: THREE spheres of light, O Varuṇa, three heavens, three firmaments ye comprehend, O Mitra:  Waxed strong, ye keep the splendour of dominion, guarding the Ordinance that lasts for ever.

5.69.d: इरावतीर्वरुण धेनवो वां मधुमद्वां सिन्धवो मित्र दुह्रे । त्रयस्तस्थुर्वृषभासस्तिसृणां धिषणानां रेतोधा वि द्युमन्तः ॥
5.69.e: Ye, Varuṇa, have kine who yield refreshment; Mitra, your floods pour water full of sweetness.  There stand the Three Steers, splendid in their brightness, who fill the three world-bowls with genial moisture.

5.69.d: प्रातर्देवीमदितिं जोहवीमि मध्यंदिन उदिता सूर्यस्य । राये मित्रावरुणा सर्वतातेळे तोकाय तनयाय शं योः ॥
5.69.e: I call at dawn on Aditi the Goddess, I call at noon and when the Sun is setting.  I pray, O Mitra-Varuṇa, for safety, for wealth and progeny, in rest and trouble.

5.69.d: या धर्तारा रजसो रोचनस्योतादित्या दिव्या पार्थिवस्य । न वां देवा अमृता आ मिनन्ति व्रतानि मित्रावरुणा ध्रुवाणि ॥
5.69.e: Ye who uphold the region, sphere of brightness, ye who support earth's realm Divine Ādityas,  The Immortal Gods, O Varuṇa and Mitra, never impair your everlasting statutes.

5.70.d: पुरूरुणा चिद्ध्यस्त्यवो नूनं वां वरुण । मित्र वंसि वां सुमतिम् ॥
5.70.e: EVEN far and wide, O Varuṇa and Mitra, doth your grace extend.  May I obtain your kind good-will.

5.70.d: ता वां सम्यगद्रुह्वाणेषमश्याम धायसे । वयं ते रुद्रा स्याम ॥
5.70.e: From you, benignant Gods, may we gain fully food for sustenance.  Such, O ye Rudras, my we be.

5.70.d: पातं नो रुद्रा पायुभिरुत त्रायेथां सुत्रात्रा । तुर्याम दस्यून्तनूभिः ॥
5.70.e: Guard us, O Rudras. with your guar4 save us, ye skilled to save, my we  Subdue the Dasyus, we ourselves,

5.70.d: मा कस्याद्भुतक्रतू यक्षं भुजेमा तनूभिः । मा शेषसा मा तनसा ॥
5.70.e: Or ne’er may we, O Wondrous Strong, enjoy another's solemn feast,  Ourselves, our sons, or progeny.

5.71.d: आ नो गन्तं रिशादसा वरुण मित्र बर्हणा । उपेमं चारुमध्वरम् ॥
5.71.e: O Varuṇa and Mitra, ye who slay the foemen, come with might  To this our goodly sacrifice.

5.71.d: विश्वस्य हि प्रचेतसा वरुण मित्र राजथः । ईशाना पिप्यतं धियः ॥
5.71.e: For, Varuṇa and Mitra, ye Sages are Rulers over all. Fill full our songs, for this ye can.

5.71.d: उप नः सुतमा गतं वरुण मित्र दाशुषः । अस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥
5.71.e: Come to the juice that we have pressed. Varuṇa, Mitra, come to drink  This Soma of the worshipper.

5.72.d: आ मित्रे वरुणे वयं गीर्भिर्जुहुमो अत्रिवत् । नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोमपीतये ॥
5.72.e: To Varuṇa and Mitra we offer with songs, as Atri did. Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.

5.72.d: व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातयज्जना । नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोमपीतये ॥
5.72.e: By Ordinance and Law ye dwell in peace secure, bestirring men.  Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.

5.72.d: मित्रश्च नो वरुणश्च जुषेतां यज्ञमिष्टये । नि बर्हिषि सदतां सोमपीतये ॥
5.72.e: May Varuṇa and Mitra, for our help, accept the sacrifice.  Sit on the sacred grass to drink the Soma juice.

5.73.d: यदद्य स्थः परावति यदर्वावत्यश्विना । यद्वा पुरू पुरुभुजा यदन्तरिक्ष आ गतम् ॥
5.73.e: WHETHER, O Aśvins, ye this day be far remote or near at hand,  In many spots or in mid-air, come hither, Lords of ample wealth.

5.73.d: इह त्या पुरुभूतमा पुरू दंसांसि बिभ्रता । वरस्या याम्यध्रिगू हुवे तुविष्टमा भुजे ॥
5.73.e: These here, who show o’er widest space, bringing full many a wondrous act,  Resistless, lovingly I seek, I call the Mightiest to enjoy.

5.73.d: ईर्मान्यद्वपुषे वपुश्चक्रं रथस्य येमथुः । पर्यन्या नाहुषा युगा मह्ना रजांसि दीयथः ॥
5.73.e: Another beauteous wheel have ye fixed there to decorate your car.  With others through the realms ye roam in might unto the neighbouring tribes.

5.73.d: तदू षु वामेना कृतं विश्वा यद्वामनु ष्टवे । नाना जातावरेपसा समस्मे बन्धुमेयथुः ॥
5.73.e: That deed of yours that is extolled, Visvas! hath all been done with this.  Born otherwise, and spotless, ye have entered kinship's bonds with us.

5.73.d: आ यद्वां सूर्या रथं तिष्ठद्रघुष्यदं सदा । परि वामरुषा वयो घृणा वरन्त आतपः ॥
5.73.e: When Sūrya mounted on your car that rolls for ever rapidly,  Birds of red hue were round about and burning splendours compassed you.

5.73.d: युवोरत्रिश्चिकेतति नरा सुम्नेन चेतसा । घर्मं यद्वामरेपसं नासत्यास्ना भुरण्यति ॥
5.73.e: Atri bethinks himself of you, O Heroes, with a friendly mind,  What time, Nāsatyas, with his mouth he stirs the spotless flame for you.

5.73.d: उग्रो वां ककुहो ययिः शृण्वे यामेषु संतनिः । यद्वां दंसोभिरश्विनात्रिर्नराववर्तति ॥
5.73.e: Strong is your swiftly moving steed, famed his exertion in the course  When by your great deeds, Aśvins, Chiefs, Atri is brought to us again.

5.73.d: मध्व ऊ षु मधूयुवा रुद्रा सिषक्ति पिप्युषी । यत्समुद्राति पर्षथः पक्वाः पृक्षो भरन्त वाम् ॥
5.73.e: Lovers of sweetness, Rudras, she who streams with sweetness waits on you.  When ye have travelled through the seas men bring you gifts of well-dressed food.

5.73.d: सत्यमिद्वा उ अश्विना युवामाहुर्मयोभुवा । ता यामन्यामहूतमा यामन्ना मृळयत्तमा ॥
5.73.e: Aśvins, with truth they call you Twain bestowers of felicity;  At sacrifice most prompt to hear, most gracious ye at sacrifice.

5.73.d: इमा ब्रह्माणि वर्धनाश्विभ्यां सन्तु शंतमा । या तक्षाम रथाँ इवावोचाम बृहन्नमः ॥
5.73.e: Most pleasing to the Aśvins be these prayers which magnify their might,  Which we have fashioned, even as cars high reverence have we spoken forth.

5.74.d: कूष्ठो देवावश्विनाद्या दिवो मनावसू । तच्छ्रवथो वृषण्वसू अत्रिर्वामा विवासति ॥
5.74.e: WHERE in the heavens are ye to-day, Gods, Aśvins, rich in constancy?  Hear this, ye excellent as Steers: Atri inviteth you to come.

5.74.d: कुह त्या कुह नु श्रुता दिवि देवा नासत्या । कस्मिन्ना यतथो जने को वां नदीनां सचा ॥
5.74.e: Where are they now? Where are the Twain, the famed Nāsatyas, Gods in heaven?  Who is the man ye strive to reach? Who of your suppliants is with you?

5.74.d: कं याथः कं ह गच्छथः कमच्छा युञ्जाथे रथम् । कस्य ब्रह्माणि रण्यथो वयं वामुश्मसीष्टये ॥
5.74.e: Whom do ye visit, whom approach? to whom direct your harnessed car?  With whose devotions are ye pleased? We long for you to further us.

5.74.d: पौरं चिद्ध्युदप्रुतं पौर पौराय जिन्वथः । यदीं गृभीततातये सिंहमिव द्रुहस्पदे ॥
5.74.e: Ye, Strengtheners, for Paura stir the filler swimming in the flood,  Advancing to be captured like a lion to the ambuscade.

5.74.d: प्र च्यवानाज्जुजुरुषो वव्रिमत्कं न मुञ्चथः । युवा यदी कृथः पुनरा काममृण्वे वध्वः ॥
5.74.e: Ye from cyavana worn with age removed his skin as ’twere a robe.  So, when ye made him young again, he stirred the longing of a dame.

5.74.d: अस्ति हि वामिह स्तोता स्मसि वां संदृशि श्रिये । नू श्रुतं म आ गतमवोभिर्वाजिनीवसू ॥
5.74.e: Here is the man who lauds you both: to see your glory are we here.  Now bear me, come with saving help, ye who are rich in store of wealth.

5.74.d: को वामद्य पुरूणामा वव्ने मर्त्यानाम् । को विप्रो विप्रवाहसा को यज्ञैर्वाजिनीवसू ॥
5.74.e: Who among many mortal men this day hath won you to himself?  What bard, accepters of the bard? Who, rich in wealth! with sacrifice?

5.74.d: आ वां रथो रथानां येष्ठो यात्वश्विना । पुरू चिदस्मयुस्तिर आङ्गूषो मर्त्येष्वा ॥
5.74.e: O Aśvins, may your car approach, most excellent of cars for speed.  Through many regions may our praise pass onward among mortal men.

5.74.d: शमू षु वां मधूयुवास्माकमस्तु चर्कृतिः । अर्वाचीना विचेतसा विभिः श्येनेव दीयतम् ॥
5.74.e: May our laudation of you Twain, lovers of meath! be sweet to you.  Fly hitherward, ye wise of heart, like falcons with your winged steeds.

5.74.d: अश्विना यद्ध कर्हि चिच्छुश्रूयातमिमं हवम् । वस्वीरू षु वां भुजः पृञ्चन्ति सु वां पृचः ॥
5.74.e: O Aśvins, when at any time ye listen to this call of mine,  For you is dainty food prepared: they mix refreshing food for you.

5.75.d: प्रति प्रियतमं रथं वृषणं वसुवाहनम् । स्तोता वामश्विनावृषिः स्तोमेन प्रति भूषति माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: To meet your treasure-bringing car, the mighty car most dear to us,  Aśvins, the Ṛṣi is prepared, your raiser, with his song of praise. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: अत्यायातमश्विना तिरो विश्वा अहं सना । दस्रा हिरण्यवर्तनी सुषुम्ना सिन्धुवाहसा माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: Pass, O ye Aśvins, pass away beyond all tribes of selfish men,  Wonderful, with your golden paths, most gracious, bringers of the flood. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: आ नो रत्नानि बिभ्रतावश्विना गच्छतं युवम् । रुद्रा हिरण्यवर्तनी जुषाणा वाजिनीवसू माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: Come to us, O ye Aśvin Pair, bringing your precious treasures, come  Ye Rudras, on your paths of gold, rejoicing, rich in store of wealth. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: सुष्टुभो वां वृषण्वसू रथे वाणीच्याहिता । उत वां ककुहो मृगः पृक्षः कृणोति वापुषो माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: O strong and Good, the voice of him who lauds you well cleaves to your car.  And that great beast, your chariot-steed, fair, wonderful, makes dainty food. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: बोधिन्मनसा रथ्येषिरा हवनश्रुता । विभिश्च्यवानमश्विना नि याथो अद्वयाविनं माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: Watchful in spirit, born on cars, impetuous, listing to his cry,  Aśvins, with winged steeds ye speed down to cyavana void of guile. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: आ वां नरा मनोयुजोऽश्वासः प्रुषितप्सवः । वयो वहन्तु पीतये सह सुम्नेभिरश्विना माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: Hither, O Heroes, let your steeds, of dappled hue, yoked at the thought,  Your flying steeds, O Aśvins, bring you hitherward, with bliss, to drink. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: अश्विनावेह गच्छतं नासत्या मा वि वेनतम् । तिरश्चिदर्यया परि वर्तिर्यातमदाभ्या माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: O Aśvins, hither come to us; Nāsatyas, be not disinclined.  Through longing for the pious turn out of the way to reach our home. Lovers of sweetness, bear my call.

5.75.d: अस्मिन्यज्ञे अदाभ्या जरितारं शुभस्पती । अवस्युमश्विना युवं गृणन्तमुप भूषथो माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: Ye Lords of Splendour, free from guile, come, stand at this our sacrifice.  Beside the singer, Aśvins, who longs for your grace and lauds you both. Lovers of sweetness, hear my call.

5.75.d: अभूदुषा रुशत्पशुराग्निरधाय्यृत्वियः । अयोजि वां वृषण्वसू रथो दस्रावमर्त्यो माध्वी मम श्रुतं हवम् ॥
5.75.e: Dawn with her white herd hath appeared, and in due time hath fire been placed.  Harnessed is your immortal car, O WonderWorkers, strong and kind. Lovers of sweetness, bear my call.

5.76.d: आ भात्यग्निरुषसामनीकमुद्विप्राणां देवया वाचो अस्थुः । अर्वाञ्चा नूनं रथ्येह यातं पीपिवांसमश्विना घर्ममच्छ ॥
5.76.e: AGNI, the bright face of the Dawns, is shining; the singers' pious voices have ascended.  Borne on your chariot, Aśvins, turn you hither and come unto our full and rich libation.

5.76.d: न संस्कृतं प्र मिमीतो गमिष्ठान्ति नूनमश्विनोपस्तुतेह । दिवाभिपित्वेऽवसागमिष्ठा प्रत्यवर्तिं दाशुषे शम्भविष्ठा ॥
5.76.e: Most frequent guests, they scorn not what is ready: even now the lauded Aśvins are beside us.  With promptest aid they come at morn and evening, the worshipper's most blessed guards from trouble.

5.76.d: उता यातं संगवे प्रातरह्नो मध्यंदिन उदिता सूर्यस्य । दिवा नक्तमवसा शंतमेन नेदानीं पीतिरश्विना ततान ॥
5.76.e: Yea, come at milking-time, at early morning, at noon of day and when the Sun is setting,  By day, by night, with favour most auspicious. Not only now the draught hath drawn the Aśvins.

5.76.d: इदं हि वां प्रदिवि स्थानमोक इमे गृहा अश्विनेदं दुरोणम् । आ नो दिवो बृहतः पर्वतादाद्भ्यो यातमिषमूर्जं वहन्ता ॥
5.76.e: For this place, Aśvins, was of old your dwelling, these were your houses, this your habitation.  Come to us from high heaven and from the mountain. Come from the waters bringing food and vigour.

5.76.d: समश्विनोरवसा नूतनेन मयोभुवा सुप्रणीती गमेम । आ नो रयिं वहतमोत वीराना विश्वान्यमृता सौभगानि ॥
5.76.e: May we obtain the Aśvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance.  Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!

5.77.d: प्रातर्यावाणा प्रथमा यजध्वं पुरा गृध्रादररुषः पिबातः । प्रातर्हि यज्ञमश्विना दधाते प्र शंसन्ति कवयः पूर्वभाजः ॥
5.77.e: FIRST worship those who come at early morning: let the Twain drink before the giftless niggard.  The Aśvins claim the sacrifice at daybreak: the sages yielding the first share extol them.

5.77.d: प्रातर्यजध्वमश्विना हिनोत न सायमस्ति देवया अजुष्टम् । उतान्यो अस्मद्यजते वि चावः पूर्वःपूर्वो यजमानो वनीयान् ॥
5.77.e: Worship at dawn and instigate the Aśvins: nor is the worshipper at eve rejected.  Besides ourselves another craves and worships: each first in worship is most highly favoured.

5.77.d: हिरण्यत्वङ्मधुवर्णो घृतस्नुः पृक्षो वहन्ना रथो वर्तते वाम् । मनोजवा अश्विना वातरंहा येनातियाथो दुरितानि विश्वा ॥
5.77.e: Covered with gold, meath-tinted, dropping fatness, your chariot with its freight of food comes hither,  Swift as thought, Aśvins, rapid as the tempest, wherewith ye travel over all obstructions.

5.77.d: यो भूयिष्ठं नासत्याभ्यां विवेष चनिष्ठं पित्वो ररते विभागे । स तोकमस्य पीपरच्छमीभिरनूर्ध्वभासः सदमित्तुतुर्यात् ॥
5.77.e: He who hath served most often the Nāsatyas, and gives the sweetest food at distribution,  Furthers with his own holy works his offspring, and ever passes those whose flames ascend not.

5.77.d: समश्विनोरवसा नूतनेन मयोभुवा सुप्रणीती गमेम । आ नो रयिं वहतमोत वीराना विश्वान्यमृता सौभगानि ॥
5.77.e: May we obtain the Aśvins' newest favour, and gain their health-bestowing happy guidance.  Bring riches hither unto us, and heroes, and all felicity and joy, Immortals!

5.78.d: अश्विनावेह गच्छतं नासत्या मा वि वेनतम् । हंसाविव पततमा सुताँ उप ॥
5.78.e: YE Aśvins, hither come to us: Nāsatyas, be not disinclined.  Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.

5.78.d: अश्विना हरिणाविव गौराविवानु यवसम् । हंसाविव पततमा सुताँ उप ॥
5.78.e: O Aśvins, like a pair of deer, like two wild cattle to the mead:  Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.

5.78.d: अश्विना वाजिनीवसू जुषेथां यज्ञमिष्टये । हंसाविव पततमा सुताँ उप ॥
5.78.e: O Aśvins rich in gifts, accept our sacrifice to prosper it:  Fly hither like two swans unto the juice we shed.

5.78.d: अत्रिर्यद्वामवरोहन्नृबीसमजोहवीन्नाधमानेव योषा । श्येनस्य चिज्जवसा नूतनेनागच्छतमश्विना शंतमेन ॥
5.78.e: As Atri when descending to the cavern called on you loudly like a wailing woman.  Ye came to him, O Aśvins, with the freshest and most auspicious fleetness of a falcon.

5.78.d: वि जिहीष्व वनस्पते योनिः सूष्यन्त्या इव । श्रुतं मे अश्विना हवं सप्तवध्रिं च मुञ्चतम् ॥
5.78.e: Tree, part asunder like the side of her who bringeth forth a child.  Ye Aśvins, listen to my call: loose Saptavadhri from his bonds.

5.78.d: भीताय नाधमानाय ऋषये सप्तवध्रये । मायाभिरश्विना युवं वृक्षं सं च वि चाचथः ॥
5.78.e: For Saptavadhri, for the seer affrighted when he wept and wailed,  Ye, Aśvins, with your magic powers rent up the tree and shattered it.

5.78.d: यथा वातः पुष्करिणीं समिङ्गयति सर्वतः । एवा ते गर्भ एजतु निरैतु दशमास्यः ॥
5.78.e: Like as the wind on every side ruffles a pool of lotuses,  So stir in thee the babe unborn, so may the ten-month babe descend.

5.78.d: यथा वातो यथा वनं यथा समुद्र एजति । एवा त्वं दशमास्य सहावेहि जरायुणा ॥
5.78.e: Like as the wind, like as the wood, like as the sea is set astir,  So also, ten-month babe, descend together with the after-birth.

5.78.d: दश मासाञ्छशयानः कुमारो अधि मातरि । निरैतु जीवो अक्षतो जीवो जीवन्त्या अधि ॥
5.78.e: The child who hath for ten months' time been lying in his mother's side,—  May he come forth alive, unharmed, yea, living from the living dame.

5.79.d: महे नो अद्य बोधयोषो राये दिवित्मती । यथा चिन्नो अबोधयः सत्यश्रवसि वाय्ये सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: O HEAVENLY Dawn, awaken us to ample opulence to-day  Even as thou hast wakened us with Satyasravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: या सुनीथे शौचद्रथे व्यौच्छो दुहितर्दिवः । सा व्युच्छ सहीयसि सत्यश्रवसि वाय्ये सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: Daughter of Heaven, thou dawnedst on Sunitha Sucadratha's son,  So dawn thou on one mightier still, on Satyasravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: सा नो अद्याभरद्वसुर्व्युच्छा दुहितर्दिवः । यो व्यौच्छः सहीयसि सत्यश्रवसि वाय्ये सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: So, bringing treasure, dawn to-day on us thou Daughter of the Sky,  As thou, O mightier yet. didst shine for Satyatravas, Vayya's son, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: अभि ये त्वा विभावरि स्तोमैर्गृणन्ति वह्नयः । मघैर्मघोनि सुश्रियो दामन्वन्तः सुरातयः सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: Here round about thee are the priests who laud thee, Bright One, with their hymns,  And men with gifts, O Bounteous Dame, splendid with wealth and offering much, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: यच्चिद्धि ते गणा इमे छदयन्ति मघत्तये । परि चिद्वष्टयो दधुर्ददतो राधो अह्रयं सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: Whatever these thy bands perform to please thee or to win them wealth,  E’en fain they gird us round and give rich gifts which ne’er are reft away, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: ऐषु धा वीरवद्यश उषो मघोनि सूरिषु । ये नो राधांस्यह्रया मघवानो अरासत सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: Give to these wealthy patrons fame, O affluent Dawn, with hero sons,  To these our princes who have brought rich gifts ne’er to be reft away, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: तेभ्यो द्युम्नं बृहद्यश उषो मघोन्या वह । ये नो राधांस्यश्व्या गव्या भजन्त सूरयः सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: Bring lofty and resplendent fame, O thou munificent Dawn, to these  Our wealthy patrons who bestow rich gifts on us of steeds and kine, high-born! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: उत नो गोमतीरिष आ वहा दुहितर्दिवः । साकं सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः शुक्रैः शोचद्भिरर्चिभिः सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: Bring us, O Daughter of the Sky, subsistence in our herds of kine,  Together with the sunbeams, with the shine of pure refulgent flames, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!

5.79.d: व्युच्छा दुहितर्दिवो मा चिरं तनुथा अपः । नेत्त्वा स्तेनं यथा रिपुं तपाति सूरो अर्चिषा सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: O Daughter of the Sky, shine forth; delay not to perform thy task.  Let not the Sun with fervent heat consume thee like a robber foe, high-born! delightful with the steeds!

5.79.d: एतावद्वेदुषस्त्वं भूयो वा दातुमर्हसि । या स्तोतृभ्यो विभावर्युच्छन्ती न प्रमीयसे सुजाते अश्वसूनृते ॥
5.79.e: So much, and more exceedingly, O Dawn, it suits thee to bestow,  Thou Radiant One who ceasest not to shine for those who sing thy praise, highborn! delightful with thy steeds!

5.80.d: द्युतद्यामानं बृहतीमृतेन ऋतावरीमरुणप्सुं विभातीम् । देवीमुषसं स्वरावहन्तीं प्रति विप्रासो मतिभिर्जरन्ते ॥
5.80.e: THE singers welcome with their hymns and praises the Goddess Dawn who bringeth in the sunlight,  Sublime, by Law true to eternal Order, bright on her path, red-tinted, far-refulgent.

5.80.d: एषा जनं दर्शता बोधयन्ती सुगान्पथः कृण्वती यात्यग्रे । बृहद्रथा बृहती विश्वमिन्वोषा ज्योतिर्यच्छत्यग्रे अह्नाम् ॥
5.80.e: She comes in front, fair, rousing up the people, making the pathways easy to be travelled.  High, on her lofty chariot, all-impelling, Dawn gives her splendour at the days' beginning.

5.80.d: एषा गोभिररुणेभिर्युजानास्रेधन्ती रयिमप्रायु चक्रे । पथो रदन्ती सुविताय देवी पुरुष्टुता विश्ववारा वि भाति ॥
5.80.e: She, harnessing her car with purple oxen. injuring none, hath brought perpetual riches.  Opening paths to happiness, the Goddess shines, praised by all, giver of every blessing.

5.80.d: एषा व्येनी भवति द्विबर्हा आविष्कृण्वाना तन्वं पुरस्तात् । ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेति साधु प्रजानतीव न दिशो मिनाति ॥
5.80.e: With changing tints she gleams in double splendour while from the eastward she displays her body.  She travels perfectly the path of Order, nor fails to reach, as one who knows, the quarters.

5.80.d: एषा शुभ्रा न तन्वो विदानोर्ध्वेव स्नाती दृशये नो अस्थात् । अप द्वेषो बाधमाना तमांस्युषा दिवो दुहिता ज्योतिषागात् ॥
5.80.e: As conscious that her limbs are bright with bathing, she stands, as ’twere, erect that we may see her.  Driving away malignity and darkness, Dawn, Child of Heaven, hath come to us with lustre.

5.80.d: एषा प्रतीची दुहिता दिवो नॄन्योषेव भद्रा नि रिणीते अप्सः । व्यूर्ण्वती दाशुषे वार्याणि पुनर्ज्योतिर्युवतिः पूर्वथाकः ॥
5.80.e: The Daughter of the Sky, like some chaste woman, bends, opposite to men, her forehead downward.  The Maid, disclosing boons to him who worships, hath brought again the daylight as aforetime.

5.81.d: युञ्जते मन उत युञ्जते धियो विप्रा विप्रस्य बृहतो विपश्चितः । वि होत्रा दधे वयुनाविदेक इन्मही देवस्य सवितुः परिष्टुतिः ॥
5.81.e: THE priests of him the lofty Priest well-skilled in hymns harness their spirit, yea, harness their holy thoughts.  He only knowing works assigns their priestly tasks. Yea, lofty is the praise of Savitar the God.

5.81.d: विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुञ्चते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । वि नाकमख्यत्सविता वरेण्योऽनु प्रयाणमुषसो वि राजति ॥
5.81.e: The Sapient One arrays himself in every form: for quadruped and biped he hath brought forth good.  Excellent Savitar hath looked on heaven's high vault, and shineth after the outgoing of the Dawn.

5.81.d: यस्य प्रयाणमन्वन्य इद्ययुर्देवा देवस्य महिमानमोजसा । यः पार्थिवानि विममे स एतशो रजांसि देवः सविता महित्वना ॥
5.81.e: Even he, the God whose going-forth and majesty the other Deities have followed with their might,  He who hath measured the terrestrial regions out by his great power, he is the Courser Savitar.

5.81.d: उत यासि सवितस्त्रीणि रोचनोत सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः समुच्यसि । उत रात्रीमुभयतः परीयस उत मित्रो भवसि देव धर्मभिः ॥
5.81.e: To the three spheres of light thou goest, Savitar, and with the rays of Sidrya thou combinest thee.  Around, on both sides thou encompassest the night: yea, thou, O God, art Mitra through thy righteous laws.

5.81.d: उतेशिषे प्रसवस्य त्वमेक इदुत पूषा भवसि देव यामभिः । उतेदं विश्वं भुवनं वि राजसि श्यावाश्वस्ते सवितः स्तोममानशे ॥
5.81.e: Over all generation thou art Lord alone: Pūṣan art thou, O God, in all thy goings-forth.  Yea, thou hast domination over all this world. Śyāvāśva hath brought praise to thee, O Savitar,

5.82.d: तत्सवितुर्वृणीमहे वयं देवस्य भोजनम् । श्रेष्ठं सर्वधातमं तुरं भगस्य धीमहि ॥
5.82.e: WE crave of Savitar the God this treasure much to be enjoyed.  The best, all-yielding, conquering gift of Bhaga we would gladly win.

5.82.d: अस्य हि स्वयशस्तरं सवितुः कच्चन प्रियम् । न मिनन्ति स्वराज्यम् ॥
5.82.e: Savitar's own supremacy, most glorious and beloved of all,  No one diminisheth in aught.

5.82.d: स हि रत्नानि दाशुषे सुवाति सविता भगः । तं भागं चित्रमीमहे ॥
5.82.e: For Savitar who is Bhaga shall send riches to his worshipper.  That wondrous portion we implore.

5.82.d: अद्या नो देव सवितः प्रजावत्सावीः सौभगम् । परा दुष्ष्वप्न्यं सुव ॥
5.82.e: Send us this day, God Savitar, prosperity with progeny.  Drive thou the evil dream away.

5.82.d: विश्वानि देव सवितर्दुरितानि परा सुव । यद्भद्रं तन्न आ सुव ॥
5.82.e: Savitar, God, send far away all sorrows and calamities,  And send us only what is good.

5.82.d: अनागसो अदितये देवस्य सवितुः सवे । विश्वा वामानि धीमहि ॥
5.82.e: Sinless in sight of Aditi through the God Savitar's influence,  May we obtain all lovely things.

5.82.d: आ विश्वदेवं सत्पतिं सूक्तैरद्या वृणीमहे । सत्यसवं सवितारम् ॥
5.82.e: We with our hymns this day elect the general God, Lord of the good,  Savitar whose decrees are true.

5.82.d: य इमे उभे अहनी पुर एत्यप्रयुच्छन् । स्वाधीर्देवः सविता ॥
5.82.e: He who for ever vigilant precedes these Twain, the Day and Night,  Is Savitar the thoughtful God.

5.82.d: य इमा विश्वा जातान्याश्रावयति श्लोकेन । प्र च सुवाति सविता ॥
5.82.e: He who gives glory unto all these living creatures with the song,  And brings them forth, is Savitar.

5.83.d: अच्छा वद तवसं गीर्भिराभिः स्तुहि पर्जन्यं नमसा विवास । कनिक्रदद्वृषभो जीरदानू रेतो दधात्योषधीषु गर्भम् ॥
5.83.e: SING with these songs thy welcome to the Mighty, with adoration praise and call Parjanya.  The Bull, loud roaring, swift to send his bounty, lays in the plants the seed. for germination.

5.83.d: वि वृक्षान्हन्त्युत हन्ति रक्षसो विश्वं बिभाय भुवनं महावधात् । उतानागा ईषते वृष्ण्यावतो यत्पर्जन्यः स्तनयन्हन्ति दुष्कृतः ॥
5.83.e: He smites the trees apart, he slays the demons: all life fears him who wields the mighty weapon.  From him exceeding strong fices e’en the guiltless, when thundering Parjanya smites the wicked.

5.83.d: रथीव कशयाश्वाँ अभिक्षिपन्नाविर्दूतान्कृणुते वर्ष्याँ३ अह । दूरात्सिंहस्य स्तनथा उदीरते यत्पर्जन्यः कृणुते वर्ष्यं१ नभः ॥
5.83.e: Like a car-driver whipping on his horses, he makes the messengers of rain spring forward.  Far off resounds the roaring of the lion, what time Parjanya fills the sky with rain-cloud.

5.83.d: प्र वाता वान्ति पतयन्ति विद्युत उदोषधीर्जिहते पिन्वते स्वः । इरा विश्वस्मै भुवनाय जायते यत्पर्जन्यः पृथिवीं रेतसावति ॥
5.83.e: Forth burst the winds, down come the lightning-flashes: the plants shoot up, the realm of light is streaming.  Food springs abundant for all living creatures, what time Parjanya quickens earth with moisture.

5.83.d: यस्य व्रते पृथिवी नन्नमीति यस्य व्रते शफवज्जर्भुरीति । यस्य व्रत ओषधीर्विश्वरूपाः स नः पर्जन्य महि शर्म यच्छ ॥
5.83.e: Thou at whose bidding earth bows low before thee, at whose command hoofed cattle fly in terror,  At whose behest the plants assume all colours, even thou Parjanya, yield us great protection.

5.83.d: दिवो नो वृष्टिं मरुतो ररीध्वं प्र पिन्वत वृष्णो अश्वस्य धाराः । अर्वाङेतेन स्तनयित्नुनेह्यपो निषिञ्चन्नसुरः पिता नः ॥
5.83.e: Send down for us the rain of heaven, ye Maruts, and let the Stallion's flood descend in torrents.  Come hither with this thunder while thou pourest the waters down, our heavenly Lord and Father.

5.83.d: अभि क्रन्द स्तनय गर्भमा धा उदन्वता परि दीया रथेन । दृतिं सु कर्ष विषितं न्यञ्चं समा भवन्तूद्वतो निपादाः ॥
5.83.e: Thunder and roar: the germ of life deposit. Fly round us on thy chariot waterladen.  Thine opened water-skin draw with thee downward, and let the hollows and the heights be level.

5.83.d: महान्तं कोशमुदचा नि षिञ्च स्यन्दन्तां कुल्या विषिताः पुरस्तात् । घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी व्युन्धि सुप्रपाणं भवत्वघ्न्याभ्यः ॥
5.83.e: Lift up the mighty vessel, pour down water, and let the liberated streams rush forward.  Saturate both the earth and heaven with fatness, and for the cows let there be drink abundant.

5.83.d: यत्पर्जन्य कनिक्रदत्स्तनयन्हंसि दुष्कृतः । प्रतीदं विश्वं मोदते यत्किं च पृथिव्यामधि ॥
5.83.e: When thou, with thunder and with roar, Parjanya, smitest sinners down,  This universe exults thereat, yea, all that is upon the earth.

5.83.d: अवर्षीर्वर्षमुदु षू गृभायाकर्धन्वान्यत्येतवा उ । अजीजन ओषधीर्भोजनाय कमुत प्रजाभ्योऽविदो मनीषाम् ॥
5.83.e: Thou hast poured down the rain-flood now withhold it. Thou hast made desert places fit for travel.  Thou hast made herbs to grow for our enjoyment: yea, thou hast won thee praise from living creatures.

5.84.d: बळित्था पर्वतानां खिद्रं बिभर्षि पृथिवि । प्र या भूमिं प्रवत्वति मह्ना जिनोषि महिनि ॥
5.84.e: THOU, of a truth,O Prthivi, bearest the tool that rends the hills:  Thou rich in torrents, who with might quickenest earth, O Mighty One.

5.84.d: स्तोमासस्त्वा विचारिणि प्रति ष्टोभन्त्यक्तुभिः । प्र या वाजं न हेषन्तं पेरुमस्यस्यर्जुनि ॥
5.84.e: To thee, O wanderer at will, ring out the lauds with beams of day,  Who drivest, like a neighing steed, the swelling cloud, O bright of hue.

5.84.d: दृळ्हा चिद्या वनस्पतीन्क्ष्मया दर्धर्ष्योजसा । यत्ते अभ्रस्य विद्युतो दिवो वर्षन्ति वृष्टयः ॥
5.84.e: Who graspest with thy might on earth. e’en the strong sovrans of the wood,  When from the lightning of thy cloud the rain-floods of the heaven descend.

5.85.d: प्र सम्राजे बृहदर्चा गभीरं ब्रह्म प्रियं वरुणाय श्रुताय । वि यो जघान शमितेव चर्मोपस्तिरे पृथिवीं सूर्याय ॥
5.85.e: SING forth a hymn sublime and solemn, grateful to glorious. Varuṇa, imperial Ruler,  Who hath struck out, like one who slays the victim, earth as a skin to spread in front of Sūrya.

5.85.d: वनेषु व्य१न्तरिक्षं ततान वाजमर्वत्सु पय उस्रियासु । हृत्सु क्रतुं वरुणो अप्स्व१ग्निं दिवि सूर्यमदधात्सोममद्रौ ॥
5.85.e: In the tree-tops the air he hath extended, put milk in kine and vigorous speed in horses,  Set intellect in hearts, fire in the waters, Siurya in heaven and Soma on the mountain.

5.85.d: नीचीनबारं वरुणः कवन्धं प्र ससर्ज रोदसी अन्तरिक्षम् । तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवं न वृष्टिर्व्युनत्ति भूम ॥
5.85.e: Varuṇa lets the big cask, opening downward, flow through the heaven and earth and air's mid-region.  Therewith the universe's Sovran waters earth as the shower of rain bedews the barley.

5.85.d: उनत्ति भूमिं पृथिवीमुत द्यां यदा दुग्धं वरुणो वष्ट्यादित् । समभ्रेण वसत पर्वतासस्तविषीयन्तः श्रथयन्त वीराः ॥
5.85.e: When Varuṇa is fain for milk he moistens the sky, the land, and earth to her foundation.  Then straight the mountains clothe them in the rain-cloud: the Heroes, putting forth their vigour, loose them.

5.85.d: इमामू ष्वासुरस्य श्रुतस्य महीं मायां वरुणस्य प्र वोचम् । मानेनेव तस्थिवाँ अन्तरिक्षे वि यो ममे पृथिवीं सूर्येण ॥
5.85.e: I will declare this mighty deed of magic, of glorious Varuṇa the Lord Immortal,  Who standing in the firmament hath meted the earth out with the Sun as with a measure.

5.85.d: इमामू नु कवितमस्य मायां महीं देवस्य नकिरा दधर्ष । एकं यदुद्ना न पृणन्त्येनीरासिञ्चन्तीरवनयः समुद्रम् ॥
5.85.e: None, verily, hath ever let or hindered this the most wise God's mighty deed of magic,  Whereby with all their flood, the lucid rivers fill not one sea wherein they pour their waters.

5.85.d: अर्यम्यं वरुण मित्र्यं वा सखायं वा सदमिद्भ्रातरं वा । वेशं वा नित्यं वरुणारणं वा यत्सीमागश्चकृमा शिश्रथस्तत् ॥
5.85.e: If we have sinned against the man who loves us, have ever wronged a brother, friend, or comrade,  The neighbour ever with us, or a stranger, O Varuṇa, remove from us the trespass.

5.85.d: कितवासो यद्रिरिपुर्न दीवि यद्वा घा सत्यमुत यन्न विद्म । सर्वा ता वि ष्य शिथिरेव देवाधा ते स्याम वरुण प्रियासः ॥
5.85.e: If we, as gamesters cheat at play, have cheated, done wrong unwittingly or sinned of purpose,  Cast all these sins away like loosened fetters, and, Varuṇa let us be thine own beloved.

5.86.d: इन्द्राग्नी यमवथ उभा वाजेषु मर्त्यम् । दृळ्हा चित्स प्र भेदति द्युम्ना वाणीरिव त्रितः ॥
5.86.e: THE mortal man whom ye, the Twain, Indra and Agni, help in fight,  Breaks through e’en strongly-guarded wealth as Tṛta burst his way through reeds.

5.86.d: या पृतनासु दुष्टरा या वाजेषु श्रवाय्या । या पञ्च चर्षणीरभीन्द्राग्नी ता हवामहे ॥
5.86.e: The Twain invincible in war, worthy to be renowned in frays,  Lords of the Fivefold. People, these, Indra and Agni, we invoke.

5.86.d: तयोरिदमवच्छवस्तिग्मा दिद्युन्मघोनोः । प्रति द्रुणा गभस्त्योर्गवां वृत्रघ्न एषते ॥
5.86.e: Impetuous is their strength, and keen the lightning of the mighty Pair,  Which from their arms speeds with the car to Vṛtra's slayer for the kine.

5.86.d: ता वामेषे रथानामिन्द्राग्नी हवामहे । पती तुरस्य राधसो विद्वांसा गिर्वणस्तमा ॥
5.86.e: Indra and Agni, we invoke you both, as such, to send your cars:  Lords of quick-coming bounty, ye who know, chief lovers of the song.

5.86.d: ता वृधन्तावनु द्यून्मर्ताय देवावदभा । अर्हन्ता चित्पुरो दधेंऽशेव देवावर्वते ॥
5.86.e: These who give increase day by day, Gods without guile for mortal man,  Worthy themselves, I honour most, Two Gods as partners, for my horse.

5.86.d: एवेन्द्राग्निभ्यामहावि हव्यं शूष्यं घृतं न पूतमद्रिभिः । ता सूरिषु श्रवो बृहद्रयिं गृणत्सु दिधृतमिषं गृणत्सु दिधृतम् ॥
5.86.e: The strength-bestowing offering thus to Indra-Agni hath been paid, as butter, purified by stones.  Deal to our princes high renown, deal wealth to those who sing your praise, deal food to those who sing your praise.

5.87.d: प्र वो महे मतयो यन्तु विष्णवे मरुत्वते गिरिजा एवयामरुत् । प्र शर्धाय प्रयज्यवे सुखादये तवसे भन्ददिष्टये धुनिव्रताय शवसे ॥
5.87.e: To Viṣṇu, to the Mighty whom the Maruts follow let your hymns born in song go forth, Evayamarut;  To the impetuous, strong band, adorned with bracelets, that rushes on in joy and ever roars for vigour.

5.87.d: प्र ये जाता महिना ये च नु स्वयं प्र विद्मना ब्रुवत एवयामरुत् । क्रत्वा तद्वो मरुतो नाधृषे शवो दाना मह्ना तदेषामधृष्टासो नाद्रयः ॥
5.87.e: They who with might were manifest, and who willingly by their own knowledge told it forth, Evayamarut.  Maruts, this strength of yours no wisdom comprehendeth: through their gifts' greatness they are moveless as the mountains.

5.87.d: प्र ये दिवो बृहतः शृण्विरे गिरा सुशुक्वानः सुभ्व एवयामरुत् । न येषामिरी सधस्थ ईष्ट आँ अग्नयो न स्वविद्युतः प्र स्यन्द्रासो धुनीनाम् ॥
5.87.e: Who by the psalm they sing are heard, from lofty heaven, the strong, the brightly shining Ones, Evayamarut;  In whose abode there is no mightier one to move them, whose lightnings are as fires, who urge the roaring rivers.

5.87.d: स चक्रमे महतो निरुरुक्रमः समानस्मात्सदस एवयामरुत् । यदायुक्त त्मना स्वादधि ष्णुभिर्विष्पर्धसो विमहसो जिगाति शेवृधो नृभिः ॥
5.87.e: He of the Mighty Stride forth strode, Evayamarut, out of the spacious dwelling-place, their home in common.  When he, himself, hath yoked his emulous strong horses on heights, he cometh forth, joy-giving, with the Heroes.

5.87.d: स्वनो न वोऽमवान्रेजयद्वृषा त्वेषो ययिस्तविष एवयामरुत् । येना सहन्त ऋञ्जत स्वरोचिषः स्थारश्मानो हिरण्ययाः स्वायुधास इष्मिणः ॥
5.87.e: Like your tremendous roar, the rainer with light flashing, strong, speeding, hath made all tremble, Evayamarut,  Wherewith victorious ye, self-luminous, press onward, with strong reins, decked with gold, impetuous and well-weaponed.

5.87.d: अपारो वो महिमा वृद्धशवसस्त्वेषं शवोऽवत्वेवयामरुत् । स्थातारो हि प्रसितौ संदृशि स्थन ते न उरुष्यता निदः शुशुक्वांसो नाग्नयः ॥
5.87.e: Unbounded is your greatness, ye of mighty power: may your bright vigour be our aid, Evayamarut;  For ye are visible helpers in the time of trouble: like fires, aglow with light, save us from shame and insult.

5.87.d: ते रुद्रासः सुमखा अग्नयो यथा तुविद्युम्ना अवन्त्वेवयामरुत् । दीर्घं पृथु पप्रथे सद्म पार्थिवं येषामज्मेष्वा महः शर्धांस्यद्भुतैनसाम् ॥
5.87.e: So may the Rudras, mighty warriors, Evayamarut, with splendid brilliancy, like fires, be our protectors;  They whose terrestrial dwelling-place is wide-extended, whom none suspect of sin, whose bands have lofty courage.

5.87.d: अद्वेषो नो मरुतो गातुमेतन श्रोता हवं जरितुरेवयामरुत् । विष्णोर्महः समन्यवो युयोतन स्मद्रथ्यो३ न दंसनाप द्वेषांसि सनुतः ॥
5.87.e: Come in a friendly spirit, come to us, O Maruts, and hear his call who praises you, Evayamarut.  Like car-borne men, one-minded with the mighty Viṣṇu, keep enmity far from us with your deeds of wonder.

5.87.d: गन्ता नो यज्ञं यज्ञियाः सुशमि श्रोता हवमरक्ष एवयामरुत् । ज्येष्ठासो न पर्वतासो व्योमनि यूयं तस्य प्रचेतसः स्यात दुर्धर्तवो निदः ॥
5.87.e: Come to our sacrifice, ye Hnly Ones, to bless it, and, free from demons, hear our call, Evayamarut. Most excellent, like mountains in the air's raid-region, be irresistible, ye, Wise, to this man'a hater.

6.1.d: त्वं ह्यग्ने प्रथमो मनोतास्या धियो अभवो दस्म होता । त्वं सीं वृषन्नकृणोर्दुष्टरीतु सहो विश्वस्मै सहसे सहध्यै ॥
6.1.e: THOU, first inventor of this prayer, O Agni, Worker of Marvels, hast become our Herald.  Thou, Bull, hast made us strength which none may conquer, strength that shall overcome all other prowess.

6.1.d: अधा होता न्यसीदो यजीयानिळस्पद इषयन्नीड्यः सन् । तं त्वा नरः प्रथमं देवयन्तो महो राये चितयन्तो अनु ग्मन् ॥
6.1.e: As Priest thou sattest at the seat of worship, furthering us, best Offerer, meet for honour.  So first to thee have pious men resorted, turning thy mind to thoughts of ample riches.

6.1.d: वृतेव यन्तं बहुभिर्वसव्यै३स्त्वे रयिं जागृवांसो अनु ग्मन् । रुशन्तमग्निं दर्शतं बृहन्तं वपावन्तं विश्वहा दीदिवांसम् ॥
6.1.e: In thee, still watching, they have followed riches, who goest with much wealth as with an army,  The radiant Agni, lofty, fair to look on, worshipped with marrow, evermore resplendent.

6.1.d: पदं देवस्य नमसा व्यन्तः श्रवस्यवः श्रव आपन्नमृक्तम् । नामानि चिद्दधिरे यज्ञियानि भद्रायां ते रणयन्त संदृष्टौ ॥
6.1.e: They who approached the God's abode with homage, eager for glory, won them perfect glory:  Yea, they gained even sacrificial titles, and found delight in thine auspicious aspect.

6.1.d: त्वां वर्धन्ति क्षितयः पृथिव्यां त्वां राय उभयासो जनानाम् । त्वं त्राता तरणे चेत्यो भूः पिता माता सदमिन्मानुषाणाम् ॥
6.1.e: On earth the people magnify thee greatly, thee their celestial and terrestrial riches.  Thou, Helper, must be known as our Preserver, Father and Mother of mankind for ever.

6.1.d: सपर्येण्यः स प्रियो विक्ष्व१ग्निर्होता मन्द्रो नि षसादा यजीयान् । तं त्वा वयं दम आ दीदिवांसमुप ज्ञुबाधो नमसा सदेम ॥
6.1.e: Dear priest among mankind, adorable Agni hath seated him, joy-giver, skilled in worship.  Let us approach thee shining in thy dwelling, kneeling upon our knees, with adoration.

6.1.d: तं त्वा वयं सुध्यो३ नव्यमग्ने सुम्नायव ईमहे देवयन्तः । त्वं विशो अनयो दीद्यानो दिवो अग्ने बृहता रोचनेन ॥
6.1.e: Longing for bliss, pure-minded, God-devoted, Agni, we seek thee, such, meet to be lauded.  Thou, Agni, leddest forth our men to battle, refulgent with the heaven's exalted splendour.

6.1.d: विशां कविं विश्पतिं शश्वतीनां नितोशनं वृषभं चर्षणीनाम् । प्रेतीषणिमिषयन्तं पावकं राजन्तमग्निं यजतं रयीणाम् ॥
6.1.e: Sage of mankind, all peoples' Lord and Master, the Bull of men, the sender down of blessings,  Still pressing on, promoting, purifying, Agni the Holy One, the Lord of riches.

6.1.d: सो अग्न ईजे शशमे च मर्तो यस्त आनट् समिधा हव्यदातिम् । य आहुतिं परि वेदा नमोभिर्विश्वेत्स वामा दधते त्वोतः ॥
6.1.e: Agni, the mortal who hath toiled and worshipped, brought thee oblations with his kindled fuel,  And well knows sacrifice with adoration, gains every joy with thee to guard and help him.

6.1.d: अस्मा उ ते महि महे विधेम नमोभिरग्ने समिधोत हव्यैः । वेदी सूनो सहसो गीर्भिरुक्थैरा ते भद्रायां सुमतौ यतेम ॥
6.1.e: Mightily let us worship thee the Mighty, with reverence, Agni! fuel and oblations,  With songs, O Son of Strength, with hymns, with altar: so may we strive for thine auspicious favour.

6.1.d: आ यस्ततन्थ रोदसी वि भासा श्रवोभिश्च श्रवस्य१स्तरुत्रः । बृहद्भिर्वाजैः स्थविरेभिरस्मे रेवद्भिरग्ने वितरं वि भाहि ॥
6.1.e: Thou who hast covered heaven and earth with splendour and with thy glories, glorious and triumphant.  Continue thou to shine on us, O Agni, with strength abundant, rich, and long enduring.

6.1.d: नृवद्वसो सदमिद्धेह्यस्मे भूरि तोकाय तनयाय पश्वः । पूर्वीरिषो बृहतीरारेअघा अस्मे भद्रा सौश्रवसानि सन्तु ॥
6.1.e: Vouchsafe us ever, as man needs, O Vasu, abundant wealth of kine for son and offspring.  Food noble, plenteous, far from sin and evil, he with us, and fair fame to make us happy.

6.1.d: पुरूण्यग्ने पुरुधा त्वाया वसूनि राजन्वसुता ते अश्याम् । पुरूणि हि त्वे पुरुवार सन्त्यग्ने वसु विधते राजनि त्वे ॥
6.1.e: May I obtain much wealth in many places by love of thee and through thy grace, King Agni;  For in thee Bounteous One, in thee the Sovran, Agni, are many boons for him who serves thee.

6.2.d: त्वं हि क्षैतवद्यशोऽग्ने मित्रो न पत्यसे । त्वं विचर्षणे श्रवो वसो पुष्टिं न पुष्यसि ॥
6.2.e: THOU, Agni, even as Mitra, hast a princely glory of thine own.  Thou, active Vasu, makest fame increase like full prosperity.

6.2.d: त्वां हि ष्मा चर्षणयो यज्ञेभिर्गीर्भिरीळते । त्वां वाजी यात्यवृको रजस्तूर्विश्वचर्षणिः ॥
6.2.e: For, verily, men pray to thee with sacrifices and with songs.  To thee the Friendly Courser, seen of all, comes speeding through the air.

6.2.d: सजोषस्त्वा दिवो नरो यज्ञस्य केतुमिन्धते । यद्ध स्य मानुषो जनः सुम्नायुर्जुह्वे अध्वरे ॥
6.2.e: Of one accord men kindle thee Heaven's signal of the sacrifice,  When, craving bliss, this race of man invites thee to the solemn rite.

6.2.d: ऋधद्यस्ते सुदानवे धिया मर्तः शशमते । ऊती ष बृहतो दिवो द्विषो अंहो न तरति ॥
6.2.e: Let the man thrive who travails sore, in prayer, far thee the Bountiful.  He with the help of lofty Dyaus comes safe through straits of enmity.

6.2.d: समिधा यस्त आहुतिं निशितिं मर्त्यो नशत् । वयावन्तं स पुष्यति क्षयमग्ने शतायुषम् ॥
6.2.e: The mortal who with fuel lights thy flame and offers unto thee,  Supports a house with many a branch, Agni, to live a hundred years.

6.2.d: त्वेषस्ते धूम ऋण्वति दिवि षञ्छुक्र आततः । सूरो न हि द्युता त्वं कृपा पावक रोचसे ॥
6.2.e: Thy bright smoke lifts itself aloft, and far-extended shines in heaven.  For, Purifier! like the Sun thou beamest with thy radiant glow.

6.2.d: अधा हि विक्ष्वीड्योऽसि प्रियो नो अतिथिः । रण्वः पुरीव जूर्यः सूनुर्न त्रययाय्यः ॥
6.2.e: For in men's houses thou must be glorified as a well-loved guest,  Gay like an elder in a fort, claiming protection like a son.

6.2.d: क्रत्वा हि द्रोणे अज्यसेऽग्ने वाजी न कृत्व्यः । परिज्मेव स्वधा गयोऽत्यो न ह्वार्यः शिशुः ॥
6.2.e: Thou, Agni, like an able steed, art urged by wisdom in the wood.  Thou art like wind; food, home art thou, like a young horse that runs astray.

6.2.d: त्वं त्या चिदच्युताग्ने पशुर्न यवसे । धामा ह यत्ते अजर वना वृश्चन्ति शिक्वसः ॥
6.2.e: E’en things imperishable, thou, O Agni, like a gazing ox,  Eatest, when hosts, Eternal One! of thee the Mighty rend the woods.

6.2.d: वेषि ह्यध्वरीयतामग्ने होता दमे विशाम् । समृधो विश्पते कृणु जुषस्व हव्यमङ्गिरः ॥
6.2.e: Agni, thou enterest as Priest the home of men who sacrifice.  Lord of the people, prosper them. Accept the ofrering, Aṅgiras!

6.2.d: अच्छा नो मित्रमहो देव देवानग्ने वोचः सुमतिं रोदस्योः । वीहि स्वस्तिं सुक्षितिं दिवो नॄन्द्विषो अंहांसि दुरिता तरेम ता तरेम तवावसा तरेम ॥
6.2.e: O Agni, God with Mitra's might, call hither the favour of the Gods from earth and heaven.  Bring weal from heaven, that men may dwell securely. May we o’ercome the foe's malign oppressions, may we o’ercome them, through thy help o’ercome them.

6.3.d: अग्ने स क्षेषदृतपा ऋतेजा उरु ज्योतिर्नशते देवयुष्टे । यं त्वं मित्रेण वरुणः सजोषा देव पासि त्यजसा मर्तमंहः ॥
6.3.e: TRUE, guardian of the Law, thy faithful servant wins ample light and dwells in peace, O Agni,  Whom thou, as Varuṇa in accord with Mitra, guardest, O God, by banishing his trouble.

6.3.d: ईजे यज्ञेभिः शशमे शमीभिर्ऋधद्वारायाग्नये ददाश । एवा चन तं यशसामजुष्टिर्नांहो मर्तं नशते न प्रदृप्तिः ॥
6.3.e: He hath paid sacrifices, toiled in worship, and offered gifts to wealth-increasing Agni.  Him the displeasure of the famous moves not, outrage and scorn affect not such a mortal.

6.3.d: सूरो न यस्य दृशतिररेपा भीमा यदेति शुचतस्त आ धीः । हेषस्वतः शुरुधो नायमक्तोः कुत्रा चिद्रण्वो वसतिर्वनेजाः ॥
6.3.e: Bright God, whose look is free from stain like Sūrya's, thou, swift, what time thou earnestly desirest,  Hast gear to give us. Come with joy at evening, where, Child of Wood, thou mayest also tarry.

6.3.d: तिग्मं चिदेम महि वर्पो अस्य भसदश्वो न यमसान आसा । विजेहमानः परशुर्न जिह्वां द्रविर्न द्रावयति दारु धक्षत् ॥
6.3.e: Fierce is his gait and vast his wondrous body: he champeth like a horse with bit and bridle,  And, darting forth his tongue, as ’twere a hatchet, burning the woods, smelteth them like a smelter.

6.3.d: स इदस्तेव प्रति धादसिष्यञ्छिशीत तेजोऽयसो न धाराम् । चित्रध्रजतिररतिर्यो अक्तोर्वेर्न द्रुषद्वा रघुपत्मजंहाः ॥
6.3.e: Archer-like, fain toshoot, he sets his arrow, and whets his splendour like the edge of iron:  The messenger of night with brilliant pathway, like a tree-roosting bird of rapid pinion.

6.3.d: स ईं रेभो न प्रति वस्त उस्राः शोचिषा रारपीति मित्रमहाः । नक्तं य ईमरुषो यो दिवा नॄनमर्त्यो अरुषो यो दिवा नॄन् ॥
6.3.e: In beams of morn he clothes him like the singer, and bright as Mitra with his splendour crackles.  Red in the night, by day the men's possession: red, he belongs to men by day, Immortal.

6.3.d: दिवो न यस्य विधतो नवीनोद्वृषा रुक्ष ओषधीषु नूनोत् । घृणा न यो ध्रजसा पत्मना यन्ना रोदसी वसुना दं सुपत्नी ॥
6.3.e: Like Heaven's when scattering beams his voice was uttered: among the plants the radiant Hero shouted,  Who with his glow in rapid course came hither to fill both worlds, well-wedded Dames, with treasure.

6.3.d: धायोभिर्वा यो युज्येभिरर्कैर्विद्युन्न दविद्योत्स्वेभिः शुष्मैः । शर्धो वा यो मरुतां ततक्ष ऋभुर्न त्वेषो रभसानो अद्यौत् ॥
6.3.e: Who, with supporting streams and rays that suit him, hath flashed like lightning with his native vigour.  Like the deft Maker of the band of Maruts, the bright impetuous One hath shone refulgent.

6.4.d: यथा होतर्मनुषो देवताता यज्ञेभिः सूनो सहसो यजासि । एवा नो अद्य समना समानानुशन्नग्न उशतो यक्षि देवान् ॥
6.4.e: As at man's service of the Gods, Invoker, thou, Son of Strength, dost sacrifice and worship,  So bring for us to-day all Gods together, bring willingly the willing Gods, O Agni.

6.4.d: स नो विभावा चक्षणिर्न वस्तोरग्निर्वन्दारु वेद्यश्चनो धात् । विश्वायुर्यो अमृतो मर्त्येषूषर्भुद्भूदतिथिर्जातवेदाः ॥
6.4.e: May Agni, radiant Herald of the morning, meet to be known, accept our praise with favour.  Dear to all life, mid mortal men Immortal, our guest, awake at dawn, is Jātavedas.

6.4.d: द्यावो न यस्य पनयन्त्यभ्वं भासांसि वस्ते सूर्यो न शुक्रः । वि य इनोत्यजरः पावकोऽश्नस्य चिच्छिश्नथत्पूर्व्याणि ॥
6.4.e: Whose might the very heavens regard with wonder: bright as the Sun he clothes himself with lustre.  He who sends forth,, Eternal Purifier, hath shattered e’en the ancient works of Aśna.

6.4.d: वद्मा हि सूनो अस्यद्मसद्वा चक्रे अग्निर्जनुषाज्मान्नम् । स त्वं न ऊर्जसन ऊर्जं धा राजेव जेरवृके क्षेष्यन्तः ॥
6.4.e: Thou art a Singer, Son! our feast-companion: Agni at birth prepared his food and pathway.  Therefore vouchsafe us strength, O Strength-bestower. Win like a King: foes trouble not thy dwelling.

6.4.d: नितिक्ति यो वारणमन्नमत्ति वायुर्न राष्ट्र्यत्येत्यक्तून् । तुर्याम यस्त आदिशामरातीरत्यो न ह्रुतः पततः परिह्रुत् ॥
6.4.e: Even he who cats his firm hard food with swiftness,and overtakes the nights as Vāyu kingdoms.  May we o’ercome those who resist thine orders, like a steed casting down the flying foemen.

6.4.d: आ सूर्यो न भानुमद्भिरर्कैरग्ने ततन्थ रोदसी वि भासा । चित्रो नयत्परि तमांस्यक्तः शोचिषा पत्मन्नौशिजो न दीयन् ॥
6.4.e: Like Sūrya with his fulgent rays, O Agni, thou overspreadest both the worlds with splendour.  Decked with bright colour he dispels the darkness, like Auśija, with clear flame swifily flying.

6.4.d: त्वां हि मन्द्रतममर्कशोकैर्ववृमहे महि नः श्रोष्यग्ने । इन्द्रं न त्वा शवसा देवता वायुं पृणन्ति राधसा नृतमाः ॥
6.4.e: We have elected thee as most delightful for thy beams' glow: hear our great laud, O Agni.  The best men praise thee as the peer of Indra in strength, mid Gods, like Viyu in thy bounty.

6.4.d: नू नो अग्नेऽवृकेभिः स्वस्ति वेषि रायः पथिभिः पर्ष्यंहः । ता सूरिभ्यो गृणते रासि सुम्नं मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ॥
6.4.e: Now, Agni, on the tranquil paths of riches come to us for our weal: save us from sorrow.  Grant chiefs and bard this boon. May we live happy, with hero children, through a hundred winters.

6.5.d: हुवे वः सूनुं सहसो युवानमद्रोघवाचं मतिभिर्यविष्ठम् । य इन्वति द्रविणानि प्रचेता विश्ववाराणि पुरुवारो अध्रुक् ॥
6.5.e: I INVOCATE your Son of Strength, the Youthful, with hymns, the Youngest God, whose speech is guileless;  Sage who sends wealth comprising every treasure, bringer of many boons, devoid of malice.

6.5.d: त्वे वसूनि पुर्वणीक होतर्दोषा वस्तोरेरिरे यज्ञियासः । क्षामेव विश्वा भुवनानि यस्मिन्त्सं सौभगानि दधिरे पावके ॥
6.5.e: At eve and morn thy pious servants bring thee their precious gifts, O Priest of many aspects,  On whom, the Purifier, all things living as on firm. ground their happiness have stablished.

6.5.d: त्वं विक्षु प्रदिवः सीद आसु क्रत्वा रथीरभवो वार्याणाम् । अत इनोषि विधते चिकित्वो व्यानुषग्जातवेदो वसूनि ॥
6.5.e: Thou from of old hast dwelt among these people, by mental power the charioteer of blessings.  Hence sendest thou, O sapient Jātavedas, to him who serves thee treasures in succession.

6.5.d: यो नः सनुत्यो अभिदासदग्ने यो अन्तरो मित्रमहो वनुष्यात् । तमजरेभिर्वृषभिस्तव स्वैस्तपा तपिष्ठ तपसा तपस्वान् ॥
6.5.e: Agni, whoever secretly attacks us, the neighbour, thou with Mitra's might! who harms us,  Burn him with thine own Steers for ever youthful, burning with burning heat, thou fiercest burner.

6.5.d: यस्ते यज्ञेन समिधा य उक्थैरर्केभिः सूनो सहसो ददाशत् । स मर्त्येष्वमृत प्रचेता राया द्युम्नेन श्रवसा वि भाति ॥
6.5.e: He who serves thee with sacrifice and fuel, with hymn, O Son of Strength, and chanted praises,  Shines out, Immortal! in the midst of mortals, a sage, with wealth, with splendour and with glory.

6.5.d: स तत्कृधीषितस्तूयमग्ने स्पृधो बाधस्व सहसा सहस्वान् । यच्छस्यसे द्युभिरक्तो वचोभिस्तज्जुषस्व जरितुर्घोषि मन्म ॥
6.5.e: Do this, O Agni, when we urge thee, quickly, triumphant in thy might subdue our foemen.  When thou art praised with words and decked with brightness, accept this chanted hymn, the singer's worship.

6.5.d: अश्याम तं काममग्ने तवोती अश्याम रयिं रयिवः सुवीरम् । अश्याम वाजमभि वाजयन्तोऽश्याम द्युम्नमजराजरं ते ॥
6.5.e: Help us, that we may gain this wish, O Agni, gain riches, Wealthy One! with store of heroes.  Desiring strength from thee may we be strengthened, and win, Eternal! thine eternal glory.

6.6.d: प्र नव्यसा सहसः सूनुमच्छा यज्ञेन गातुमव इच्छमानः । वृश्चद्वनं कृष्णयामं रुशन्तं वीती होतारं दिव्यं जिगाति ॥
6.6.e: HE who seeks furtherance and grace to help him goes to the Son of Strength with newest worship,  Calling the heavenly Priest to share the banquet, who rends the wood, bright, with his blackened pathway.

6.6.d: स श्वितानस्तन्यतू रोचनस्था अजरेभिर्नानदद्भिर्यविष्ठः । यः पावकः पुरुतमः पुरूणि पृथून्यग्निरनुयाति भर्वन् ॥
6.6.e: White-hued and thundering he dwells in splendour, Most Youthful, with the loudvoiced and eternal-  Agni, most variform, the Purifier, who follows crunching many ample forests.

6.6.d: वि ते विष्वग्वातजूतासो अग्ने भामासः शुचे शुचयश्चरन्ति । तुविम्रक्षासो दिव्या नवग्वा वना वनन्ति धृषता रुजन्तः ॥
6.6.e: Incited by the wind thy flames, O Agni, move onward, Pure One! pure, in all directions.  Thy most destructive heavenly Navagvas break the woods down and devastate them boldly.

6.6.d: ये ते शुक्रासः शुचयः शुचिष्मः क्षां वपन्ति विषितासो अश्वाः । अध भ्रमस्त उर्विया वि भाति यातयमानो अधि सानु पृश्नेः ॥
6.6.e: Thy pure white horses from their bonds are loosened: O Radiant One, they shear the ground beneath them,  And far and wide shines out thy flame, and flickers rapidly moving over earth's high ridges.

6.6.d: अध जिह्वा पापतीति प्र वृष्णो गोषुयुधो नाशनिः सृजाना । शूरस्येव प्रसितिः क्षातिरग्नेर्दुर्वर्तुर्भीमो दयते वनानि ॥
6.6.e: Forth darts the Bull's tongue like the sharp stone weapon discharged by him who fights to win the cattle.  Agni's fierce flame is like a hero's onset: dread and resistless he destroys the forests.

6.6.d: आ भानुना पार्थिवानि ज्रयांसि महस्तोदस्य धृषता ततन्थ । स बाधस्वाप भया सहोभिः स्पृधो वनुष्यन्वनुषो नि जूर्व ॥
6.6.e: Thou with the sunlight of the great Impeller hast boldly over-spread the earth's expanses.  So drive away with conquering might all perils. fighting out foemen burn up those who harm us.

6.6.d: स चित्र चित्रं चितयन्तमस्मे चित्रक्षत्र चित्रतमं वयोधाम् । चन्द्रं रयिं पुरुवीरं बृहन्तं चन्द्र चन्द्राभिर्गृणते युवस्व ॥
6.6.e: Wondrous! of wondrous power! give to the singer wealth wondrous, marked, most wonderful, life-giving.  Wealth bright, O Bright One, vast, with many heroes, give with thy bright flames to the man who lauds thee.

6.7.d: मूर्धानं दिवो अरतिं पृथिव्या वैश्वानरमृत आ जातमग्निम् । कविं सम्राजमतिथिं जनानामासन्ना पात्रं जनयन्त देवाः ॥
6.7.e: Him, messenger of earth and head of heaven, Agni Vaiśvānara, born in holy Order,  The Sage, the King, the guest of men, a vessel fit for their mouths, the Gods have generated.

6.7.d: नाभिं यज्ञानां सदनं रयीणां महामाहावमभि सं नवन्त । वैश्वानरं रथ्यमध्वराणां यज्ञस्य केतुं जनयन्त देवाः ॥
6.7.e: Him have they praised, mid-point of sacrifices, great cistern of libations, seat of riches.  Vaiśvānara, conveyer of oblations, ensign of worship, have the Gods engendered.

6.7.d: त्वद्विप्रो जायते वाज्यग्ने त्वद्वीरासो अभिमातिषाहः । वैश्वानर त्वमस्मासु धेहि वसूनि राजन्त्स्पृहयाय्याणि ॥
6.7.e: From thee, O Agni, springs the mighty singer, from thee come heroes who subdue the foeman.  O King, Vaiśvānara, bestow thou on us excellent treasures worthy to belonged fo r.

6.7.d: त्वां विश्वे अमृत जायमानं शिशुं न देवा अभि सं नवन्ते । तव क्रतुभिरमृतत्वमायन्वैश्वानर यत्पित्रोरदीदेः ॥
6.7.e: To thee, Immortal! when to life thou springest, all the Gods sing for joy as to their infant.  They by thy mental powers were made immortal, Vaiśvānara, when thou shonest from thy Parents.

6.7.d: वैश्वानर तव तानि व्रतानि महान्यग्ने नकिरा दधर्ष । यज्जायमानः पित्रोरुपस्थेऽविन्दः केतुं वयुनेष्वह्नाम् ॥
6.7.e: Agni Vaiśvānara, no one hath ever resisted these thy mighty ordinances,  When thou, arising from thy Parents' bosom, foundest the light for days' appointed courses.

6.7.d: वैश्वानरस्य विमितानि चक्षसा सानूनि दिवो अमृतस्य केतुना । तस्येदु विश्वा भुवनाधि मूर्धनि वया इव रुरुहुः सप्त विस्रुहः ॥
6.7.e: The summits of the heaven are traversed through and through by the Immortal's light, Vaiśvānara's brilliancy.  All creatures in existence rest upon his head. The Seven swift-flowing Streams have grown like branches forth,

6.7.d: वि यो रजांस्यमिमीत सुक्रतुर्वैश्वानरो वि दिवो रोचना कविः । परि यो विश्वा भुवनानि पप्रथेऽदब्धो गोपा अमृतस्य रक्षिता ॥
6.7.e: Vaiśvānara, who measured out the realms of air, Sage very wise who made the lucid spheres of heaven,  The Undeceivable who spread out all the worlds, keeper is he and guard of immortality.

6.8.d: पृक्षस्य वृष्णो अरुषस्य नू सहः प्र नु वोचं विदथा जातवेदसः । वैश्वानराय मतिर्नव्यसी शुचिः सोम इव पवते चारुरग्नये ॥
6.8.e: AT Jātavedas' holy gathering I will tell aloud the conquering might of the swift red-hued Steer.  A pure and fresher hymn flows to Vaiśvānara, even as for Agni lovely Soma is made pure.

6.8.d: स जायमानः परमे व्योमनि व्रतान्यग्निर्व्रतपा अरक्षत । व्य१न्तरिक्षममिमीत सुक्रतुर्वैश्वानरो महिना नाकमस्पृशत् ॥
6.8.e: That Agni, when in loftiest heaven he sprang to life, Guardian of Holy Laws, kept and observed them well.  Exceeding wise, he measured out the firmament. Vaiśvānara attained to heaven by mightiness.

6.8.d: व्यस्तभ्नाद्रोदसी मित्रो अद्भुतोऽन्तर्वावदकृणोज्ज्योतिषा तमः । वि चर्मणीव धिषणे अवर्तयद्वैश्वानरो विश्वमधत्त वृष्ण्यम् ॥
6.8.e: Wonderful Mitra propped the heaven and earth apart, and covered and concealed  the darkness with his light.  He made the two bowls part asunder like two skins. Vaiśvānara put forth all his creative power.

6.8.d: अपामुपस्थे महिषा अगृभ्णत विशो राजानमुप तस्थुर्ऋग्मियम् । आ दूतो अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः ॥
6.8.e: The Migbty seized him in the bosom of the floods: the people waited on the King who should be praised.  As envoy of Vivasvān MatariSvan brought Agni Vaiśvānara hither from far away.

6.8.d: युगेयुगे विदथ्यं गृणद्भ्योऽग्ने रयिं यशसं धेहि नव्यसीम् । पव्येव राजन्नघशंसमजर नीचा नि वृश्च वनिनं न तेजसा ॥
6.8.e: In every age bestow upon the singers wealth, worthy of holy synods, glorious, ever new.  King, undecaying, as it were with sharpened bolt, smite down the sinner like a tree with lightning-flash.

6.8.d: अस्माकमग्ने मघवत्सु धारयानामि क्षत्रमजरं सुवीर्यम् । वयं जयेम शतिनं सहस्रिणं वैश्वानर वाजमग्ने तवोतिभिः ॥
6.8.e: Do thou bestow, O Agni, on our wealthy chiefs, rule, with good heroes, undecaying, bending not.  So may we win for us strength. O Vaiśvānara, hundredfold, thousandfold, O Agni, by thy help.

6.8.d: अदब्धेभिस्तव गोपाभिरिष्टेऽस्माकं पाहि त्रिषधस्थ सूरीन् । रक्षा च नो ददुषां शर्धो अग्ने वैश्वानर प्र च तारीः स्तवानः ॥
6.8.e: O thou who dwellest in three places, Helper, keep with effective guards our princely patrons.  Keep our band, Agni, who have brought thee presents. Lengthen their lives, Vaiśvānara, when lauded.

6.9.d: अहश्च कृष्णमहरर्जुनं च वि वर्तेते रजसी वेद्याभिः । वैश्वानरो जायमानो न राजावातिरज्ज्योतिषाग्निस्तमांसि ॥
6.9.e: ONE half of day is dark, and bright the other: both atmospheres move on by sage devices.  Agni Vaiśvānara, when born as Sovran, hath with his lustre overcome the darkness.

6.9.d: नाहं तन्तुं न वि जानाम्योतुं न यं वयन्ति समरेऽतमानाः । कस्य स्वित्पुत्र इह वक्त्वानि परो वदात्यवरेण पित्रा ॥
6.9.e: I know not either warp or woof, I know not the web they weave when moving to the contest.  Whose son shall here speak words that must be spoken without assistance from the Father near him?

6.9.d: स इत्तन्तुं स वि जानात्योतुं स वक्त्वान्यृतुथा वदाति । य ईं चिकेतदमृतस्य गोपा अवश्चरन्परो अन्येन पश्यन् ॥
6.9.e: For both the warp and woof he understandeth, and in due time shall speak what should be spoken,  Who knoweth as the immortal world's Protector, descending, seeing with no aid from other.

6.9.d: अयं होता प्रथमः पश्यतेममिदं ज्योतिरमृतं मर्त्येषु । अयं स जज्ञे ध्रुव आ निषत्तोऽमर्त्यस्तन्वा३ वर्धमानः ॥
6.9.e: He is the Priest, the first of all: behold him. Mid mortal men he is the light immortal.  Here was he born, firm-seated in his station Immortal, ever waxing in his body.

6.9.d: ध्रुवं ज्योतिर्निहितं दृशये कं मनो जविष्ठं पतयत्स्वन्तः । विश्वे देवाः समनसः सकेता एकं क्रतुमभि वि यन्ति साधु ॥
6.9.e: A firm light hath been set for men to look on: among all things that fly the mind is swiftest.  All Gods of one accord, with one intention, move unobstructed to a single purpose.

6.9.d: वि मे कर्णा पतयतो वि चक्षुर्वी३दं ज्योतिर्हृदय आहितं यत् । वि मे मनश्चरति दूरआधीः किं स्विद्वक्ष्यामि किमु नू मनिष्ये ॥
6.9.e: Mine ears unclose to hear, mine eye to see him; the light that harbours in my spirit broadens.  Far roams my mind whose thoughts are in the distance. What shall I speak, what shall I now imagine?

6.9.d: विश्वे देवा अनमस्यन्भियानास्त्वामग्ने तमसि तस्थिवांसम् । वैश्वानरोऽवतूतये नोऽमर्त्योऽवतूतये नः ॥
6.9.e: All the Gods bowed them down in fear before thee, Agni, when thou wast dwelling in the darkness.  Vaiśvānara be gracious to assist us, may the Immortal favour us and help us.

6.10.d: पुरो वो मन्द्रं दिव्यं सुवृक्तिं प्रयति यज्ञे अग्निमध्वरे दधिध्वम् । पुर उक्थेभिः स हि नो विभावा स्वध्वरा करति जातवेदाः ॥
6.10.e: INSTALL at sacrifice, while the rite advances, your pleasant, heavenly Agni, meet for praises.  With hymns-for he illumines us-install him. He, Jātavedas, makes our rites successful.

6.10.d: तमु द्युमः पुर्वणीक होतरग्ने अग्निभिर्मनुष इधानः । स्तोमं यमस्मै ममतेव शूषं घृतं न शुचि मतयः पवन्ते ॥
6.10.e: Hear this laud, Radiant Priest of many aspects, O Agni with the fires of man enkindled,  Laud which bards send forth pure as sacred butter, strength to this man, as ’twere for self-advantage.

6.10.d: पीपाय स श्रवसा मर्त्येषु यो अग्नये ददाश विप्र उक्थैः । चित्राभिस्तमूतिभिश्चित्रशोचिर्व्रजस्य साता गोमतो दधाति ॥
6.10.e: Mid mortal men that singer thrives in glory who offers gifts with hymns of praise to Agni,  And the God, wondrous bright, with wondrous succours helps him to win a stable filled with cattle.

6.10.d: आ यः पप्रौ जायमान उर्वी दूरेदृशा भासा कृष्णाध्वा । अध बहु चित्तम ऊर्म्यायास्तिरः शोचिषा ददृशे पावकः ॥
6.10.e: He, at his birth, whose path is black behind him, filled heaven and earth with far-apparent splendour:  And he himself hath been. through night's thick darkness, made manifest by light, the Purifier.

6.10.d: नू नश्चित्रं पुरुवाजाभिरूती अग्ने रयिं मघवद्भ्यश्च धेहि । ये राधसा श्रवसा चात्यन्यान्त्सुवीर्येभिश्चाभि सन्ति जनान् ॥
6.10.e: With thy most mighty aid, confer, O Agni, wonderful wealth on us and on our princes,  Who stand preeminent, surpassing others in liberal gifts, in fame, and hero virtues.

6.10.d: इमं यज्ञं चनो धा अग्न उशन्यं त आसानो जुहुते हविष्मान् । भरद्वाजेषु दधिषे सुवृक्तिमवीर्वाजस्य गध्यस्य सातौ ॥
6.10.e: Agni, accept this sacrifice with gladness, which, seated here, the worshipper presenteth.  Fair hymns hadst thou among the Bharadvājas, and holpest them to gain abundant vigour.

6.10.d: वि द्वेषांसीनुहि वर्धयेळां मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ॥
6.10.e: Scatter our foes, increase our store. May we he glad a hundred winters with brave sons.

6.11.d: यजस्व होतरिषितो यजीयानग्ने बाधो मरुतां न प्रयुक्ति । आ नो मित्रावरुणा नासत्या द्यावा होत्राय पृथिवी ववृत्याः ॥
6.11.e: EAGERLY Sacrifice thou, most skilful, Agni! Priest, pressing on as if the Maruts sent thee.  To our oblation bring the two Nāsatyas, Mitra and Varuṇa and Earth and Heaven.

6.11.d: त्वं होता मन्द्रतमो नो अध्रुगन्तर्देवो विदथा मर्त्येषु । पावकया जुह्वा३ वह्निरासाग्ने यजस्व तन्वं१ तव स्वाम् ॥
6.11.e: Thou art our guileless, most delightful Herald, the God, among mankind, of holy synods.  A Priest with purifying tongue, O Agni, sacrifice with thy mouth to thine own body.

6.11.d: धन्या चिद्धि त्वे धिषणा वष्टि प्र देवाञ्जन्म गृणते यजध्यै । वेपिष्ठो अङ्गिरसां यद्ध विप्रो मधु च्छन्दो भनति रेभ इष्टौ ॥
6.11.e: For even the blessed longing that is in thee would bring the Gods down to the singer's worship,  When the Aṅgirases' sagest Sage, the Poet, sings the sweet measure at the solemn service.

6.11.d: अदिद्युतत्स्वपाको विभावाग्ने यजस्व रोदसी उरूची । आयुं न यं नमसा रातहव्या अञ्जन्ति सुप्रयसं पञ्च जनाः ॥
6.11.e: Bright hath he beamed, the wise, the far-refulgent. Worship the two widespreading Worlds, O Agni,  Whom as the Living One rich in oblations the Five Tribes, bringing gifts, adorn with homage.

6.11.d: वृञ्जे ह यन्नमसा बर्हिरग्नावयामि स्रुग्घृतवती सुवृक्तिः । अम्यक्षि सद्म सदने पृथिव्या अश्रायि यज्ञः सूर्ये न चक्षुः ॥
6.11.e: When I with reverence clip the grass for Agni, when the trimmed ladle, fullof oil, is lifted,  Firm on the seat of earth is based the altar: eye-like, the sacrifice is directed Sun-ward.

6.11.d: दशस्या नः पुर्वणीक होतर्देवेभिरग्ने अग्निभिरिधानः । रायः सूनो सहसो वावसाना अति स्रसेम वृजनं नांहः ॥
6.11.e: Enrich us, O thou Priest of many aspects, with the Gods, Agni, with thy fires, enkindled.  O Son of Strength, clad in the robe of riches, may we escape from woe as from  a prison.

6.12.d: मध्ये होता दुरोणे बर्हिषो राळग्निस्तोदस्य रोदसी यजध्यै । अयं स सूनुः सहस ऋतावा दूरात्सूर्यो न शोचिषा ततान ॥
6.12.e: KING of trimmed grass, Herald within the dwelling, may Agni worship the Impeller's World-halves.  He, Son of Strength, the Holy, from a distance hath spread himself abroad with light like Sūrya.

6.12.d: आ यस्मिन्त्वे स्वपाके यजत्र यक्षद्राजन्त्सर्वतातेव नु द्यौः । त्रिषधस्थस्ततरुषो न जंहो हव्या मघानि मानुषा यजध्यै ॥
6.12.e: In thee, most wise, shall Dyaus, for full perfection, King! Holy One! pronounce the call to worship.  Found in three places, like the Speeder's footstep, come to present men's riches as oblations!

6.12.d: तेजिष्ठा यस्यारतिर्वनेराट् तोदो अध्वन्न वृधसानो अद्यौत् । अद्रोघो न द्रविता चेतति त्मन्नमर्त्योऽवर्त्र ओषधीषु ॥
6.12.e: Whose blaze most splendid, sovran in the forest, shines waxing on his way like the - Impeller.  He knows himself, like as a guileless smelter, not to be stayed among the plants, Immortal.

6.12.d: सास्माकेभिरेतरी न शूषैरग्निः ष्टवे दम आ जातवेदाः । द्र्वन्नो वन्वन्क्रत्वा नार्वोस्रः पितेव जारयायि यज्ञैः ॥
6.12.e: Our friends extol him like a steed for vigour even Agni in the dwelling, jatave~as.  Trce-fed, he fights with power as doth a champion, like Dawn's Sire to be praised with sacrifices.

6.12.d: अध स्मास्य पनयन्ति भासो वृथा यत्तक्षदनुयाति पृथ्वीम् । सद्यो यः स्यन्द्रो विषितो धवीयानृणो न तायुरति धन्वा राट् ॥
6.12.e: Men wonder at his shining glows when, paring the woods with case, o’er the broad earth he goeth,  And, like a rushing flood, loosed quickly, burneth, swift as a guilty thief, o’er desert places.

6.12.d: स त्वं नो अर्वन्निदाया विश्वेभिरग्ने अग्निभिरिधानः । वेषि रायो वि यासि दुच्छुना मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ॥
6.12.e: So mighty thou protectest us from slander, O Champion, Agni! with all fires enkindled.  Bring opulence and drive away affliction. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.

6.13.d: त्वद्विश्वा सुभग सौभगान्यग्ने वि यन्ति वनिनो न वयाः । श्रुष्टी रयिर्वाजो वृत्रतूर्ये दिवो वृष्टिरीड्यो रीतिरपाम् ॥
6.13.e: FROM thee, as branches from a tree, O Agni, from thee, Auspicious God! spring all our blessings-  Wealth swiftly, strength in battle with our foemen, the rain besought of heaven, the flow of waters.

6.13.d: त्वं भगो न आ हि रत्नमिषे परिज्मेव क्षयसि दस्मवर्चाः । अग्ने मित्रो न बृहत ऋतस्यासि क्षत्ता वामस्य देव भूरेः ॥
6.13.e: Thou art our Bhaga to send wealth thou dwellest, like circumambient air, with wondrous splendour.  Friend art thou of the lofty Law, like Mitra, Controller, Agni! God! of many a blessing.

6.13.d: स सत्पतिः शवसा हन्ति वृत्रमग्ने विप्रो वि पणेर्भर्ति वाजम् । यं त्वं प्रचेत ऋतजात राया सजोषा नप्त्रापां हिनोषि ॥
6.13.e: Agni! the hero slays with might his foeman; the singer bears away the Paṇi's booty-  Even he whom thou, Sage, born in Law, incitest by wealth, accordant with the Child of Waters.

6.13.d: यस्ते सूनो सहसो गीर्भिरुक्थैर्यज्ञैर्मर्तो निशितिं वेद्यानट् । विश्वं स देव प्रति वारमग्ने धत्ते धान्यं१ पत्यते वसव्यैः ॥
6.13.e: The man who, Son of Strength 1 with sacrifices, hymns, lauds, attracts thy fervour to the altar,  Enjoys each precious thing, O God, O Agni, gains wealth of corn and is the lord of treasures.

6.13.d: ता नृभ्य आ सौश्रवसा सुवीराग्ने सूनो सहसः पुष्यसे धाः । कृणोषि यच्छवसा भूरि पश्वो वयो वृकायारये जसुरये ॥
6.13.e: Grant, Son of Strength, to men for their subsistence such things as bring high fame and hero children.  For thou with might givest much food in cattle even to the wicked wolf when he is hungry.

6.13.d: वद्मा सूनो सहसो नो विहाया अग्ने तोकं तनयं वाजि नो दाः । विश्वाभिर्गीर्भिरभि पूर्तिमश्यां मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ॥
6.13.e: Eloquent, Son of Strength, Most Mighty, Agni, vouchsafe us seed and offspring, full of vigour.  May I by all my songs obtain abundance. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.

6.14.d: अग्ना यो मर्त्यो दुवो धियं जुजोष धीतिभिः । भसन्नु ष प्र पूर्व्य इषं वुरीतावसे ॥
6.14.e: WHOSO to Agni hath endeared his thought and service by his hymns,  That mortal cats before the rest, and finds sufficiency of food.

6.14.d: अग्निरिद्धि प्रचेता अग्निर्वेधस्तम ऋषिः । अग्निं होतारमीळते यज्ञेषु मनुषो विशः ॥
6.14.e: Agni, in truth, is passing wise, most skilled in ordering, a Seer.  At sacrifices Manus' sons glorify Agni as their Priest.

6.14.d: नाना ह्य१ग्नेऽवसे स्पर्धन्ते रायो अर्यः । तूर्वन्तो दस्युमायवो व्रतैः सीक्षन्तो अव्रतम् ॥
6.14.e: The foeman's wealth in many a place, Agni, is emulous to help.  Men fight the fiend, and seek by rites to overcome the riteless foe.

6.14.d: अग्निरप्सामृतीषहं वीरं ददाति सत्पतिम् । यस्य त्रसन्ति शवसः संचक्षि शत्रवो भिया ॥
6.14.e: Agni bestows the hero chief, winner of waters, firm in fray.  Soon as they look upon his might his enemies tremble in alarm.

6.14.d: अग्निर्हि विद्मना निदो देवो मर्तमुरुष्यति । सहावा यस्यावृतो रयिर्वाजेष्ववृतः ॥
6.14.e: For with his wisdom Agni, God, protects the mortal from reproach,  Whose conquering wealth is never checked, is never checked in deeds of might.

6.14.d: अच्छा नो मित्रमहो देव देवानग्ने वोचः सुमतिं रोदस्योः । वीहि स्वस्तिं सुक्षितिं दिवो नॄन्द्विषो अंहांसि दुरिता तरेम ता तरेम तवावसा तरेम ॥
6.14.e: O Agni, God with Mitra's might call hither the favour of the Gods from earth and heaven.  Bring weal from heaven that men may dwell securely. May we o’ercome the foe's malign oppressions, may we o’ercome them, through thy help o’ercome them.

6.15.d: इममू षु वो अतिथिमुषर्बुधं विश्वासां विशां पतिमृञ्जसे गिरा । वेतीद्दिवो जनुषा कच्चिदा शुचिर्ज्योक्चिदत्ति गर्भो यदच्युतम् ॥
6.15.e: WITH this my song I strive to reach this guest of yours, who wakes at early morn, the Lord of all the tribes.  Each time he comes from heaven, the Pure One from of old: from ancient days the Child cats everlasting food.

6.15.d: मित्रं न यं सुधितं भृगवो दधुर्वनस्पतावीड्यमूर्ध्वशोचिषम् । स त्वं सुप्रीतो वीतहव्ये अद्भुत प्रशस्तिभिर्महयसे दिवेदिवे ॥
6.15.e: Whom, well-dis sed, the Blirgus stablished as a rriend, whom men must glorify, high-flaming in the wood.  As such, most friendly, thou art every day extolled in lauds by Vitahavya, O thou wondrous God.

6.15.d: स त्वं दक्षस्यावृको वृधो भूरर्यः परस्यान्तरस्य तरुषः । रायः सूनो सहसो मर्त्येष्वा छर्दिर्यच्छ वीतहव्याय सप्रथो भरद्वाजाय सप्रथः ॥
6.15.e: Be thou the foeless helper of the skilful man, subduer of the enemy near or far away.  Bestow a wealthy home on men, O Son of Strength. Give Vitahavya riches spreading far and wide, give Bharadvāja wide-spread wealth.

6.15.d: द्युतानं वो अतिथिं स्वर्णरमग्निं होतारं मनुषः स्वध्वरम् । विप्रं न द्युक्षवचसं सुवृक्तिभिर्हव्यवाहमरतिं देवमृञ्जसे ॥
6.15.e: Him, your refulgent guest, Agni who comes from heaven, the Herald of mankind, well-skilled in sacred rites,  Who, like a holy singer, utters heavenly words, oblation-bearer, envoy, God, I seek with hymns.

6.15.d: पावकया यश्चितयन्त्या कृपा क्षामन्रुरुच उषसो न भानुना । तूर्वन्न यामन्नेतशस्य नू रण आ यो घृणे न ततृषाणो अजरः ॥
