6.15.e: Who with his purifying, eye-attracting form hath shone upon the earth as with the light of Dawn;  Who speeding on, as in the fight of Etaia, cometh, untouched by age, as one athirst in heat.

6.15.d: अग्निमग्निं वः समिधा दुवस्यत प्रियम्प्रियं वो अतिथिं गृणीषणि । उप वो गीर्भिरमृतं विवासत देवो देवेषु वनते हि वार्यं देवो देवेषु वनते हि नो दुवः ॥
6.15.e: Worship ye Agni, Agni, with your log of wood; praise your beloved, your beloved guest with songs.  Invite ye the Immortal hither with your hymns. A God among the Gods, he loveth what is choice, loveth our service, God mid Gods.

6.15.d: समिद्धमग्निं समिधा गिरा गृणे शुचिं पावकं पुरो अध्वरे ध्रुवम् । विप्रं होतारं पुरुवारमद्रुहं कविं सुम्नैरीमहे जातवेदसम् ॥
6.15.e: Agni inflamed with fuel in my song I sing, pure, Cleanser, steadlast, set in tront at sacrifice.  Wise Jātavedas we implore with prayers for bliss the Priest, the holy Singer, bounteous, void of guile.

6.15.d: त्वां दूतमग्ने अमृतं युगेयुगे हव्यवाहं दधिरे पायुमीड्यम् । देवासश्च मर्तासश्च जागृविं विभुं विश्पतिं नमसा नि षेदिरे ॥
6.15.e: Men, Agni, in each age have made thee, Deathiess One, their envoy, offering-bearer, guard adorable.  With reverence Gods and mortals have established thee, the ever-watchful, omnipresent Household Lord.

6.15.d: विभूषन्नग्न उभयाँ अनु व्रता दूतो देवानां रजसी समीयसे । यत्ते धीतिं सुमतिमावृणीमहेऽध स्मा नस्त्रिवरूथः शिवो भव ॥
6.15.e: Thou, Agni, ordering the works and ways of both, as envoy of the Gods traversest both the worlds.  When we lay claim to thy regard and gracious fare, be thou to us a thriceprotecting friendly guard.

6.15.d: तं सुप्रतीकं सुदृशं स्वञ्चमविद्वांसो विदुष्टरं सपेम । स यक्षद्विश्वा वयुनानि विद्वान्प्र हव्यमग्निरमृतेषु वोचत् ॥
6.15.e: Him fair of face, rapid, and fair to look on, him very wise may we who know not follow.  Let him who knows all rules invite for worship, Agru announce our offering to the Immortals.

6.15.d: तमग्ने पास्युत तं पिपर्षि यस्त आनट् कवये शूर धीतिम् । यज्ञस्य वा निशितिं वोदितिं वा तमित्पृणक्षि शवसोत राया ॥
6.15.e: Him, Agni, thou deliverest and savest who brings him prayer to thee the Wise, O Hero,  The end of sacrifice or its inception; yea, thou endowest him with power and riches.

6.15.d: त्वमग्ने वनुष्यतो नि पाहि त्वमु नः सहसावन्नवद्यात् । सं त्वा ध्वस्मन्वदभ्येतु पाथः सं रयिः स्पृहयाय्यः सहस्री ॥
6.15.e: Guard us from him who would assail us, Agni; preserve us, O thou Victor, from dishonour.  Here let the place of darkening come upon thee: may wealth be ours, desirable in thousands.

6.15.d: अग्निर्होता गृहपतिः स राजा विश्वा वेद जनिमा जातवेदाः । देवानामुत यो मर्त्यानां यजिष्ठः स प्र यजतामृतावा ॥
6.15.e: Agni, the Priest, is King, Lord of the homestead, he, Jatayedas, knows all generations.  Most skilful worshipper mid Gods and mortals, may he begin the sacrifice, the Holy.

6.15.d: अग्ने यदद्य विशो अध्वरस्य होतः पावकशोचे वेष्ट्वं हि यज्वा । ऋता यजासि महिना वि यद्भूर्हव्या वह यविष्ठ या ते अद्य ॥
6.15.e: Whate’er to-day thou, bright-flamed Priest, enjoyest from the man's rite-for thou art sacrificer-  Worship, for duly dost thou spread in greatness: bear off thine ofrerings of to-day, Most Youthful.

6.15.d: अभि प्रयांसि सुधितानि हि ख्यो नि त्वा दधीत रोदसी यजध्यै । अवा नो मघवन्वाजसातावग्ने विश्वानि दुरिता तरेम ता तरेम तवावसा तरेम ॥
6.15.e: Look thou upon the viands duly laid for thee. Fain would he set thee here to worship Heaven and,Earth.  Help us, O liberal Agni, in the strife for spoil, so that we may o’ercome all things that trouble us, o’ercome, o’ercome them with thy help.

6.15.d: अग्ने विश्वेभिः स्वनीक देवैरूर्णावन्तं प्रथमः सीद योनिम् । कुलायिनं घृतवन्तं सवित्रे यज्ञं नय यजमानाय साधु ॥
6.15.e: Together with all Gods, O fair-faced Agni, be seated first upon the woollined altar,  Nest-like, bedewed with oil. Bear this our worship to Savitar who sacrifices rightly.

6.15.d: इममु त्यमथर्ववदग्निं मन्थन्ति वेधसः । यमङ्कूयन्तमानयन्नमूरं श्याव्याभ्यः ॥
6.15.e: Here the arranging priests, as did Atharvan, rub this Agni forth,  Whom, not bewildered, as he moved in winding ways, they brought from gloom.

6.15.d: जनिष्वा देववीतये सर्वताता स्वस्तये । आ देवान्वक्ष्यमृताँ ऋतावृधो यज्ञं देवेषु पिस्पृशः ॥
6.15.e: For the Gods’ banquet be thou born, for full perfection and for weal.  Bring the Immortal Gods who strengthen holy Law: so let our sacrifice reach the Gods.

6.15.d: वयमु त्वा गृहपते जनानामग्ने अकर्म समिधा बृहन्तम् । अस्थूरि नो गार्हपत्यानि सन्तु तिग्मेन नस्तेजसा सं शिशाधि ॥
6.15.e: O Agni, Lord and Master of men's homesteads, with kindled fuel we have made thee mighty.  Let not our household gear be found defective. Sharpen us with thy penetrating splendour.

6.16.d: त्वमग्ने यज्ञानां होता विश्वेषां हितः । देवेभिर्मानुषे जने ॥
6.16.e: PRIEST of all sacrifices hast thou been appointed by the Gods,  Agni, amid the race of man.

6.16.d: स नो मन्द्राभिरध्वरे जिह्वाभिर्यजा महः । आ देवान्वक्षि यक्षि च ॥
6.16.e: So with thy joyous tongues for us sacrifice nobly in this rite.  Bring thou the Gods and worship them.

6.16.d: वेत्था हि वेधो अध्वनः पथश्च देवाञ्जसा । अग्ने यज्ञेषु सुक्रतो ॥
6.16.e: For well, O God, Disposer, thou knowest, straight on, the paths and ways,  Agni, most wise in sacrifice.

6.16.d: त्वामीळे अध द्विता भरतो वाजिभिः शुनम् । ईजे यज्ञेषु यज्ञियम् ॥
6.16.e: Thee, too, hath Bhārata of old, with mighty men, implored for bliss.  And worshipped thee the worshipful.

6.16.d: त्वमिमा वार्या पुरु दिवोदासाय सुन्वते । भरद्वाजाय दाशुषे ॥
6.16.e: Thou givest these abundant boons to Divodāsa pouring forth,  To Bharadvāja offering gifts.

6.16.d: त्वं दूतो अमर्त्य आ वहा दैव्यं जनम् । शृण्वन्विप्रस्य सुष्टुतिम् ॥
6.16.e: Do thou, Immortal Messenger, bring hither the Celestial Folk;  Hearing the singer's eulogy.

6.16.d: त्वामग्ने स्वाध्यो३ मर्तासो देववीतये । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते ॥
6.16.e: Mortals with pious thought implore thee, Agni, God, at holy rites,  To come unto the feast of Gods.

6.16.d: तव प्र यक्षि संदृशमुत क्रतुं सुदानवः । विश्वे जुषन्त कामिनः ॥
6.16.e: I glorify thine aspect and the might of thee the Bountilul.  All those who love shall joy in thee,

6.16.d: त्वं होता मनुर्हितो वह्निरासा विदुष्टरः । अग्ने यक्षि दिवो विशः ॥
6.16.e: Invoker placed by Manus, thou, Agni, art near, the wisest Priest:  Pay worship to the Tribes of Heaven.

6.16.d: अग्न आ याहि वीतये गृणानो हव्यदातये । नि होता सत्सि बर्हिषि ॥
6.16.e: Come, Agni, lauded, to the feast; come to the offering of the gifts.  As Priest be seated on the grass.

6.16.d: तं त्वा समिद्भिरङ्गिरो घृतेन वर्धयामसि । बृहच्छोचा यविष्ठ्य ॥
6.16.e: So, Aṅgiras, we make thee strong with fuel and with holy oil.  Blaze high, thou youngest of the Gods.

6.16.d: स नः पृथु श्रवाय्यमच्छा देव विवाससि । बृहदग्ने सुवीर्यम् ॥
6.16.e: For us thou winnest, Agni, God, heroic strength exceeding great,  Far-spreading and of high renown.

6.16.d: त्वामग्ने पुष्करादध्यथर्वा निरमन्थत । मूर्ध्नो विश्वस्य वाघतः ॥
6.16.e: Agni, Atharvan brought thee forth, by rubbing, from the lotus-flower,  The head of Visva, of the Priest.

6.16.d: तमु त्वा दध्यङ्ङृषिः पुत्र ईधे अथर्वणः । वृत्रहणं पुरंदरम् ॥
6.16.e: Thee. Vṛtra's slayer, breaker down of castles, hath Atharvan's son,  Dadhyac the Ṛṣi, lighted up.

6.16.d: तमु त्वा पाथ्यो वृषा समीधे दस्युहन्तमम् । धनंजयं रणेरणे ॥
6.16.e: The hero Pathya kindled thee the Dasyus'. most destructive foe,  Winner of spoil in every fight.

6.16.d: एह्यू षु ब्रवाणि तेऽग्न इत्थेतरा गिरः । एभिर्वर्धास इन्दुभिः ॥
6.16.e: Come, here, O Agni, will I sing verily other songs to thee,  And with these drops shalt thou grow strong.

6.16.d: यत्र क्व च ते मनो दक्षं दधस उत्तरम् । तत्रा सदः कृणवसे ॥
6.16.e: Where’er thy mind applies itself, vigour preeminent hast thou:  There wilt thou gain a dwelling-place.

6.16.d: नहि ते पूर्तमक्षिपद्भुवन्नेमानां वसो । अथा दुवो वनवसे ॥
6.16.e: Not for a moment only lasts thy bounty, good to many a one!  Our service therefore shalt thou gain.

6.16.d: आग्निरगामि भारतो वृत्रहा पुरुचेतनः । दिवोदासस्य सत्पतिः ॥
6.16.e: Agni, the Bhārata, hath been sought, the Vṛtra-slayer, marked of all,  Yea, Divodāsa's Hero Lord.

6.16.d: स हि विश्वाति पार्थिवा रयिं दाशन्महित्वना । वन्वन्नवातो अस्तृतः ॥
6.16.e: For he gave riches that surpass in greatness all the things of earth,  Fighting untroubled, unsubdued.

6.16.d: स प्रत्नवन्नवीयसाग्ने द्युम्नेन संयता । बृहत्ततन्थ भानुना ॥
6.16.e: Thou, Agni, as in days of old, with recent glory, gathered light,  Hast overspread the lofty heaven.

6.16.d: प्र वः सखायो अग्नये स्तोमं यज्ञं च धृष्णुया । अर्च गाय च वेधसे ॥
6.16.e: Bring to your Agni, O my friends, boldly your laud and sacrifice:  Give the Disposer praise and song.

6.16.d: स हि यो मानुषा युगा सीदद्धोता कविक्रतुः । दूतश्च हव्यवाहनः ॥
6.16.e: For as sagacious Herald he hath sat through every age of man,  Oblation-bearing messenger.

6.16.d: ता राजाना शुचिव्रतादित्यान्मारुतं गणम् । वसो यक्षीह रोदसी ॥
6.16.e: Bring those Two Kings whose ways are pure, Ādityas, and the Marut host,  Excellent God! and Heaven and Earth.

6.16.d: वस्वी ते अग्ने संदृष्टिरिषयते मर्त्याय । ऊर्जो नपादमृतस्य ॥
6.16.e: For strong and active mortal man, excellent, Agni, is the look Of thee Immortal, Son of Strength

6.16.d: क्रत्वा दा अस्तु श्रेष्ठोऽद्य त्वा वन्वन्त्सुरेक्णाः । मर्त आनाश सुवृक्तिम् ॥
6.16.e: Rich through his wisdom, noblest be the giver serving thee to-day:  The man hath brought his hymn of praise.

6.16.d: ते ते अग्ने त्वोता इषयन्तो विश्वमायुः । तरन्तो अर्यो अरातीर्वन्वन्तो अर्यो अरातीः ॥
6.16.e: These, Agni, these are helped by thee, who strong and active all their lives,  O'ercome the malice of the foe, fight down the malice ofthe foe.

6.16.d: अग्निस्तिग्मेन शोचिषा यासद्विश्वं न्य१त्रिणम् । अग्निर्नो वनते रयिम् ॥
6.16.e: May Agni with his pointed blaze cast down each fierce devouring fiend  May Agni win us wealth by war.

6.16.d: सुवीरं रयिमा भर जातवेदो विचर्षणे । जहि रक्षांसि सुक्रतो ॥
6.16.e: O active Jātavedas, bring riches with store of hero sons:  Slay thou the demons, O Most Wise.

6.16.d: त्वं नः पाह्यंहसो जातवेदो अघायतः । रक्षा णो ब्रह्मणस्कवे ॥
6.16.e: Keep us, O Jātavedas, from the troubling of the man of sin:  Guard us thou Sage who knowest prayer.

6.16.d: यो नो अग्ने दुरेव आ मर्तो वधाय दाशति । तस्मान्नः पाह्यंहसः ॥
6.16.e: Whatever sinner, Agni, brings oblations to procure our death,  Save us from woe that he would work.

6.16.d: त्वं तं देव जिह्वया परि बाधस्व दुष्कृतम् । मर्तो यो नो जिघांसति ॥
6.16.e: Drive from us with thy tongue, O God, the man who doeth evil deeds,  The mortal who would strike us dead.

6.16.d: भरद्वाजाय सप्रथः शर्म यच्छ सहन्त्य । अग्ने वरेण्यं वसु ॥
6.16.e: Give shelter reaching far and wide to Bharadvāja, conquering Lord!  Agni, send wealth most excellent.

6.16.d: अग्निर्वृत्राणि जङ्घनद्द्रविणस्युर्विपन्यया । समिद्धः शुक्र आहुतः ॥
6.16.e: May Agni slay the Vṛtras,—fain for riches, through the lord of song,  Served with oblation, kindled, bright.

6.16.d: गर्भे मातुः पितुष्पिता विदिद्युतानो अक्षरे । सीदन्नृतस्य योनिमा ॥
6.16.e: His Father's Father, shining in his Mother's everlasting side,  Set on the seat of holy Law.

6.16.d: ब्रह्म प्रजावदा भर जातवेदो विचर्षणे । अग्ने यद्दीदयद्दिवि ॥
6.16.e: O active Jātavedas, bring devotion that wins progeny, Agni, that it may shine to heaven.

6.16.d: उप त्वा रण्वसंदृशं प्रयस्वन्तः सहस्कृत । अग्ने ससृज्महे गिरः ॥
6.16.e: O Child of Strength, to thee whose look is lovely we with dainty food,  O Agni, have poured forth our songs.

6.16.d: उप च्छायामिव घृणेरगन्म शर्म ते वयम् । अग्ने हिरण्यसंदृशः ॥
6.16.e: To thee for shelter are we come, as to the shade from fervent heat  Agni, who glitterest like gold.

6.16.d: य उग्र इव शर्यहा तिग्मशृङ्गो न वंसगः । अग्ने पुरो रुरोजिथ ॥
6.16.e: Mighty as one who slays with shafts, or like a bull with sharpened horn,  Agni, thou breakest down the forts.

6.16.d: आ यं हस्ते न खादिनं शिशुं जातं न बिभ्रति । विशामग्निं स्वध्वरम् ॥
6.16.e: Whom, like an infant newly born, devourer, in their arms they bear,  Men's Agni, skilled in holy rites.

6.16.d: प्र देवं देववीतये भरता वसुवित्तमम् । आ स्वे योनौ नि षीदतु ॥
6.16.e: Bear to the banquet of the Gods the God best finder-out of wealth,  Let him he seated in his place.

6.16.d: आ जातं जातवेदसि प्रियं शिशीतातिथिम् । स्योन आ गृहपतिम् ॥
6.16.e: In Jātavedas kindle ye the dear guest who hath now appeared  In a soft place, the homestead's Lord.

6.16.d: अग्ने युक्ष्वा हि ये तवाश्वासो देव साधवः । अरं वहन्ति मन्यवे ॥
6.16.e: Harness, O Agni, O thou God, thy steeds which are most excellent:  They bear thee as thy spirit wills.

6.16.d: अच्छा नो याह्या वहाभि प्रयांसि वीतये । आ देवान्त्सोमपीतये ॥
6.16.e: Come hither, bring the Gods to us to taste the sacrificial feast,  To drink the draught of Soma juice.

6.16.d: उदग्ने भारत द्युमदजस्रेण दविद्युतत् । शोचा वि भाह्यजर ॥
6.16.e: O Agni of the Bharatas, blaze high with everlasting might,  Shine forth and gleam, Eternal One.

6.16.d: वीती यो देवं मर्तो दुवस्येदग्निमीळीताध्वरे हविष्मान् । होतारं सत्ययजं रोदस्योरुत्तानहस्तो नमसा विवासेत् ॥
6.16.e: The mortal man who serves the God with banquet, and, bringing gifts at sacrifice, lauds Agni,  May well attract, with prayer and hands uplifted, the Priest of Heaven and Earth, true Sacrificer.

6.16.d: आ ते अग्न ऋचा हविर्हृदा तष्टं भरामसि । ते ते भवन्तूक्षण ऋषभासो वशा उत ॥
6.16.e: Agni, we bring thee, with our hymn, oblation fashioned in the heart.  Let these be oxen unto thee, let these be bulls and kine to thee.

6.16.d: अग्निं देवासो अग्रियमिन्धते वृत्रहन्तमम् । येना वसून्याभृता तृळ्हा रक्षांसि वाजिना ॥
6.16.e: The Gods enkindle Agni, best slayer of Vṛtra, first in rank,  The Mighty, One who brings us wealth and crushes down the Rākṣasas.

6.17.d: पिबा सोममभि यमुग्र तर्द ऊर्वं गव्यं महि गृणान इन्द्र । वि यो धृष्णो वधिषो वज्रहस्त विश्वा वृत्रममित्रिया शवोभिः ॥
6.17.e: DRINK Soma, Mighty One, for which, when lauded, thou breakest through the cattle-stall, O Indra;  Thou who, O Bold One, armed with thunder smotest Vṛtra with might, and every hostile being.

6.17.d: स ईं पाहि य ऋजीषी तरुत्रो यः शिप्रवान्वृषभो यो मतीनाम् । यो गोत्रभिद्वज्रभृद्यो हरिष्ठाः स इन्द्र चित्राँ अभि तृन्धि वाजान् ॥
6.17.e: Drink it thou God who art impetuous victor, Lord of our hymns, with beauteousjaws, the Hero,  Render of kine-stalls, car-borne, thunder-wielding, so pierce thy way to wondrous strength, O Indra.

6.17.d: एवा पाहि प्रत्नथा मन्दतु त्वा श्रुधि ब्रह्म वावृधस्वोत गीर्भिः । आविः सूर्यं कृणुहि पीपिहीषो जहि शत्रूँरभि गा इन्द्र तृन्धि ॥
6.17.e: Drink as of old, and let the draught delight thee. hear thou our prayer and let our songs exalt thee.  Make the Sun visible, make food abundant, slaughter the foes, pierce through and free the cattle.

6.17.d: ते त्वा मदा बृहदिन्द्र स्वधाव इमे पीता उक्षयन्त द्युमन्तम् । महामनूनं तवसं विभूतिं मत्सरासो जर्हृषन्त प्रसाहम् ॥
6.17.e: These gladdening drops, O Indra, Self-sustainer, quaffed shall augment thee in thy mighty splendour.  Yea, let the cheering drops delight thee greatly, great, perfect, strong, powerful, all-subduing.

6.17.d: येभिः सूर्यमुषसं मन्दसानोऽवासयोऽप दृळ्हानि दर्द्रत् । महामद्रिं परि गा इन्द्र सन्तं नुत्था अच्युतं सदसस्परि स्वात् ॥
6.17.e: Gladdened whereby, bursting the firm enclosures, thou gavest splendour to the Sun and Morning.  The mighty rock that compassed in the cattle, ne’er moved, thou shookest from its seat, O Indra.

6.17.d: तव क्रत्वा तव तद्दंसनाभिरामासु पक्वं शच्या नि दीधः । और्णोर्दुर उस्रियाभ्यो वि दृळ्होदूर्वाद्गा असृजो अङ्गिरस्वान् ॥
6.17.e: Thou with thy wisdom, power, and works of wonder, hast stored the ripe milk in the raw cows' udders  Unbarred the firm doors for the kine of Morning, and, with the Aṅgirases, set free the cattle.

6.17.d: पप्राथ क्षां महि दंसो व्यु१र्वीमुप द्यामृष्वो बृहदिन्द्र स्तभायः । अधारयो रोदसी देवपुत्रे प्रत्ने मातरा यह्वी ऋतस्य ॥
6.17.e: Thou hast spread out wide earth, a mighty marvel, and, high thyself, propped lofty heaven, O Indra.  Both worlds, whose Sons are Gods, thou hast supported, young, Mothers from old time ofholy Order.

6.17.d: अध त्वा विश्वे पुर इन्द्र देवा एकं तवसं दधिरे भराय । अदेवो यदभ्यौहिष्ट देवान्त्स्वर्षाता वृणत इन्द्रमत्र ॥
6.17.e: Yea, Indra, all the Deities installed thee their one strong Champion in the van for battle.  What time the godless was the Gods’ assailant, Indra they chose to win the light of heaven.

6.17.d: अध द्यौश्चित्ते अप सा नु वज्राद्द्वितानमद्भियसा स्वस्य मन्योः । अहिं यदिन्द्रो अभ्योहसानं नि चिद्विश्वायुः शयथे जघान ॥
6.17.e: Yea, e’en that heaven itself of old bent backward before thy bolt, in terror of its anger,  When Indra, life of every living creature, smote down within his lair the assailing Dragon.

6.17.d: अध त्वष्टा ते मह उग्र वज्रं सहस्रभृष्टिं ववृतच्छताश्रिम् । निकाममरमणसं येन नवन्तमहिं सं पिणगृजीषिन् ॥
6.17.e: Yea, Strong One! Tvaṣṭar turned for thee, the Mighty, the bolt with thousand spikes and hundred edges,  Eager and prompt at will, wherewith thou crushedst the boasting Dragon, O impetuous Hero.

6.17.d: वर्धान्यं विश्वे मरुतः सजोषाः पचच्छतं महिषाँ इन्द्र तुभ्यम् । पूषा विष्णुस्त्रीणि सरांसि धावन्वृत्रहणं मदिरमंशुमस्मै ॥
6.17.e: He dressed a hundred buffaloes, O Indra, for thee whom all accordant Maruts strengthen.  He, Pūṣan Viṣṇu, poured forth three great vessels to him, the juice that cheers, that slaughters Vṛtra.

6.17.d: आ क्षोदो महि वृतं नदीनां परिष्ठितमसृज ऊर्मिमपाम् । तासामनु प्रवत इन्द्र पन्थां प्रार्दयो नीचीरपसः समुद्रम् ॥
6.17.e: Thou settest free the rushing wave of waters, the floods' great swell encompassed and obstructed.  Along steep slopes their course thou tumedst, Indra, directed downward, speeding to the ocean.

6.17.d: एवा ता विश्वा चकृवांसमिन्द्रं महामुग्रमजुर्यं सहोदाम् । सुवीरं त्वा स्वायुधं सुवज्रमा ब्रह्म नव्यमवसे ववृत्यात् ॥
6.17.e: So may our new prayer bring thee to protect us, thee well-armed Hero with thy bolt of thunder,  Indra, who made these worlds, the Strong, the ty, who never groweth old, the victory-giver.

6.17.d: स नो वाजाय श्रवस इषे च राये धेहि द्युमत इन्द्र विप्रान् । भरद्वाजे नृवत इन्द्र सूरीन्दिवि च स्मैधि पार्ये न इन्द्र ॥
6.17.e: So, Indra, form us brilliant holy singers for strength, for glory, and for food and riches.  Give Bharadvāja hero patrons, Indra Indra, be ours upon the day of trial.

6.17.d: अया वाजं देवहितं सनेम मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ॥
6.17.e: With this may we obtain strength God-appointed, and brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.

6.18.d: तमु ष्टुहि यो अभिभूत्योजा वन्वन्नवातः पुरुहूत इन्द्रः । अषाळ्हमुग्रं सहमानमाभिर्गीर्भिर्वर्ध वृषभं चर्षणीनाम् ॥
6.18.e: GLORIFY him whose might is all-surpassing, Indra the much-invoked who fights uninjured.  Magnify with these songs the never-vanquished, the Strong, the Bull of men, the Mighty Victor.

6.18.d: स युध्मः सत्वा खजकृत्समद्वा तुविम्रक्षो नदनुमाँ ऋजीषी । बृहद्रेणुश्च्यवनो मानुषीणामेकः कृष्टीनामभवत्सहावा ॥
6.18.e: He, Champion, Hero, Warrior, Lord of battles, impetuous, loudly roaring, great destroyer,  Who whirls the dust on high, alone, oerthrower, hath made all races of mankind his subjects.

6.18.d: त्वं ह नु त्यददमायो दस्यूँरेकः कृष्टीरवनोरार्याय । अस्ति स्विन्नु वीर्यं१ तत्त इन्द्र न स्विदस्ति तदृतुथा वि वोचः ॥
6.18.e: Thou, thou alone, hast tamed the Dasyus; singly thou hast subdued the people for the Ārya.  In this, or is it not, thine hero exploit, Indra? Declare it at the proper season.

6.18.d: सदिद्धि ते तुविजातस्य मन्ये सहः सहिष्ठ तुरतस्तुरस्य । उग्रमुग्रस्य तवसस्तवीयोऽरध्रस्य रध्रतुरो बभूव ॥
6.18.e: For true, I deem, thy strength is, thine the Mighty, thine, O Most Potent, thine the Conquering Victor;  Strong, of the strong, Most Mighty, of the mighty, thine, driver of the churl to acts of bounty.

6.18.d: तन्नः प्रत्नं सख्यमस्तु युष्मे इत्था वदद्भिर्वलमङ्गिरोभिः । हन्नच्युतच्युद्दस्मेषयन्तमृणोः पुरो वि दुरो अस्य विश्वाः ॥
6.18.e: Be this our ancient bond of friendship with you and with Aṅgirases here who speak of Vala.  Thou, Wondrous, Shaker of things firm, didst smite him in his fresh strength, and force his doors and castles.

6.18.d: स हि धीभिर्हव्यो अस्त्युग्र ईशानकृन्महति वृत्रतूर्ये । स तोकसाता तनये स वज्री वितन्तसाय्यो अभवत्समत्सु ॥
6.18.e: With holy thoughts must he be called, the Mighty, showing his power in the great fight with Vṛtra.  He must be called to give us seed and offspring, the Thunderer must he moved and sped to battle.

6.18.d: स मज्मना जनिम मानुषाणाममर्त्येन नाम्नाति प्र सर्स्रे । स द्युम्नेन स शवसोत राया स वीर्येण नृतमः समोकाः ॥
6.18.e: He in his might, with name that lives for ever, hath far surpassed all human generations.  He, most heroic, hath his home with splendour, with glory and with riches and with valour.

6.18.d: स यो न मुहे न मिथू जनो भूत्सुमन्तुनामा चुमुरिं धुनिं च । वृणक्पिप्रुं शम्बरं शुष्णमिन्द्रः पुरां च्यौत्नाय शयथाय नू चित् ॥
6.18.e: Stranger to guile, who ne’er was false or faithless, bearing a name that may be well remembered,  Indra crushed Cumuri, Dhuni, Śambara, Pipru, and Śuṣṇa, that their castles fell in ruin.

6.18.d: उदावता त्वक्षसा पन्यसा च वृत्रहत्याय रथमिन्द्र तिष्ठ । धिष्व वज्रं हस्त आ दक्षिणत्राभि प्र मन्द पुरुदत्र मायाः ॥
6.18.e: With saving might that must be praised and lauded, Indra, ascend thy car to smite down Vṛtra.  In thy right hand hold fast thy bolt of thunder, and weaken, Bounteous Lord, his art and magic.

6.18.d: अग्निर्न शुष्कं वनमिन्द्र हेती रक्षो नि धक्ष्यशनिर्न भीमा । गम्भीरय ऋष्वया यो रुरोजाध्वानयद्दुरिता दम्भयच्च ॥
6.18.e: As Agni, as the dart burns the dry forest, like the dread shaft burn down the fiends, O Indra;  Thou who with high deep-reaching spear hast broken, hast covered over mischief and destroyed it.

6.18.d: आ सहस्रं पथिभिरिन्द्र राया तुविद्युम्न तुविवाजेभिरर्वाक् । याहि सूनो सहसो यस्य नू चिददेव ईशे पुरुहूत योतोः ॥
6.18.e: With wealth, by thousand paths come hither, Agni, paths that bring ample strength, O thou Most Splendid.  Come, Son of Strength, o’er whom, Invoked of many! the godless hath no power to keep thee distant.

6.18.d: प्र तुविद्युम्नस्य स्थविरस्य घृष्वेर्दिवो ररप्शे महिमा पृथिव्याः । नास्य शत्रुर्न प्रतिमानमस्ति न प्रतिष्ठिः पुरुमायस्य सह्योः ॥
6.18.e: From heaven, from earth is bruited forth the greatness of him the firm, the fiery, the resplendent.  No foe hath he, no counterpart, no refuge is there from him the Conqueror full of wisdom

6.18.d: प्र तत्ते अद्या करणं कृतं भूत्कुत्सं यदायुमतिथिग्वमस्मै । पुरू सहस्रा नि शिशा अभि क्षामुत्तूर्वयाणं धृषता निनेथ ॥
6.18.e: This day the deed that thou hast done is famous, when thou, for him, with many thousand others  Laidest low Kutsa, Āyu, Atithigva, and boldly didst deliver Tūrvayāṇa.

6.18.d: अनु त्वाहिघ्ने अध देव देवा मदन्विश्वे कवितमं कवीनाम् । करो यत्र वरिवो बाधिताय दिवे जनाय तन्वे गृणानः ॥
6.18.e: In thee, O God, the wisest of the Sages, all Gods were joyful when thou slewest Ahi.  When lauded for thyself, thou gavest freedom to sore-afflicted Heaven and to the people.

6.18.d: अनु द्यावापृथिवी तत्त ओजोऽमर्त्या जिहत इन्द्र देवाः । कृष्वा कृत्नो अकृतं यत्ते अस्त्युक्थं नवीयो जनयस्व यज्ञैः ॥
6.18.e: This power of thine both heaven and earth acknowledge, the deathless Gods acknowledge it, O Indra.  Do what thou ne’er hast done, O Mighty Worker: beget a new hymn at thy sacrifices.

6.19.d: महाँ इन्द्रो नृवदा चर्षणिप्रा उत द्विबर्हा अमिनः सहोभिः । अस्मद्र्यग्वावृधे वीर्यायोरुः पृथुः सुकृतः कर्तृभिर्भूत् ॥
6.19.e: GREAT, hero-like controlling men is Indra, unwasting in his powers, doubled in vastness.  He, turned to us, hath grown to hero vigour: broad, wide, he hath been decked by those who serve him.

6.19.d: इन्द्रमेव धिषणा सातये धाद्बृहन्तमृष्वमजरं युवानम् । अषाळ्हेन शवसा शूशुवांसं सद्यश्चिद्यो वावृधे असामि ॥
6.19.e: The bowl made Indra swift to gather booty, the High, the Lofty, Youthful, Undecaying,  Him who hath waxed by strength which none may conquer, and even at once grown to complete perfection.

6.19.d: पृथू करस्ना बहुला गभस्ती अस्मद्र्य१क्सं मिमीहि श्रवांसि । यूथेव पश्वः पशुपा दमूना अस्माँ इन्द्राभ्या ववृत्स्वाजौ ॥
6.19.e: Stretch out those hands of thine, extend to us-ward thy wide capacious arms, and grant us glory.  Like as the household herdsman guards the cattle, so move thou round about us in the combat.

6.19.d: तं व इन्द्रं चतिनमस्य शाकैरिह नूनं वाजयन्तो हुवेम । यथा चित्पूर्वे जरितार आसुरनेद्या अनवद्या अरिष्टाः ॥
6.19.e: Now, fain for strength, let us invite your Indra hither, who lieth hidden with his Heroes,—  Free from all blame, without reproach, uninjured, e’en as were those who sang, of old, his praises.

6.19.d: धृतव्रतो धनदाः सोमवृद्धः स हि वामस्य वसुनः पुरुक्षुः । सं जग्मिरे पथ्या३ रायो अस्मिन्त्समुद्रे न सिन्धवो यादमानाः ॥
6.19.e: With steadfast laws, wealth-giver, strong through Soma, he hath much fair and precious food to feed us.  In him unite all paths that lead to riches, like rivers that commingle with the ocean.

6.19.d: शविष्ठं न आ भर शूर शव ओजिष्ठमोजो अभिभूत उग्रम् । विश्वा द्युम्ना वृष्ण्या मानुषाणामस्मभ्यं दा हरिवो मादयध्यै ॥
6.19.e: Bring unto us the mightiest might, O Hero, strong and most potent force, thou great Subduer!  All splendid vigorous powers of men vouchsafe us, Lord of Bay Steeds, that they may make us joyful.

6.19.d: यस्ते मदः पृतनाषाळमृध्र इन्द्र तं न आ भर शूशुवांसम् । येन तोकस्य तनयस्य सातौ मंसीमहि जिगीवांसस्त्वोताः ॥
6.19.e: Bring us, grown mighty in its strength, O Indra, thy friendly rapturous joy that wins the battle,  Wherewith by thee assisted and triumphant, we may laud thee in gaining seed and offspring.

6.19.d: आ नो भर वृषणं शुष्ममिन्द्र धनस्पृतं शूशुवांसं सुदक्षम् । येन वंसाम पृतनासु शत्रून्तवोतिभिरुत जामीँरजामीन् ॥
6.19.e: Indra, bestow on us the power heroic skilled and exceeding strong, that wins the booty,  Wherewith, by thine assistance, we may conquer our foes in battle, be they kin or stranger.

6.19.d: आ ते शुष्मो वृषभ एतु पश्चादोत्तरादधरादा पुरस्तात् । आ विश्वतो अभि समेत्वर्वाङिन्द्र द्युम्नं स्वर्वद्धेह्यस्मे ॥
6.19.e: Let thine heroic strength come from behind us, before us, from above us or below us.  From every side may it approach us, Indra. Give us the glory of the realm of splendour.

6.19.d: नृवत्त इन्द्र नृतमाभिरूती वंसीमहि वामं श्रोमतेभिः । ईक्षे हि वस्व उभयस्य राजन्धा रत्नं महि स्थूरं बृहन्तम् ॥
6.19.e: With most heroic aid from thee, like heroes Indra, may we win wealth by deeds glory.  Thou, King, art Lord of earthly, heavenly treasure: vouchsafe us riches vast, sublime, and lasting.

6.19.d: मरुत्वन्तं वृषभं वावृधानमकवारिं दिव्यं शासमिन्द्रम् । विश्वासाहमवसे नूतनायोग्रं सहोदामिह तं हुवेम ॥
6.19.e: The Bull, whose strength hath waxed, whom Maruts follow, free-giving Indra, the Celestial Ruler,  Mighty, all-conquering, the victory-giver, him let us call to grant us new protection.

6.19.d: जनं वज्रिन्महि चिन्मन्यमानमेभ्यो नृभ्यो रन्धया येष्वस्मि । अधा हि त्वा पृथिव्यां शूरसातौ हवामहे तनये गोष्वप्सु ॥
6.19.e: Give up the people who are high and haughty to these men and to me, O Thunder-wielder!  Therefore upon the earth do we invoke thee, where heroes win, for sons and kine and waters.

6.19.d: वयं त एभिः पुरुहूत सख्यैः शत्रोःशत्रोरुत्तर इत्स्याम । घ्नन्तो वृत्राण्युभयानि शूर राया मदेम बृहता त्वोताः ॥
6.19.e: Through these thy friendships, God invoked of many! may we be victors over every foeman.  Slaying both kinds of foe, may we, O Hero, be happy, helped by thee, with ample riches.

6.20.d: द्यौर्न य इन्द्राभि भूमार्यस्तस्थौ रयिः शवसा पृत्सु जनान् । तं नः सहस्रभरमुर्वरासां दद्धि सूनो सहसो वृत्रतुरम् ॥
6.20.e: GIVE us wealth, Indra, that with might, as heaven o’ertops the earth, o’ercomes our foes in battle  Wealth that brings thousands and that wins the corn-lands, wealth, Son of Strength! that vanquishes the foeman.

6.20.d: दिवो न तुभ्यमन्विन्द्र सत्रासुर्यं देवेभिर्धायि विश्वम् । अहिं यद्वृत्रमपो वव्रिवांसं हन्नृजीषिन्विष्णुना सचानः ॥
6.20.e: Even as the power of Dyaus, to thee, O Indra, all Asura sway was by the Gods entrusted,  When thou, Impetuous! leagued with Viṣṇu, slewest Vṛtra the Dragon who enclosed the waters.

6.20.d: तूर्वन्नोजीयान्तवसस्तवीयान्कृतब्रह्मेन्द्रो वृद्धमहाः । राजाभवन्मधुनः सोम्यस्य विश्वासां यत्पुरां दर्त्नुमावत् ॥
6.20.e: Indra, Strong, Victor, Mightier than the mighty, addressed with prayer and perfect in his splendour,  Lord of the bolt that breaketh forts in pieces, became the King of the sweet juice of Soma..

6.20.d: शतैरपद्रन्पणय इन्द्रात्र दशोणये कवयेऽर्कसातौ । वधैः शुष्णस्याशुषस्य मायाः पित्वो नारिरेचीत्किं चन प्र ॥
6.20.e: There, Indra, while the light was won, the Paṇis f1ed, 'neath a hundred blows, for wise Dasoni,  And greedy Śuṣṇa's magical devices nor left he any of their food remaining.

6.20.d: महो द्रुहो अप विश्वायु धायि वज्रस्य यत्पतने पादि शुष्णः । उरु ष सरथं सारथये करिन्द्रः कुत्साय सूर्यस्य सातौ ॥
6.20.e: What time the thunder fell and Śuṣṇa perished, all life's support from the great Druh was taken.  Indra made room for his car-drivcr Kutsa who sate beside him, when he gained the sunlight.

6.20.d: प्र श्येनो न मदिरमंशुमस्मै शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर्मथायन् । प्रावन्नमीं साप्यं ससन्तं पृणग्राया समिषा सं स्वस्ति ॥
6.20.e: As the Hawk rent for him the stalk that gladdens, he wrenched the head from Namuci the Dāsa.  He guarded Nam, Sayya's son, in slumber, and sated him with food, success, and riches.

6.20.d: वि पिप्रोरहिमायस्य दृळ्हाः पुरो वज्रिञ्छवसा न दर्दः । सुदामन्तद्रेक्णो अप्रमृष्यमृजिश्वने दात्रं दाशुषे दाः ॥
6.20.e: Thou, thunder-armed, with thy great might hast shattered Pipru's strong forts who knew the wiles of serpents.  Thou gavest to thy worshipper Ṛjiśvan imperishable Wealth, O Bounteous Giver.

6.20.d: स वेतसुं दशमायं दशोणिं तूतुजिमिन्द्रः स्वभिष्टिसुम्नः । आ तुग्रं शश्वदिभं द्योतनाय मातुर्न सीमुप सृजा इयध्यै ॥
6.20.e: The crafty Vetasu, the swift Dasni, and Tugra speedily with all his servants,  Hath Indra, gladdening with strong assistance, forced near as ’twere to glorify the Mother.

6.20.d: स ईं स्पृधो वनते अप्रतीतो बिभ्रद्वज्रं वृत्रहणं गभस्तौ । तिष्ठद्धरी अध्यस्तेव गर्ते वचोयुजा वहत इन्द्रमृष्वम् ॥
6.20.e: Resistless, with the hosts he battles, bearing in both his arms the Vṛtra-slaying thunder.  He mounts his Bays, as the car-seat an archer: yoked at a word they bear the lofty Indra.

6.20.d: सनेम तेऽवसा नव्य इन्द्र प्र पूरवः स्तवन्त एना यज्ञैः । सप्त यत्पुरः शर्म शारदीर्दर्द्धन्दासीः पुरुकुत्साय शिक्षन् ॥
6.20.e: May we, O Indra, gain by thy new favour: so Parus laud thee, with their sacrifices,  That thou hast wrecked seven autumn forts, their shelter, slain Dāsa tribes and aided Purukutsa.

6.20.d: त्वं वृध इन्द्र पूर्व्यो भूर्वरिवस्यन्नुशने काव्याय । परा नववास्त्वमनुदेयं महे पित्रे ददाथ स्वं नपातम् ॥
6.20.e: Favouring Uśanā the son of Kavi, thou wast his ancient strengthener, O Indra.  Thou gavest Navavāstva. as a present, to the great father gavest back his grandson.

6.20.d: त्वं धुनिरिन्द्र धुनिमतीर्ऋणोरपः सीरा न स्रवन्तीः । प्र यत्समुद्रमति शूर पर्षि पारया तुर्वशं यदुं स्वस्ति ॥
6.20.e: Thou, roaring Indra, drovest on the waters that made a roaring sound like rushing rivers,  What time, O Hero, o’er the sea thou broughtest, in safety broughtest Turvaśa and Yadu.

6.20.d: तव ह त्यदिन्द्र विश्वमाजौ सस्तो धुनीचुमुरी या ह सिष्वप् । दीदयदित्तुभ्यं सोमेभिः सुन्वन्दभीतिरिध्मभृतिः पक्थ्य१र्कैः ॥
6.20.e: This Indra, was thy work in war: thou sentest Dhuni and Cumuri to sleep and slumber.  Dabhīti lit the flame for thee, and worshipped with fuel, hymns, poured Soma, dressed oblations.

6.21.d: इमा उ त्वा पुरुतमस्य कारोर्हव्यं वीर हव्या हवन्ते । धियो रथेष्ठामजरं नवीयो रयिर्विभूतिरीयते वचस्या ॥
6.21.e: THESE the most constant singer's invocations call thee who art to be invoked, O Hero;  Hymns call anew the chariot-borne, Eternal: by eloquence men gain abundant riches.

6.21.d: तमु स्तुष इन्द्रं यो विदानो गिर्वाहसं गीर्भिर्यज्ञवृद्धम् । यस्य दिवमति मह्ना पृथिव्याः पुरुमायस्य रिरिचे महित्वम् ॥
6.21.e: I praise that Indra, known to all men, honoured with songs, extolled with hymns at sacrifices,  Whose majesty, rich in wondrous arts, surpasseth the magnitude of earth, and heaven in greatness.

6.21.d: स इत्तमोऽवयुनं ततन्वत्सूर्येण वयुनवच्चकार । कदा ते मर्ता अमृतस्य धामेयक्षन्तो न मिनन्ति स्वधावः ॥
6.21.e: He hath made pathways, with the Sun to aid him, throughout the darkness that extended pathless.  Mortals who yearn to worship ne’er dishonour, O Mighty God, thy Law who art Immortal.

6.21.d: यस्ता चकार स कुह स्विदिन्द्रः कमा जनं चरति कासु विक्षु । कस्ते यज्ञो मनसे शं वराय को अर्क इन्द्र कतमः स होता ॥
6.21.e: And he who did these things, where is that Indra? among what tribes? what people doth he visit?  What sacrifice contents thy mind , and wishes? What priest among them all? what hymn, O Indra?

6.21.d: इदा हि ते वेविषतः पुराजाः प्रत्नास आसुः पुरुकृत्सखायः । ये मध्यमास उत नूतनास उतावमस्य पुरुहूत बोधि ॥
6.21.e: Yea, here were they who, born of old, have served thee, thy friends of ancient time, thou active Worker.  Bethink thee now of these, Invoked of many! the midmost and the recent, and the youngest.

6.21.d: तं पृच्छन्तोऽवरासः पराणि प्रत्ना त इन्द्र श्रुत्यानु येमुः । अर्चामसि वीर ब्रह्मवाहो यादेव विद्म तात्त्वा महान्तम् ॥
6.21.e: Inquiring after him, thy later servants, Indra, have gained thy former old traditions.  Hero, to whom the prayer is brought, we praise thee as great for that wherein we know thee mighty.

6.21.d: अभि त्वा पाजो रक्षसो वि तस्थे महि जज्ञानमभि तत्सु तिष्ठ । तव प्रत्नेन युज्येन सख्या वज्रेण धृष्णो अप ता नुदस्व ॥
6.21.e: The demon's strength is gathered fast against thee: great as that strength hath grown, go forth to meet it.  With thine own ancient friend and companion, the thunderbolt, brave Champion! drive it backward.

6.21.d: स तु श्रुधीन्द्र नूतनस्य ब्रह्मण्यतो वीर कारुधायः । त्वं ह्या३पिः प्रदिवि पितॄणां शश्वद्बभूथ सुहव एष्टौ ॥
6.21.e: Hear, too, the prayer of this thy present beadsman, O Indra, Hero, cherishing the singer.  For thou wast aye our fathers' Friend aforetime, still swift to listen to their supplication.

6.21.d: प्रोतये वरुणं मित्रमिन्द्रं मरुतः कृष्वावसे नो अद्य । प्र पूषणं विष्णुमग्निं पुरंधिं सवितारमोषधीः पर्वताँश्च ॥
6.21.e: Bring to our help this day, for our protection, Varuṇa, Mitra , Indra, and the Maruts,  Pūṣan and Viṣṇu, Agni and Purandhi, Savitar also, and the Plants and Mountains.

6.21.d: इम उ त्वा पुरुशाक प्रयज्यो जरितारो अभ्यर्चन्त्यर्कैः । श्रुधी हवमा हुवतो हुवानो न त्वावाँ अन्यो अमृत त्वदस्ति ॥
6.21.e: The singers here exalt with hymns and praises thee who art very Mighty and Most Holy.  Hear, when invoked, the invoker's invocation. Beside thee there is nonelike thee, Immortal!

6.21.d: नू म आ वाचमुप याहि विद्वान्विश्वेभिः सूनो सहसो यजत्रैः । ये अग्निजिह्वा ऋतसाप आसुर्ये मनुं चक्रुरुपरं दसाय ॥
6.21.e: Now to my words come quickly thou who knowest, O Son of Strength, with all who claim our worship,  Who visit sacred rites, whose tongue is Agni, Gods who made Manu stronger than the Dasyu.

6.21.d: स नो बोधि पुरएता सुगेषूत दुर्गेषु पथिकृद्विदानः । ये अश्रमास उरवो वहिष्ठास्तेभिर्न इन्द्राभि वक्षि वाजम् ॥
6.21.e: On good and evil ways be thou our Leader, thou who art known to all as Path-preparer.  Bring power to us, O Indra, with thy Horses, Steeds that are best to draw, broad-backed, unwearied.

6.22.d: य एक इद्धव्यश्चर्षणीनामिन्द्रं तं गीर्भिरभ्यर्च आभिः । यः पत्यते वृषभो वृष्ण्यावान्त्सत्यः सत्वा पुरुमायः सहस्वान् ॥
6.22.e: WITH these my hymns I glorify that Indra who is alone to be invoked by mortals,  The Lord, the Mighty One, of manly vigour, victorious, Hero, true, and full of wisdom.

6.22.d: तमु नः पूर्वे पितरो नवग्वाः सप्त विप्रासो अभि वाजयन्तः । नक्षद्दाभं ततुरिं पर्वतेष्ठामद्रोघवाचं मतिभिः शविष्ठम् ॥
6.22.e: Our sires of old,. Navagvas, sages seven, while urging him to show his might, extolled him,  Dwelling on heights, swift, smiting down opponents, guileless in word, and in his thoughts most mighty.

6.22.d: तमीमह इन्द्रमस्य रायः पुरुवीरस्य नृवतः पुरुक्षोः । यो अस्कृधोयुरजरः स्वर्वान्तमा भर हरिवो मादयध्यै ॥
6.22.e: We seek that Indra to obtain his riches that bring much food, and men, and store of heroes.  Bring us, Lord of Bay Steeds, to make us joyful, celestial wealth, abundant, undecaying.

6.22.d: तन्नो वि वोचो यदि ते पुरा चिज्जरितार आनशुः सुम्नमिन्द्र । कस्ते भागः किं वयो दुध्र खिद्वः पुरुहूत पुरूवसोऽसुरघ्नः ॥
6.22.e: Tell thou us this, if at thy hand aforetime the earlier singers have obtained good fortune,  What is thy share and portion, Strong Subduer, Asura-slayer, rich, invoked of many?

6.22.d: तं पृच्छन्ती वज्रहस्तं रथेष्ठामिन्द्रं वेपी वक्वरी यस्य नू गीः । तुविग्राभं तुविकूर्मिं रभोदां गातुमिषे नक्षते तुम्रमच्छ ॥
6.22.e: He who for car-borne Indra, armed with thunder, hath a hymn, craving, deeply-piercing, fluent,  Who sends a song effectual, firmly-grasping, and strength-bestowing, he comes near the mighty.

6.22.d: अया ह त्यं मायया वावृधानं मनोजुवा स्वतवः पर्वतेन । अच्युता चिद्वीळिता स्वोजो रुजो वि दृळ्हा धृषता विरप्शिन् ॥
6.22.e: Strong of thyself, thou by this art hast shattered, with thought-swift Parvata, him who waxed against thee,  And, Mightiest! roaring! boldly rent in pieces things that were firmly fixed and never shaken.

6.22.d: तं वो धिया नव्यस्या शविष्ठं प्रत्नं प्रत्नवत्परितंसयध्यै । स नो वक्षदनिमानः सुवह्मेन्द्रो विश्वान्यति दुर्गहाणि ॥
6.22.e: Him will we fit for you with new devotion, the strongest Ancient One, in ancient manner.  So may that Indra, boundless, faithful Leader, conduct us o’er all places hard to traverse.

6.22.d: आ जनाय द्रुह्वणे पार्थिवानि दिव्यानि दीपयोऽन्तरिक्षा । तपा वृषन्विश्वतः शोचिषा तान्ब्रह्मद्विषे शोचय क्षामपश्च ॥
6.22.e: Thou for the people who oppress hast kindled the earthly firmament and that of heaven.  With heat, O Bull, on every side consume them: heat earth and flood for him who hates devotion.

6.22.d: भुवो जनस्य दिव्यस्य राजा पार्थिवस्य जगतस्त्वेषसंदृक् । धिष्व वज्रं दक्षिण इन्द्र हस्ते विश्वा अजुर्य दयसे वि मायाः ॥
6.22.e: Of all the Heavenly Folk, of earthly creatures thou art the King, O God of splendid aspect.  In thy right hand, O Indra, grasp die thunder: Eternal! thou destroyest all enchantments.

6.22.d: आ संयतमिन्द्र णः स्वस्तिं शत्रुतूर्याय बृहतीममृध्राम् । यया दासान्यार्याणि वृत्रा करो वज्रिन्त्सुतुका नाहुषाणि ॥
6.22.e: Give us confirmed prosperity, O Indra, vast and exhaustless for the foe's subduing.  Strengthen therewith the Ārya's hate and Dāsa's, and let the arms of Nahusas be mighty.

6.22.d: स नो नियुद्भिः पुरुहूत वेधो विश्ववाराभिरा गहि प्रयज्यो । न या अदेवो वरते न देव आभिर्याहि तूयमा मद्र्यद्रिक् ॥
6.22.e: Come with thy team which brings all blessings hither, Disposer, much-invoked, exceeding holy.  Thou whom no fiend, no God can stay or hinder, come swittly with these Steeds in my direction.

6.23.d: सुत इत्त्वं निमिश्ल इन्द्र सोमे स्तोमे ब्रह्मणि शस्यमान उक्थे । यद्वा युक्ताभ्यां मघवन्हरिभ्यां बिभ्रद्वज्रं बाह्वोरिन्द्र यासि ॥
6.23.e: THOU art attached to pressed-out Soma, Indra, at laud, at prayer, and when the hymn is chanted;  Or when with yoked Bays, Maghavan, thou comest, O Indra, bearing in thine arms the thunder.

6.23.d: यद्वा दिवि पार्ये सुष्विमिन्द्र वृत्रहत्येऽवसि शूरसातौ । यद्वा दक्षस्य बिभ्युषो अबिभ्यदरन्धयः शर्धत इन्द्र दस्यून् ॥
6.23.e: Or when on that decisive day thou holpest the presser of the juice at Vṛtra's slaughter;  Or when thou, while the strong one feared, undaunted, gavest to death, Indra, the daring Dasyus.

6.23.d: पाता सुतमिन्द्रो अस्तु सोमं प्रणेनीरुग्रो जरितारमूती । कर्ता वीराय सुष्वय उ लोकं दाता वसु स्तुवते कीरये चित् ॥
6.23.e: Let Indra drink the pressed-out Soma, Helper and mighty Guide of him who sings his praises.  He gives the hero room who pours oblations, and treasure even to the lowly singer.

6.23.d: गन्तेयान्ति सवना हरिभ्यां बभ्रिर्वज्रं पपिः सोमं ददिर्गाः । कर्ता वीरं नर्यं सर्ववीरं श्रोता हवं गृणतः स्तोमवाहाः ॥
6.23.e: E’en humble rites with his Bay steeds he visits: he wields the bolt, drinks Soma, gives us cattle.  He makes the valiant rich in store of heroes, accepts our praise and hears the singer's calling.

6.23.d: अस्मै वयं यद्वावान तद्विविष्म इन्द्राय यो नः प्रदिवो अपस्कः । सुते सोमे स्तुमसि शंसदुक्थेन्द्राय ब्रह्म वर्धनं यथासत् ॥
6.23.e: What he hath longed for we have brought to Indra, who from the days of old hath done us service.  While Soma flows we will sing hymn, and laud him, so that our prayer may streng. then Indra's vigour.

6.23.d: ब्रह्माणि हि चकृषे वर्धनानि तावत्त इन्द्र मतिभिर्विविष्मः । सुते सोमे सुतपाः शंतमानि राण्ड्या क्रियास्म वक्षणानि यज्ञैः ॥
6.23.e: Thou hast made prayer the means of thine exalting, therefore we wait on thee with hymns, O Indra.  May we, by the pressed Soma, Somadrinker! bring thee, with sacrifice, blissful sweet refreshment.

6.23.d: स नो बोधि पुरोळाशं रराणः पिबा तु सोमं गोऋजीकमिन्द्र । एदं बर्हिर्यजमानस्य सीदोरुं कृधि त्वायत उ लोकम् ॥
6.23.e: Mark well our sacrificial cake, delighted Indra, drink Soma and the milk commingled.  Here on the sacrificer's grass be seated: give ample room to thy devoted servant.

6.23.d: स मन्दस्वा ह्यनु जोषमुग्र प्र त्वा यज्ञास इमे अश्नुवन्तु । प्रेमे हवासः पुरुहूतमस्मे आ त्वेयं धीरवस इन्द्र यम्याः ॥
6.23.e: O Mighty One, be joyful as thou willest. Let these our sacrifices reach and find thee;  And may this hymn and these our invocations turn thee, whom many men invoke, to help us.

6.23.d: तं वः सखायः सं यथा सुतेषु सोमेभिरीं पृणता भोजमिन्द्रम् । कुवित्तस्मा असति नो भराय न सुष्विमिन्द्रोऽवसे मृधाति ॥
6.23.e: Friends, when thejuices flow, replenish duly your own, your bounteous Indra with the Soma.  Will it not aid him to support us? Indra. spares him who sheds the juice to win his favour.

6.23.d: एवेदिन्द्रः सुते अस्तावि सोमे भरद्वाजेषु क्षयदिन्मघोनः । असद्यथा जरित्र उत सूरिरिन्द्रो रायो विश्ववारस्य दाता ॥
6.23.e: While Soma flowed, thus Indra hath been lauded, Ruler of nobles, mid the Bharadvājas,  That Indra may become the singer's patron and give him wealth in every kind of treasure.

6.24.d: वृषा मद इन्द्रे श्लोक उक्था सचा सोमेषु सुतपा ऋजीषी । अर्चत्र्यो मघवा नृभ्य उक्थैर्द्युक्षो राजा गिरामक्षितोतिः ॥
6.24.e: STRONG rapturous joy, praise, glory are with Indra: impetuous God, he quaffs the juice of Soma:  That Maghavan whom men must laud with singing, Heaven-dweller, King of songs, whose help is lasting.

6.24.d: ततुरिर्वीरो नर्यो विचेताः श्रोता हवं गृणत उर्व्यूतिः । वसुः शंसो नरां कारुधाया वाजी स्तुतो विदथे दाति वाजम् ॥
6.24.e: He, Friend of man, most wise, victorious Hero, hears, with far-reaching aid, the singer call him.  Excellent, Praise of Men, the bard's Supporter, Strong, he gives strength, extolled in holy synod.

6.24.d: अक्षो न चक्र्योः शूर बृहन्प्र ते मह्ना रिरिचे रोदस्योः । वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यू३तयो रुरुहुरिन्द्र पूर्वीः ॥
6.24.e: The lofty axle of thy wheels, O Hero, is not surpassed by heaven and earth in greatness.  Like branches of a tree, Invoked of many manifold aids spring forth from thee, O Indra.

6.24.d: शचीवतस्ते पुरुशाक शाका गवामिव स्रुतयः संचरणीः । वत्सानां न तन्तयस्त इन्द्र दामन्वन्तो अदामानः सुदामन् ॥
6.24.e: Strong Lord, thine energies, endowed with vigour, are like the paths of kine converging homeward.  Like bonds of cord, Indra, that bind the younglings, no bonds are they, O thou of boundless bounty.

6.24.d: अन्यदद्य कर्वरमन्यदु श्वोऽसच्च सन्मुहुराचक्रिरिन्द्रः । मित्रो नो अत्र वरुणश्च पूषार्यो वशस्य पर्येतास्ति ॥
6.24.e: One act to-day, another act tomorrow oft Indra makes what is not yet existeni.  Here have we Mitra, Varuṇa, and Pūṣan to overcome the foeman's domination.

6.24.d: वि त्वदापो न पर्वतस्य पृष्ठादुक्थेभिरिन्द्रानयन्त यज्ञैः । तं त्वाभिः सुष्टुतिभिर्वाजयन्त आजिं न जग्मुर्गिर्वाहो अश्वाः ॥
6.24.e: By song and sacrifice men brought the waters from thee, as from a mountain's ridge, O Indra.  Urging thy might, with these fair lauds they seek thee, O theme of song, as horses rush tobattle.

6.24.d: न यं जरन्ति शरदो न मासा न द्याव इन्द्रमवकर्शयन्ति । वृद्धस्य चिद्वर्धतामस्य तनूः स्तोमेभिरुक्थैश्च शस्यमाना ॥
6.24.e: That Indra whom nor months nor autumn seasons wither with age, nor fleeting days enfeeble,—  Still may his body Wax, e’en now so mighty, glorified by the lauds and hymns that praise him.

6.24.d: न वीळवे नमते न स्थिराय न शर्धते दस्युजूताय स्तवान् । अज्रा इन्द्रस्य गिरयश्चिदृष्वा गम्भीरे चिद्भवति गाधमस्मै ॥
6.24.e: Extolled, he bends not to the strong, the steadfast, nor to the bold incited by the Dasyu.  High mountains are as level plains to Indra: even in the deep he finds firm ground to rest on.

6.24.d: गम्भीरेण न उरुणामत्रिन्प्रेषो यन्धि सुतपावन्वाजान् । स्था ऊ षु ऊर्ध्व ऊती अरिषण्यन्नक्तोर्व्युष्टौ परितक्म्यायाम् ॥
6.24.e: Impetuous Speeder through all depth and distance, give strengthening food, thou drinker of the juices.  Stand up erect to help us, unreluctant, what time the gloom of night brightens to morning.

6.24.d: सचस्व नायमवसे अभीक इतो वा तमिन्द्र पाहि रिषः । अमा चैनमरण्ये पाहि रिषो मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः ॥
6.24.e: Hasting to help, come hither and protect him, keep him from harm when he is here, O Indra.  At home, abroad, from injury preserve him. May brave sons gladden us through a hundred winters.

6.25.d: या त ऊतिरवमा या परमा या मध्यमेन्द्र शुष्मिन्नस्ति । ताभिरू षु वृत्रहत्येऽवीर्न एभिश्च वाजैर्महान्न उग्र ॥
6.25.e: WITH thine assistance, O thou Mighty Indra, be it the least, the midmost, or the highest,—  Great with those aids and by these powers support us, Strong God! in battle that subdues our foemen.

6.25.d: आभिः स्पृधो मिथतीररिषण्यन्नमित्रस्य व्यथया मन्युमिन्द्र । आभिर्विश्वा अभियुजो विषूचीरार्याय विशोऽव तारीर्दासीः ॥
6.25.e: With these discomfit hosts that fight against us, and check the opponent's wrath, thyself uninjured.  With these chase all our foes to every quarter: subdue the tribes of Dāsas to the Ārya.

6.25.d: इन्द्र जामय उत येऽजामयोऽर्वाचीनासो वनुषो युयुज्रे । त्वमेषां विथुरा शवांसि जहि वृष्ण्यानि कृणुही पराचः ॥
6.25.e: Those who array themselves as foes to smite us, O Indra, be they kin or be they strangers,—  Strike thou their manly strength that it be feeble, and drive in headlong flight our foemen backward.

6.25.d: शूरो वा शूरं वनते शरीरैस्तनूरुचा तरुषि यत्कृण्वैते । तोके वा गोषु तनये यदप्सु वि क्रन्दसी उर्वरासु ब्रवैते ॥
6.25.e: With strength of limb the hero slays the hero, when bright in arms they range them for the combat.  When two opposing hosts contend in battle for seed and offspring, waters, kine, or corn-lands.

6.25.d: नहि त्वा शूरो न तुरो न धृष्णुर्न त्वा योधो मन्यमानो युयोध । इन्द्र नकिष्ट्वा प्रत्यस्त्येषां विश्वा जातान्यभ्यसि तानि ॥
6.25.e: Yet no strong man hath conquered thee, no hero, no brave, no warrior trusting in his valour.  Not one of these is match for thee, O Indra. Thou far surpassest all these living creatures.

6.25.d: स पत्यत उभयोर्नृम्णमयोर्यदी वेधसः समिथे हवन्ते । वृत्रे वा महो नृवति क्षये वा व्यचस्वन्ता यदि वितन्तसैते ॥
6.25.e: He is the Lord of both these armies' valour when the commanders call them to the conflict:  When with their ranks expanded they are fighting with a great foe or for a home with heroes.

6.25.d: अध स्मा ते चर्षणयो यदेजानिन्द्र त्रातोत भवा वरूता । अस्माकासो ये नृतमासो अर्य इन्द्र सूरयो दधिरे पुरो नः ॥
6.25.e: And when the people stir themselves for battle, be thou their saviour, Indra, and protector,  And theirs, thy manliest of our friends, the pious, the chiefs who have installed us priests, O Indra.

6.25.d: अनु ते दायि मह इन्द्रियाय सत्रा ते विश्वमनु वृत्रहत्ये । अनु क्षत्रमनु सहो यजत्रेन्द्र देवेभिरनु ते नृषह्ये ॥
6.25.e: To thee for high dominion hath been for evermore, for slaughtering the Vṛtras,  All lordly power and might, O Holy Indra, given by Gods for victory in battle.

6.25.d: एवा नः स्पृधः समजा समत्स्विन्द्र रारन्धि मिथतीरदेवीः । विद्याम वस्तोरवसा गृणन्तो भरद्वाजा उत त इन्द्र नूनम् ॥
6.25.e: So urge our hosts together in the combats: yield up the godless bands that fight against us.  Singing, at morn may we find thee with favour, yea, Indra, and e’en now, we Bharadvājas.

6.26.d: श्रुधी न इन्द्र ह्वयामसि त्वा महो वाजस्य सातौ वावृषाणाः । सं यद्विशोऽयन्त शूरसाता उग्रं नोऽवः पार्ये अहन्दाः ॥
6.26.e: O INDRA, hear us. Raining down the Soma, we call on thee to win us mighty valour.  Give us strong succour on the day of trial, when the tribes gather on the field of battle.

6.26.d: त्वां वाजी हवते वाजिनेयो महो वाजस्य गध्यस्य सातौ । त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं तरुत्रं त्वां चष्टे मुष्टिहा गोषु युध्यन् ॥
6.26.e: The warrior, son of warrior sire, invokes thee, to gain great strength that may be won as booty:  To thee, the brave man's Lord, the fiends' subduer, he looks when fighting hand to hand for cattle.

6.26.d: त्वं कविं चोदयोऽर्कसातौ त्वं कुत्साय शुष्णं दाशुषे वर्क् । त्वं शिरो अमर्मणः पराहन्नतिथिग्वाय शंस्यं करिष्यन् ॥
6.26.e: Thou didst impel the sage to win the daylight, didst ruin Śuṣṇa for the pious Kutsa.  The invulnerable demon's head thou clavest when thou wouldst win the praise of Atithigva.

6.26.d: त्वं रथं प्र भरो योधमृष्वमावो युध्यन्तं वृषभं दशद्युम् । त्वं तुग्रं वेतसवे सचाहन्त्वं तुजिं गृणन्तमिन्द्र तूतोः ॥
6.26.e: The lofty battle-car thou broughtest forward; thou holpest Dasadyu the strong when fighting.  Along with Vetasu thou slewest Tugra, and madest Tuji strong, who praised thee, Indra.

6.26.d: त्वं तदुक्थमिन्द्र बर्हणा कः प्र यच्छता सहस्रा शूर दर्षि । अव गिरेर्दासं शम्बरं हन्प्रावो दिवोदासं चित्राभिरूती ॥
6.26.e: Thou madest good the laud, what time thou rentest a hundred thousand fighting foes, O Hero,  Slewest the Dāsa Śambara of the mountain, and with strange aids didst succour Divodāsa.

6.26.d: त्वं श्रद्धाभिर्मन्दसानः सोमैर्दभीतये चुमुरिमिन्द्र सिष्वप् । त्वं रजिं पिठीनसे दशस्यन्त्शष्टिं सहस्रा शच्या सचाहन् ॥
6.26.e: Made glad with Soma-draughts and faith, thou sentest Cumuri to his sleep, to please Dabhīti.  Thou, kindly giving Raji to Pithinas, slewest with might, at once, the sixty thousand.

6.26.d: अहं चन तत्सूरिभिरानश्यां तव ज्याय इन्द्र सुम्नमोजः । त्वया यत्स्तवन्ते सधवीर वीरास्त्रिवरूथेन नहुषा शविष्ठ ॥
6.26.e: May I too, with the liberal chiefs, O Indra, acquire thy blin supreme and domination,  When, Mightiest! Hero-girt! Nahuṣa heroes boast them in thee, the triply-strong Defender.

6.26.d: वयं ते अस्यामिन्द्र द्युम्नहूतौ सखायः स्याम महिन प्रेष्ठाः । प्रातर्दनिः क्षत्रश्रीरस्तु श्रेष्ठो घने वृत्राणां सनये धनानाम् ॥
6.26.e: So may we he thy friends, thy best beloved, O Indra, at this holy invocation.  Best be Pratardani, illustrious ruler, in slaying foemen and in gaining riches.

6.27.d: किमस्य मदे किम्वस्य पीताविन्द्रः किमस्य सख्ये चकार । रणा वा ये निषदि किं ते अस्य पुरा विविद्रे किमु नूतनासः ॥
6.27.e: WHAT deed hath Indra done in the wild transport, in quaffing or in friendship with, the Soma?  What joys have men of ancient times or recent obtained within the chamber of libation?

6.27.d: सदस्य मदे सद्वस्य पीताविन्द्रः सदस्य सख्ये चकार । रणा वा ये निषदि सत्ते अस्य पुरा विविद्रे सदु नूतनासः ॥
6.27.e: In its wild joy Indra hath proved him faithful, faithful in quaffing, faithful in its friendship.  His truth is the delight that in this chamber the men of old and recent times have tasted.

6.27.d: नहि नु ते महिमनः समस्य न मघवन्मघवत्त्वस्य विद्म । न राधसोराधसो नूतनस्येन्द्र नकिर्ददृश इन्द्रियं ते ॥
6.27.e: All thy vast power, O Maghavan, we know not, know not the riches of thy full abundance.  No one hath seen that might of thine, productive of bounty every day renewed, O Indra.

6.27.d: एतत्त्यत्त इन्द्रियमचेति येनावधीर्वरशिखस्य शेषः । वज्रस्य यत्ते निहतस्य शुष्मात्स्वनाच्चिदिन्द्र परमो ददार ॥
6.27.e: This one great power of thine our eyes have witnessed, wherewith thou slewest Varasikha's children,  When by the force of thy descending thunder, at the mere solund, their boldest was demolished.

6.27.d: वधीदिन्द्रो वरशिखस्य शेषोऽभ्यावर्तिने चायमानाय शिक्षन् । वृचीवतो यद्धरियूपीयायां हन्पूर्वे अर्धे भियसापरो दर्त् ॥
6.27.e: In aid of Abhyavartin Cayamana, Indra destroyed the seed of Varasikha.  At Hariyupiya he smote the vanguard of the Vrcivans, and the rear fled frighted.

6.27.d: त्रिंशच्छतं वर्मिण इन्द्र साकं यव्यावत्यां पुरुहूत श्रवस्या । वृचीवन्तः शरवे पत्यमानाः पात्रा भिन्दाना न्यर्थान्यायन् ॥
6.27.e: Three thousand, mailed, in quest of fame, together, on the Yavyavati, O much-sought Indra,  Vrcivan's sons, falling before the arrow, like bursting vessels went to their destruction.

6.27.d: यस्य गावावरुषा सूयवस्यू अन्तरू षु चरतो रेरिहाणा । स सृञ्जयाय तुर्वशं परादाद्वृचीवतो दैववाताय शिक्षन् ॥
6.27.e: He, whose two red Steers, seeking goodly pasture, plying their tongues move on 'twixt earth and heaven,  Gave Turvaśa to Sṛñjaya, and, to aid him, gave the Vrcivans up to Daivavata.

6.27.d: द्वयाँ अग्ने रथिनो विंशतिं गा वधूमतो मघवा मह्यं सम्राट् । अभ्यावर्ती चायमानो ददाति दूणाशेयं दक्षिणा पार्थवानाम् ॥
6.27.e: Two wagon-teams, with damsels, twenty oxen, O Agni, Abhydvartin Cayamdna,  The liberal Sovran, giveth me. This guerdon of Prthu's seed is hard to win from others.

6.28.d: आ गावो अग्मन्नुत भद्रमक्रन्त्सीदन्तु गोष्ठे रणयन्त्वस्मे । प्रजावतीः पुरुरूपा इह स्युरिन्द्राय पूर्वीरुषसो दुहानाः ॥
6.28.e: THE Kine have come and brought good fortune: let them rest in the cow-pen and be happy near us.  Here let them stay prolific, many-coloured, and yield through many morns their milk for Indra.

6.28.d: इन्द्रो यज्वने पृणते च शिक्षत्युपेद्ददाति न स्वं मुषायति । भूयोभूयो रयिमिदस्य वर्धयन्नभिन्ने खिल्ये नि दधाति देवयुम् ॥
6.28.e: Indra aids him who offers sacrifice and gifts: he takes not what is his, and gives him more thereto.  Increasing ever more and ever more his wealth, he makes the pious dwell within unbroken bounds.

6.28.d: न ता नशन्ति न दभाति तस्करो नासामामित्रो व्यथिरा दधर्षति । देवाँश्च याभिर्यजते ददाति च ज्योगित्ताभिः सचते गोपतिः सह ॥
6.28.e: These are ne’er lost, no robber ever injures them: no evil-minded foe attempts to harass them.  The master of the Kine lives many a year with these, the Cows whereby he pours his gifts and serves the Gods.

6.28.d: न ता अर्वा रेणुककाटो अश्नुते न संस्कृतत्रमुप यन्ति ता अभि । उरुगायमभयं तस्य ता अनु गावो मर्तस्य वि चरन्ति यज्वनः ॥
6.28.e: The charger with his dusty brow o’ertakes them not, and never to the shambles do they take their way.  These Cows, the cattle of the pious worshipper, roam over widespread pasture where no danger is.

6.28.d: गावो भगो गाव इन्द्रो मे अच्छान्गावः सोमस्य प्रथमस्य भक्षः । इमा या गावः स जनास इन्द्र इच्छामीद्धृदा मनसा चिदिन्द्रम् ॥
6.28.e: To me the Cows seem Bhaga, they seem Indra, they seem a portion of the first-poured Soma.  These present Cows, they, O ye Indra. I long for Indra with my heart and spirit.

6.28.d: यूयं गावो मेदयथा कृशं चिदश्रीरं चित्कृणुथा सुप्रतीकम् । भद्रं गृहं कृणुथ भद्रवाचो बृहद्वो वय उच्यते सभासु ॥
6.28.e: O Cows, ye fatten e’en the worn and wasted, and make the unlovely beautiful tolook on.  Prosper my house, ye with auspicious voices. Your power is glorified in our assemblies.

6.28.d: प्रजावतीः सूयवसं रिशन्तीः शुद्धा अपः सुप्रपाणे पिबन्तीः । मा वः स्तेन ईशत माघशंसः परि वो हेती रुद्रस्य वृज्याः ॥
6.28.e: Crop goodly pasturage and be prolific drink pure sweet water at good drinking places.  Never be thief or sinful man your matter, and may the dart of Rudra still avoid you.

6.28.d: उपेदमुपपर्चनमासु गोषूप पृच्यताम् । उप ऋषभस्य रेतस्युपेन्द्र तव वीर्ये ॥
6.28.e: Now let this close admixture be close intermigled with these Cows,  Mixt with the Steer's prolific flow, and, Indra, with thy hero might.

6.29.d: इन्द्रं वो नरः सख्याय सेपुर्महो यन्तः सुमतये चकानाः । महो हि दाता वज्रहस्तो अस्ति महामु रण्वमवसे यजध्वम् ॥
6.29.e: YOUR men have followed Indra for his friendship, and for his loving-kindness glorified him.  For he bestows great wealth, the Thunder-wielder: worship him, Great and Kind, to win his favour.

6.29.d: आ यस्मिन्हस्ते नर्या मिमिक्षुरा रथे हिरण्यये रथेष्ठाः । आ रश्मयो गभस्त्योः स्थूरयोराध्वन्नश्वासो वृषणो युजानाः ॥
6.29.e: Him to whose hand, men closely cling, and drivers stand on his golden chariot firmly stationed.  With his firm arms he holds the reins; his Horses, the Stallions, are yoked ready for the journey.

6.29.d: श्रिये ते पादा दुव आ मिमिक्षुर्धृष्णुर्वज्री शवसा दक्षिणावान् । वसानो अत्कं सुरभिं दृशे कं स्व१र्ण नृतविषिरो बभूथ ॥
6.29.e: Thy devotees embrace thy feet for glory. Bold, thunder-armed, rich, through thy strength, in guerdon,  Robed in a garment fair as heaven to look on, thou hast displayed thee like an active dancer.

6.29.d: स सोम आमिश्लतमः सुतो भूद्यस्मिन्पक्तिः पच्यते सन्ति धानाः । इन्द्रं नरः स्तुवन्तो ब्रह्मकारा उक्था शंसन्तो देववाततमाः ॥
6.29.e: That Soma when effused hath best consistence, for which the food is dressed and grain is mingled;  By which the men who pray, extolling Indra chief favourites of Gods, recite their praises.

6.29.d: न ते अन्तः शवसो धाय्यस्य वि तु बाबधे रोदसी महित्वा । आ ता सूरिः पृणति तूतुजानो यूथेवाप्सु समीजमान ऊती ॥
6.29.e: No limit of thy might hath been appointed, which by its greatness sundered earth and heaven.  These the Prince filleth full with strong endeavour, driving, as ’twere, with help his flocks to waters.

6.29.d: एवेदिन्द्रः सुहव ऋष्वो अस्तूती अनूती हिरिशिप्रः सत्वा । एवा हि जातो असमात्योजाः पुरू च वृत्रा हनति नि दस्यून् ॥
6.29.e: So be the lofty Indra prompt to listen, Helper unaided, golden-visored Hero.  Yea, so may he, shown forth in might unequalled, smite down the many Vṛtras and the Dasyus.

6.30.d: भूय इद्वावृधे वीर्यायँ एको अजुर्यो दयते वसूनि । प्र रिरिचे दिव इन्द्रः पृथिव्या अर्धमिदस्य प्रति रोदसी उभे ॥
6.30.e: INDRA hath waxed yet more for hero prowess, alone, Eternal, he bestoweth treasures.  Indra transcendeth both the worlds in greatness: one half of him equalleth earth and heaven.

6.30.d: अधा मन्ये बृहदसुर्यमस्य यानि दाधार नकिरा मिनाति । दिवेदिवे सूर्यो दर्शतो भूद्वि सद्मान्युर्विया सुक्रतुर्धात् ॥
6.30.e: Yea, mighty I esteem his Godlike nature: none hindereth what he hath once determined.  Near and afar he spread and set the regions, and every day the Sun became apparent.

6.30.d: अद्या चिन्नू चित्तदपो नदीनां यदाभ्यो अरदो गातुमिन्द्र । नि पर्वता अद्मसदो न सेदुस्त्वया दृळ्हानि सुक्रतो रजांसि ॥
6.30.e: E’en now endures thine exploit of the Rivers, when, Indra, for their floods thou clavest passage.  Like men who sit at meat the mountains settled: by thee, Most Wise! the regions were made steadfast.

6.30.d: सत्यमित्तन्न त्वावाँ अन्यो अस्तीन्द्र देवो न मर्त्यो ज्यायान् । अहन्नहिं परिशयानमर्णोऽवासृजो अपो अच्छा समुद्रम् ॥
6.30.e: This is the truth, none else is like thee, Indra, no God superior to thee, no mortal.  Thou slewest Ahi who besieged the waters, and lettest loose the streams to hurry seaward.

6.30.d: त्वमपो वि दुरो विषूचीरिन्द्र दृळ्हमरुजः पर्वतस्य । राजाभवो जगतश्चर्षणीनां साकं सूर्यं जनयन्द्यामुषासम् ॥
6.30.e: Indra, thou breakest up the floods and portals on all sides, and the firmness of the mountain.  Thou art the King of men, of all that liveth, engendering at once Sun, Heaven, and Morning.

6.31.d: अभूरेको रयिपते रयीणामा हस्तयोरधिथा इन्द्र कृष्टीः । वि तोके अप्सु तनये च सूरेऽवोचन्त चर्षणयो विवाचः ॥
6.31.e: SOLE Lord of wealth art thou, O Lord of riches: thou in thine hands hast held the people, Indra!  Men have invoked thee with contending voices for seed and waters, progeny and sunlight.

6.31.d: त्वद्भियेन्द्र पार्थिवानि विश्वाच्युता चिच्च्यावयन्ते रजांसि । द्यावाक्षामा पर्वतासो वनानि विश्वं दृळ्हं भयते अज्मन्ना ते ॥
6.31.e: Through fear of thee, O Indra, all the regions of earth, though naught may move them, shake and tremble.  All that is firm is frightened at thy coming, -the earth, the heaven, the mountain, and the forest.

6.31.d: त्वं कुत्सेनाभि शुष्णमिन्द्राशुषं युध्य कुयवं गविष्टौ । दश प्रपित्वे अध सूर्यस्य मुषायश्चक्रमविवे रपांसि ॥
6.31.e: With Kutsa, Indra! thou didst conquer Śuṣṇa, voracious, bane of crops, in fight for cattle.  In the close fray thou rentest him: thou stolest the Sun's wheel and didst drive away misfortunes.

6.31.d: त्वं शतान्यव शम्बरस्य पुरो जघन्थाप्रतीनि दस्योः । अशिक्षो यत्र शच्या शचीवो दिवोदासाय सुन्वते सुतक्रे भरद्वाजाय गृणते वसूनि ॥
6.31.e: Thou smotest to the ground the hundred castles, impregnable, of Śambara the Dasyu,  When, Strong, with might thou holpest Divodāsa who poured libations out, O Soma-buyer, and madest Bharadvāja rich who praised thee.

6.31.d: स सत्यसत्वन्महते रणाय रथमा तिष्ठ तुविनृम्ण भीमम् । याहि प्रपथिन्नवसोप मद्रिक्प्र च श्रुत श्रावय चर्षणिभ्यः ॥
6.31.e: As such, true Hero, for great joy of battle mount thy terrific car, O Brave and Manly.  Come with thine help to me, thou distant Roamer, and, glorious God, spread among men my glory.

6.32.d: अपूर्व्या पुरुतमान्यस्मै महे वीराय तवसे तुराय । विरप्शिने वज्रिणे शंतमानि वचांस्यासा स्थविराय तक्षम् ॥
6.32.e: I WITH my lips have fashioned for this Hero words never matched, most plentiful and auspicious,  For him the Ancient, Great, Strong, Energetic, the very mighty Wielder of the Thunder.

6.32.d: स मातरा सूर्येणा कवीनामवासयद्रुजदद्रिं गृणानः । स्वाधीभिर्ऋक्वभिर्वावशान उदुस्रियाणामसृजन्निदानम् ॥
6.32.e: Amid the sages, with the Sun he brightened the Parents: glorified, he burst the mountain;  And, roaring with the holy-thoughted singers, he loosed the bond that held the beams of Morning.

6.32.d: स वह्निभिर्ऋक्वभिर्गोषु शश्वन्मितज्ञुभिः पुरुकृत्वा जिगाय । पुरः पुरोहा सखिभिः सखीयन्दृळ्हा रुरोज कविभिः कविः सन् ॥
6.32.e: Famed for great deeds, with priests who kneel and laud him, he still hath conquered in the frays for cattle,  And broken down the forts, the Fort-destroyer, a Friend with friends, a Sage among the sages.

6.32.d: स नीव्याभिर्जरितारमच्छा महो वाजेभिर्महद्भिश्च शुष्मैः । पुरुवीराभिर्वृषभ क्षितीनामा गिर्वणः सुविताय प्र याहि ॥
6.32.e: Come with thy girthed mares, with abundant vigour and plenteous strength to him who sings thy praises.  Come hither, borne by mares with many heroes, Lover of song! Steer! for the people's welfare.

6.32.d: स सर्गेण शवसा तक्तो अत्यैरप इन्द्रो दक्षिणतस्तुराषाट् । इत्था सृजाना अनपावृदर्थं दिवेदिवे विविषुरप्रमृष्यम् ॥
6.32.e: Indra with rush and might, sped by his Coursers, hath swiftly won the waters from the southward.  Thus set at liberty the rivers daily flow to their goal, incessant and exhaustless.

6.33.d: य ओजिष्ठ इन्द्र तं सु नो दा मदो वृषन्त्स्वभिष्टिर्दास्वान् । सौवश्व्यं यो वनवत्स्वश्वो वृत्रा समत्सु सासहदमित्रान् ॥
6.33.e: GIVE us the rapture that is mightiest, Indra, prompt to bestow and swift to aid, O Hero,  That wins with brave steeds where brave steeds encounter, and quells the Vṛtras and the foes in battle.

6.33.d: त्वां ही३न्द्रावसे विवाचो हवन्ते चर्षणयः शूरसातौ । त्वं विप्रेभिर्वि पणीँरशायस्त्वोत इत्सनिता वाजमर्वा ॥
6.33.e: For with loud voice the tribes invoke thee, Indra, to aid them in the battlefield of heroes.  Thou, with the singers, hast pierced through the Paṇis: the charger whom thou aidest wins the booty.

6.33.d: त्वं ताँ इन्द्रोभयाँ अमित्रान्दासा वृत्राण्यार्या च शूर । वधीर्वनेव सुधितेभिरत्कैरा पृत्सु दर्षि नृणां नृतम ॥
6.33.e: Both races, Indra, of opposing foemen, O Hero, both the Ārya and the Dāsa,  Hast thou struck down like woods with well-shot lightnings: thou rentest them in fight, most manly Chieftain!

6.33.d: स त्वं न इन्द्राकवाभिरूती सखा विश्वायुरविता वृधे भूः । स्वर्षाता यद्ध्वयामसि त्वा युध्यन्तो नेमधिता पृत्सु शूर ॥
6.33.e: Indra, befriend us with no scanty succour, prosper and aid us, Loved of all that liveth,  When, fighting for the sunlight, we invoke thee, O Hero, in the fray, in war's division.

6.33.d: नूनं न इन्द्रापराय च स्या भवा मृळीक उत नो अभिष्टौ । इत्था गृणन्तो महिनस्य शर्मन्दिवि ष्याम पार्ये गोषतमाः ॥
6.33.e: Be ours, O Indra, now and for the future, be graciously inclined and near to help us.  Thus may we, singing, sheltered by the Mighty, win many cattle on the day of trial.

6.34.d: सं च त्वे जग्मुर्गिर इन्द्र पूर्वीर्वि च त्वद्यन्ति विभ्वो मनीषाः । पुरा नूनं च स्तुतय ऋषीणां पस्पृध्र इन्द्रे अध्युक्थार्का ॥
6.34.e: FULL Many songs have met in thee, O Indra, and many a noble thought from thee proceedeth.  Now and of old the eulogies of sages, their holy hymns and lauds, have yearned for Indra.

6.34.d: पुरुहूतो यः पुरुगूर्त ऋभ्वाँ एकः पुरुप्रशस्तो अस्ति यज्ञैः । रथो न महे शवसे युजानो३ऽस्माभिरिन्द्रो अनुमाद्यो भूत् ॥
6.34.e: He, praised of many, bold, invoked of many, alone is glorified at sacrifices.  Like a car harnessed for some great achievement, Indra must be the cause of our rejoicing.

6.34.d: न यं हिंसन्ति धीतयो न वाणीरिन्द्रं नक्षन्तीदभि वर्धयन्तीः । यदि स्तोतारः शतं यत्सहस्रं गृणन्ति गिर्वणसं शं तदस्मै ॥
6.34.e: They make their way to Indra and exalt him, bim whom no prayers and no laudations trouble;  For when a hundred or a thousand singers. laud him who loves the song their praise delights him.

6.34.d: अस्मा एतद्दिव्य१र्चेव मासा मिमिक्ष इन्द्रे न्ययामि सोमः । जनं न धन्वन्नभि सं यदापः सत्रा वावृधुर्हवनानि यज्ञैः ॥
6.34.e: As brightness mingles with the Moon in heaven, the offered Soma yearns to mix with Indra.  Like water brought to men in desert places, our gifts at sacrifice have still refreshed him.

6.34.d: अस्मा एतन्मह्याङ्गूषमस्मा इन्द्राय स्तोत्रं मतिभिरवाचि । असद्यथा महति वृत्रतूर्य इन्द्रो विश्वायुरविता वृधश्च ॥
6.34.e: To him this mighty eulogy, to Indra hath this our laud been uttered by the poets,  That in the great encounter with the foemen, Loved of all life, Indra may guard and help us.

6.35.d: कदा भुवन्रथक्षयाणि ब्रह्म कदा स्तोत्रे सहस्रपोष्यं दाः । कदा स्तोमं वासयोऽस्य राया कदा धियः करसि वाजरत्नाः ॥
6.35.e: WHEN shall our prayers rest in thy car beside thee? When dost thou give the singer food for thousands?  When wilt thou clothe this poet's laud with plenty, and when wilt thou enrich our hymns with booty?

6.35.d: कर्हि स्वित्तदिन्द्र यन्नृभिर्नॄन्वीरैर्वीरान्नीळयासे जयाजीन् । त्रिधातु गा अधि जयासि गोष्विन्द्र द्युम्नं स्वर्वद्धेह्यस्मे ॥
6.35.e: When wilt thou gatber men with men, O Indra, heroes with heroes, and prevail in combat?  Thou shalt win triply kine in frays for cattle, so, Indra, give thou us celestial glory.

6.35.d: कर्हि स्वित्तदिन्द्र यज्जरित्रे विश्वप्सु ब्रह्म कृणवः शविष्ठ । कदा धियो न नियुतो युवासे कदा गोमघा हवनानि गच्छाः ॥
6.35.e: Yea, when wilt thou, O Indra, thou Most Mighty, make the prayer all-sustaining for the singer?  When wilt thou yoke, as we yoke songs, thy Horses, and come to offerings that bring wealth in cattle?

6.35.d: स गोमघा जरित्रे अश्वश्चन्द्रा वाजश्रवसो अधि धेहि पृक्षः । पीपिहीषः सुदुघामिन्द्र धेनुं भरद्वाजेषु सुरुचो रुरुच्याः ॥
6.35.e: Grant to the Singer food with store of cattle, splendid with horses and the fame of riches.  Send food to swell the milch-cow good at milking: bright be its shine among the Bharadvājas.

6.35.d: तमा नूनं वृजनमन्यथा चिच्छूरो यच्छक्र वि दुरो गृणीषे । मा निररं शुक्रदुघस्य धेनोराङ्गिरसान्ब्रह्मणा विप्र जिन्व ॥
6.35.e: Lead otherwise this present foeman, Śakra! Hence art thou praised as Hero, foe destroyer  Him who gives pure gifts may I praise unceasing. Sage, quicken the Aṅgirases by devotion.

6.36.d: सत्रा मदासस्तव विश्वजन्याः सत्रा रायोऽध ये पार्थिवासः । सत्रा वाजानामभवो विभक्ता यद्देवेषु धारयथा असुर्यम् ॥
6.36.e: THY raptures ever were for all men's profit: so evermore have been thine earthly riches.  Thou still hast been the dealer-forth of vigour, since among Gods thou hast had power and Godhead.

6.36.d: अनु प्र येजे जन ओजो अस्य सत्रा दधिरे अनु वीर्याय । स्यूमगृभे दुधयेऽर्वते च क्रतुं वृञ्जन्त्यपि वृत्रहत्ये ॥
6.36.e: Men have obtained his strength by sacrificing, and ever urged him, on to hero valour.  For the rein-seizing, the impetuous Charger they furnished power even for Vṛtra's slaughter.

6.36.d: तं सध्रीचीरूतयो वृष्ण्यानि पौंस्यानि नियुतः सश्चुरिन्द्रम् । समुद्रं न सिन्धव उक्थशुष्मा उरुव्यचसं गिर आ विशन्ति ॥
6.36.e: Associate with him, as teams of horses, help, manly might, and vigour follow Indra.  As rivers reach the sea, so, strong with praises, our holy songs reach him the Comprehensive.

6.36.d: स रायस्खामुप सृजा गृणानः पुरुश्चन्द्रस्य त्वमिन्द्र वस्वः । पतिर्बभूथासमो जनानामेको विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा ॥
6.36.e: Lauded by us, let flow the spring, O Indra, of excellent and brightly-shining riches.  For thou art Lord of men, without an equal: of all the world thou art the only Sovran.

6.36.d: स तु श्रुधि श्रुत्या यो दुवोयुर्द्यौर्न भूमाभि रायो अर्यः । असो यथा नः शवसा चकानो युगेयुगे वयसा चेकितानः ॥
6.36.e: Hear what thou mayst hear, thou who, fain for worship, as heaven girds earth, guardest thy servant's treasure;  Tlat thou mayst be our own, joying in power, famed through thy might in every generation.

6.37.d: अर्वाग्रथं विश्ववारं त उग्रेन्द्र युक्तासो हरयो वहन्तु । कीरिश्चिद्धि त्वा हवते स्वर्वानृधीमहि सधमादस्ते अद्य ॥
6.37.e: LET thy Bay Horses, yoked, O mighty Indra, bring thy car hither fraught with every blessing.  For thee, the Heavenly, e’en the poor invoketh: may we this day, thy feast-companions, prosper.

6.37.d: प्रो द्रोणे हरयः कर्माग्मन्पुनानास ऋज्यन्तो अभूवन् । इन्द्रो नो अस्य पूर्व्यः पपीयाद्द्युक्षो मदस्य सोम्यस्य राजा ॥
6.37.e: Forth to the vat the brown drops flow for service, and purified proceed directly forward.  May Indra drink of this, our guest aforetime, Celestial King of the strong draught of Soma.

6.37.d: आसस्राणासः शवसानमच्छेन्द्रं सुचक्रे रथ्यासो अश्वाः । अभि श्रव ऋज्यन्तो वहेयुर्नू चिन्नु वायोरमृतं वि दस्येत् ॥
6.37.e: Bringing us hitherward all-potent Indra on well-wheeled chariot, may the Steeds who bear him  Convey him on the road direct to glory, and ne’er may Vāyu's Amṛta cease and fail him.

6.37.d: वरिष्ठो अस्य दक्षिणामियर्तीन्द्रो मघोनां तुविकूर्मितमः । यया वज्रिवः परियास्यंहो मघा च धृष्णो दयसे वि सूरीन् ॥
6.37.e: Supreme, he stirs this man to give the guerdon,—Indra, most efficacious of the princes,—  Wherewith, O Thunderer, thou removest sorrow, and, Bold One! partest wealth among the nobles.

6.37.d: इन्द्रो वाजस्य स्थविरस्य दातेन्द्रो गीर्भिर्वर्धतां वृद्धमहाः । इन्द्रो वृत्रं हनिष्ठो अस्तु सत्वा ता सूरिः पृणति तूतुजानः ॥
6.37.e: Indra is hewho gives enduring vigour: may our songs magnify the God Most Mighty.  Best Vṛtra-slayer be the Hero Indra these things he gives as Prince, with strong endeavour.

6.38.d: अपादित उदु नश्चित्रतमो महीं भर्षद्द्युमतीमिन्द्रहूतिम् । पन्यसीं धीतिं दैव्यस्य यामञ्जनस्य रातिं वनते सुदानुः ॥
6.38.e: HE hath drunk hence, Most Marvellous, and carried away our great and splendid call on Indra.  The Bounteous, when we serve the Gods, accepteth song yet more famous and the gifts we bring him.

6.38.d: दूराच्चिदा वसतो अस्य कर्णा घोषादिन्द्रस्य तन्यति ब्रुवाणः । एयमेनं देवहूतिर्ववृत्यान्मद्र्य१गिन्द्रमियमृच्यमाना ॥
6.38.e: The speaker filleth with a cry to Indra his ears who cometh nigh e’en from a distance.  May this my call bring Indra to my presence, this call to Gods composed in sacred verses.

6.38.d: तं वो धिया परमया पुराजामजरमिन्द्रमभ्यनूष्यर्कैः । ब्रह्मा च गिरो दधिरे समस्मिन्महाँश्च स्तोमो अधि वर्धदिन्द्रे ॥
6.38.e: Him have I sung with my best song and praises, Indra of ancient birth and Everlasting.  For prayer and songs in him are concentrated: let laud wax mighty when addressed to Indra:

6.38.d: वर्धाद्यं यज्ञ उत सोम इन्द्रं वर्धाद्ब्रह्म गिर उक्था च मन्म । वर्धाहैनमुषसो यामन्नक्तोर्वर्धान्मासाः शरदो द्याव इन्द्रम् ॥
6.38.e: Indra, whom sacrifice shall strengthen, Soma, and song and hymn, and praises and devotion,  Whom Dawns shall strengthen when the night departeth, Indra whom days shall strengthen, months, and autumns.

6.38.d: एवा जज्ञानं सहसे असामि वावृधानं राधसे च श्रुताय । महामुग्रमवसे विप्र नूनमा विवासेम वृत्रतूर्येषु ॥
6.38.e: Him, born for conquering might in full perfection, and waxen strongfor bounty and for glory,  Great, Powerful, will we to-day, O singer, invite to aid. us and to quell our foemen.

6.39.d: मन्द्रस्य कवेर्दिव्यस्य वह्नेर्विप्रमन्मनो वचनस्य मध्वः । अपा नस्तस्य सचनस्य देवेषो युवस्व गृणते गोअग्राः ॥
6.39.e: OF this our charming, our celestial Soma, eloquent, wise, Priest, with inspired devotion,  Of this thy close attendant, hast thou drunken. God, send the singer food with milk to grace it.

6.39.d: अयमुशानः पर्यद्रिमुस्रा ऋतधीतिभिर्ऋतयुग्युजानः । रुजदरुग्णं वि वलस्य सानुं पणीँर्वचोभिरभि योधदिन्द्रः ॥
6.39.e: Craving the kine, rushing against the mountain led on by Law, with holyminded comrades,  He broke the never-broken ridge of Vala. With words of might Indra subdued the Paṇis.

6.39.d: अयं द्योतयदद्युतो व्य१क्तून्दोषा वस्तोः शरद इन्दुरिन्द्र । इमं केतुमदधुर्नू चिदह्नां शुचिजन्मन उषसश्चकार ॥
6.39.e: This Indu lighted darksome nights, O Indra, throughout the years, at morning and at evening.  Him have they stablished as the days' bright ensign. He made the Mornings to be born in splendour.

6.39.d: अयं रोचयदरुचो रुचानो३ऽयं वासयद्व्यृ१तेन पूर्वीः । अयमीयत ऋतयुग्भिरश्वैः स्वर्विदा नाभिना चर्षणिप्राः ॥
6.39.e: He shone and caused to shme the worlds that shone not. By Law he lighted up the host of Mornings.  He moves with Steeds yoked by eternal Order, contenting men with nave that finds the sunlight.

6.39.d: नू गृणानो गृणते प्रत्न राजन्निषः पिन्व वसुदेयाय पूर्वीः । अप ओषधीरविषा वनानि गा अर्वतो नॄनृचसे रिरीहि ॥
6.39.e: Now, praised, O Ancient King! fill thou the singer with plenteous food that he may deal forth treasures.  Give waters, herbs that have no poison, forests, and kine, and steeds, and men, to him who lauds thee.

6.40.d: इन्द्र पिब तुभ्यं सुतो मदायाव स्य हरी वि मुचा सखाया । उत प्र गाय गण आ निषद्याथा यज्ञाय गृणते वयो धाः ॥
6.40.e: DRINK, Indra; juice is shed to make thee joyful: loose thy Bay Steeds and give thy friends their freedom.  Begin the song, seated in our assembly. Give strength for sacrifice to him who singeth.

6.40.d: अस्य पिब यस्य जज्ञान इन्द्र मदाय क्रत्वे अपिबो विरप्शिन् । तमु ते गावो नर आपो अद्रिरिन्दुं समह्यन्पीतये समस्मै ॥
6.40.e: Drink thou of this whereof at birth, O Indra, thou drankest, Mighty One for power and rapture.  The men, the pressing-stones, the cows, the waters have made this Soma ready for thy drinking.

6.40.d: समिद्धे अग्नौ सुत इन्द्र सोम आ त्वा वहन्तु हरयो वहिष्ठाः । त्वायता मनसा जोहवीमीन्द्रा याहि सुविताय महे नः ॥
6.40.e: The fire is kindled, Soma pressed, O Indra: let thy Bays, best to draw, convey thee hither.  With mind devoted, Indra, I invoke thee. Come, for our great prosperity approach us.

6.40.d: आ याहि शश्वदुशता ययाथेन्द्र महा मनसा सोमपेयम् । उप ब्रह्माणि शृणव इमा नोऽथा ते यज्ञस्तन्वे३ वयो धात् ॥
6.40.e: Indra, come hither: evermore thou camest through our great strong desire to drink the Soma.  Listen and hear the prayers which now we offer, and let this sacrifice increase thy vigour.

6.40.d: यदिन्द्र दिवि पार्ये यदृधग्यद्वा स्वे सदने यत्र वासि । अतो नो यज्ञमवसे नियुत्वान्त्सजोषाः पाहि गिर्वणो मरुद्भिः ॥
6.40.e: Mayst thou, O Indra, on the day of trial, present or absent, wheresoe’er thou dwellest,  Thence, with thy team, accordant with the Maruts, Song-lover! guard our sacrifice, to help us.

6.41.d: अहेळमान उप याहि यज्ञं तुभ्यं पवन्त इन्दवः सुतासः । गावो न वज्रिन्त्स्वमोको अच्छेन्द्रा गहि प्रथमो यज्ञियानाम् ॥
6.41.e: COME gracious to our sacrifice, O Indra: pressed Soma-drops are purified to please thee.  As cattle seek their home, so Thunderwielder, come, Indra, first of those who claim our worship.

6.41.d: या ते काकुत्सुकृता या वरिष्ठा यया शश्वत्पिबसि मध्व ऊर्मिम् । तया पाहि प्र ते अध्वर्युरस्थात्सं ते वज्रो वर्ततामिन्द्र गव्युः ॥
6.41.e: With that well-formed most wide-extending palate, wherewith thou ever drinkest streams of sweetness,  Drink thou; the Adhvaryu standeth up before thee: let thy spoil-winning thunderbolt attend thee.

6.41.d: एष द्रप्सो वृषभो विश्वरूप इन्द्राय वृष्णे समकारि सोमः । एतं पिब हरिवः स्थातरुग्र यस्येशिषे प्रदिवि यस्ते अन्नम् ॥
6.41.e: This drop, steer-strong and omniform, the Soma, hath been made ready for the Bull, for India.  Drink this, Lord of the Bays, thou Strong Supporter, this that is thine of old, thy food for ever.

6.41.d: सुतः सोमो असुतादिन्द्र वस्यानयं श्रेयाञ्चिकितुषे रणाय । एतं तितिर्व उप याहि यज्ञं तेन विश्वास्तविषीरा पृणस्व ॥
6.41.e: Soma when pressed excels the unpressed Soma, better, for one who knows, to give him pleasure.  Come to this sacrifice of ours, O Victor replenish all thy powers with this libation.

6.41.d: ह्वयामसि त्वेन्द्र याह्यर्वाङरं ते सोमस्तन्वे भवाति । शतक्रतो मादयस्वा सुतेषु प्रास्माँ अव पृतनासु प्र विक्षु ॥
6.41.e: We call on thee, O Indra: come thou hither: sufficient be the Soma for thy body.  Rejoice thee, Śatakratu! in the juices guard us in wars, guard us among our people.

6.42.d: प्रत्यस्मै पिपीषते विश्वानि विदुषे भर । अरंगमाय जग्मयेऽपश्चाद्दघ्वने नरे ॥
6.42.e: BRING sacrificial gifts to him, Omniscient, for he longs to drink,  The Wanderer who comes with speed, the Hero ever in the van.

6.42.d: एमेनं प्रत्येतन सोमेभिः सोमपातमम् । अमत्रेभिर्ऋजीषिणमिन्द्रं सुतेभिरिन्दुभिः ॥
6.42.e: With Soma go ye nigh to him chief drinker of the Soma's juice:  With beakers to the Impetuous God, to Indra with the drops effused.

6.42.d: यदी सुतेभिरिन्दुभिः सोमेभिः प्रतिभूषथ । वेदा विश्वस्य मेधिरो धृषत्तंतमिदेषते ॥
6.42.e: What time, with Soma, with the juice effused, ye come before the God,  Full wise he knows the hope of each, and, Bold One, strikes this foe and that.

6.42.d: अस्माअस्मा इदन्धसोऽध्वर्यो प्र भरा सुतम् । कुवित्समस्य जेन्यस्य शर्धतोऽभिशस्तेरवस्परत् ॥
6.42.e: To him, Adhvaryu! yea, to him give offerings of the juice expressed.  Will he not keep us safely from the spiteful curse of each presumptuous high-born foe?

6.43.d: यस्य त्यच्छम्बरं मदे दिवोदासाय रन्धयः । अयं स सोम इन्द्र ते सुतः पिब ॥
6.43.e: IN whose wild joy thou madest once Śambara Divodāsa's prey,  This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra: drink!

6.43.d: यस्य तीव्रसुतं मदं मध्यमन्तं च रक्षसे । अयं स सोम इन्द्र ते सुतः पिब ॥
6.43.e: Whose gladdening draught, shed from the points, thou guardest in the midst and end,  This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra drink!

6.43.d: यस्य गा अन्तरश्मनो मदे दृळ्हा अवासृजः । अयं स सोम इन्द्र ते सुतः पिब ॥
6.43.e: In whose wild joy thou settest free the kine held fast within the rock,  This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra: drink!

6.43.d: यस्य मन्दानो अन्धसो माघोनं दधिषे शवः । अयं स सोम इन्द्र ते सुतः पिब ॥
6.43.e: This, in whose juice delighting thou gainest the might of Maghavan,  This Soma is pressed out for thee, O Indra drink!

6.44.d: यो रयिवो रयिंतमो यो द्युम्नैर्द्युम्नवत्तमः । सोमः सुतः स इन्द्र तेऽस्ति स्वधापते मदः ॥
6.44.e: THAT which is wealthiest, Wealthy God in splendoursmost illustrious,  Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.

6.44.d: यः शग्मस्तुविशग्म ते रायो दामा मतीनाम् । सोमः सुतः स इन्द्र तेऽस्ति स्वधापते मदः ॥
6.44.e: Effectual, Most Effectual One! thine, as bestowing wealth of hymns,  Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.

6.44.d: येन वृद्धो न शवसा तुरो न स्वाभिरूतिभिः । सोमः सुतः स इन्द्र तेऽस्ति स्वधापते मदः ॥
6.44.e: Wherewith thou art increased in strength, and conquerest with thy proper aids,  Soma is pressed: thy gladdening draught, Indra! libation's Lord! is this.

6.44.d: त्यमु वो अप्रहणं गृणीषे शवसस्पतिम् । इन्द्रं विश्वासाहं नरं मंहिष्ठं विश्वचर्षणिम् ॥
6.44.e: Him for your sake I glorify as Lord of Strength who wrongeth none,  The Hero Indra, conquering all, Most Bounteous, God of all the tribes.

6.44.d: यं वर्धयन्तीद्गिरः पतिं तुरस्य राधसः । तमिन्न्वस्य रोदसी देवी शुष्मं सपर्यतः ॥
6.44.e: Those Goddesses, both Heaven and Earth, revere the power and might of him,  Him whom our songs increase in strength, the Lord of bounty swift to come.

6.44.d: तद्व उक्थस्य बर्हणेन्द्रायोपस्तृणीषणि । विपो न यस्योतयो वि यद्रोहन्ति सक्षितः ॥
6.44.e: To seat your Indra, I will spread abroad with power this song of praise.  The saving succours that abide in him, like songs, extend and grow.

6.44.d: अविदद्दक्षं मित्रो नवीयान्पपानो देवेभ्यो वस्यो अचैत् । ससवान्त्स्तौलाभिर्धौतरीभिरुरुष्या पायुरभवत्सखिभ्यः ॥
6.44.e: A recent Friend, he found the skilful priest: he drank, and showed forth treasure from the Gods.  He conquered, borne by strong all-shaking mares, and was with far-spread power his friends' Protector.

6.44.d: ऋतस्य पथि वेधा अपायि श्रिये मनांसि देवासो अक्रन् । दधानो नाम महो वचोभिर्वपुर्दृशये वेन्यो व्यावः ॥
6.44.e: In course of Law the sapient juice was quaffed: the Deities to glory turned their mind.  Winning through hymns a lofty title, he, the Lovely, made his beauteous form apparent.

6.44.d: द्युमत्तमं दक्षं धेह्यस्मे सेधा जनानां पूर्वीररातीः । वर्षीयो वयः कृणुहि शचीभिर्धनस्य सातावस्माँ अविड्ढि ॥
6.44.e: Bestow on us the most illustrious strength ward off men's manifold malignities.  Give with thy might abundant vital force, and aid us graciously in gaining riches.
