6.44.d: इन्द्र तुभ्यमिन्मघवन्नभूम वयं दात्रे हरिवो मा वि वेनः । नकिरापिर्ददृशे मर्त्यत्रा किमङ्ग रध्रचोदनं त्वाहुः ॥
6.44.e: We turn to thee as Giver, liberal Indra. Lord of the Bay Steeds, be not thou ungracious.  No friend among mankind have we to lookto: why have men called thee him who spurs the niggard?

6.44.d: मा जस्वने वृषभ नो ररीथा मा ते रेवतः सख्ये रिषाम । पूर्वीष्ट इन्द्र निष्षिधो जनेषु जह्यसुष्वीन्प्र वृहापृणतः ॥
6.44.e: Give us not up, Strong Hero! to the hungry: unharmed be we whom thou, so rich, befriendest.  Full many a boon hast thou for men demolish those who present no gifts nor pour oblations.

6.44.d: उदभ्राणीव स्तनयन्नियर्तीन्द्रो राधांस्यश्व्यानि गव्या । त्वमसि प्रदिवः कारुधाया मा त्वादामान आ दभन्मघोनः ॥
6.44.e: As Indra thundering impels the rain-clouds, so doth he send us store of kine and horses.  Thou art of old the Cherisher of singers let not the rich who bring no gifts deceive thee.

6.44.d: अध्वर्यो वीर प्र महे सुतानामिन्द्राय भर स ह्यस्य राजा । यः पूर्व्याभिरुत नूतनाभिर्गीर्भिर्वावृधे गृणतामृषीणाम् ॥
6.44.e: Adbyaryu, hero, bring to mighty Indrafor he is King thereof-the pressed-out juices;  To him exalted by the hymns and praises, ancient and modern, of the singing Ṛṣis.

6.44.d: अस्य मदे पुरु वर्पांसि विद्वानिन्द्रो वृत्राण्यप्रती जघान । तमु प्र होषि मधुमन्तमस्मै सोमं वीराय शिप्रिणे पिबध्यै ॥
6.44.e: In the wild joy of this hath Indra, knowing full many a form, struck down resistless Vṛtras.  Proclaim aloud to him the savoury Soma so that the Hero, strong of jaw, may drink it.

6.44.d: पाता सुतमिन्द्रो अस्तु सोमं हन्ता वृत्रं वज्रेण मन्दसानः । गन्ता यज्ञं परावतश्चिदच्छा वसुर्धीनामविता कारुधायाः ॥
6.44.e: May Indra drink this Soma poured to please him, and cheered therewith slay Vṛtra with his thunder.  Come to our sacrifice even from a distance, good lover of our songs, the bard's Supporter.

6.44.d: इदं त्यत्पात्रमिन्द्रपानमिन्द्रस्य प्रियममृतमपायि । मत्सद्यथा सौमनसाय देवं व्य१स्मद्द्वेषो युयवद्व्यंहः ॥
6.44.e: The cup whence Indra drinks the draught is present: the Amṛta dear to Indra hath been drunken,  That it may cheer the God to gracious favour, and keep far from us hatred and affliction.

6.44.d: एना मन्दानो जहि शूर शत्रूञ्जामिमजामिं मघवन्नमित्रान् । अभिषेणाँ अभ्या३देदिशानान्पराच इन्द्र प्र मृणा जही च ॥
6.44.e: Therewith enraptured, Hero, slay our foemen, the unfriendly, Maghavan be they kin or strangers,  Those who still aim their hostile darts to smite us, turn them to flight, O Indra, crush and kill them.

6.44.d: आसु ष्मा णो मघवन्निन्द्र पृत्स्व१स्मभ्यं महि वरिवः सुगं कः । अपां तोकस्य तनयस्य जेष इन्द्र सूरीन्कृणुहि स्मा नो अर्धम् ॥
6.44.e: O Indra Maghavan, in these our battles win easy paths for us and ample freedom.  That we may gain waters and seed and offspring, set thou our princes on thy side, O Indra.

6.44.d: आ त्वा हरयो वृषणो युजाना वृषरथासो वृषरश्मयोऽत्याः । अस्मत्राञ्चो वृषणो वज्रवाहो वृष्णे मदाय सुयुजो वहन्तु ॥
6.44.e: Let thy Bay Stallions, harnessed, bring thee hither, Steeds with strong chariot and strong reins to hold them,  Strong Horses, speeding hither, bearing thunder, well-harnessed, for the strong exciting potion.

6.44.d: आ ते वृषन्वृषणो द्रोणमस्थुर्घृतप्रुषो नोर्मयो मदन्तः । इन्द्र प्र तुभ्यं वृषभिः सुतानां वृष्णे भरन्ति वृषभाय सोमम् ॥
6.44.e: Beside the vat, Strong God! stand thy strong Horses, shining with holy oil, like waves exulting.  Indra, they bring to thee, the Strong and Mighty, Soma of juices shed by mighty press-stones.

6.44.d: वृषासि दिवो वृषभः पृथिव्या वृषा सिन्धूनां वृषभः स्तियानाम् । वृष्णे त इन्दुर्वृषभ पीपाय स्वादू रसो मधुपेयो वराय ॥
6.44.e: Thou art the Bull of earth, the Bull of heaven, Bull of the rivers, Bull of standing waters.  For thee, the Strong, O Bull, hath Indu swollen. juice pleasant, sweet to drink, for thine election.

6.44.d: अयं देवः सहसा जायमान इन्द्रेण युजा पणिमस्तभायत् । अयं स्वस्य पितुरायुधानीन्दुरमुष्णादशिवस्य मायाः ॥
6.44.e: This God, with might, when first he had his being, with Indra for ally, held fast the Paṇi.  This Indu stole away the warlike weapons, and foiled the arts of his malignant father.

6.44.d: अयमकृणोदुषसः सुपत्नीरयं सूर्ये अदधाज्ज्योतिरन्तः । अयं त्रिधातु दिवि रोचनेषु त्रितेषु विन्ददमृतं निगूळ्हम् ॥
6.44.e: The Dawns he wedded to a glorious Consort, and set within the Sun the light that lights him.  He found in heaven, in the third lucid regions, the threefold Amṛta in its close concealment.

6.44.d: अयं द्यावापृथिवी वि ष्कभायदयं रथमयुनक्सप्तरश्मिम् । अयं गोषु शच्या पक्वमन्तः सोमो दाधार दशयन्त्रमुत्सम् ॥
6.44.e: He stayed and held the heaven and earth asunder: the chariot with the sevenfold reins he harnessed.  This Soma Set with power within the milch-kine a spring whose ripe contents ten fingers empty.

6.45.d: य आनयत्परावतः सुनीती तुर्वशं यदुम् । इन्द्रः स नो युवा सखा ॥
6.45.e: THAT Indra is our youthful Friend, who with his trusty guidance led  Turvaśa, Yadu from afar.

6.45.d: अविप्रे चिद्वयो दधदनाशुना चिदर्वता । इन्द्रो जेता हितं धनम् ॥
6.45.e: Even to the dull and uninspired Indra, gives vital power, and wins  Even with slow steed the offered prize.

6.45.d: महीरस्य प्रणीतयः पूर्वीरुत प्रशस्तयः । नास्य क्षीयन्त ऊतयः ॥
6.45.e: Great are his ways of guiding us, andṅanilbld are Ins eulogies:  His kind protections never fail.

6.45.d: सखायो ब्रह्मवाहसेऽर्चत प्र च गायत । स हि नः प्रमतिर्मही ॥
6.45.e: Friends, sing your psalm and offer praise to him to whom the prayer is brought:  For our great Providence is he.

6.45.d: त्वमेकस्य वृत्रहन्नविता द्वयोरसि । उतेदृशे यथा वयम् ॥
6.45.e: Thou, Slaughterer of Vṛtra, art Guardian and Friend of one and two,  Yea, of a man like one of us.

6.45.d: नयसीद्वति द्विषः कृणोष्युक्थशंसिनः । नृभिः सुवीर उच्यसे ॥
6.45.e: Beyond men's hate thou leadest us, and givest cause to sing thy praise:  Good hero art thou called by men.

6.45.d: ब्रह्माणं ब्रह्मवाहसं गीर्भिः सखायमृग्मियम् । गां न दोहसे हुवे ॥
6.45.e: I call with hymns, as ’twere a cow to milk, the Friend who merits praise,  The Brahman who accepts the prayer.

6.45.d: यस्य विश्वानि हस्तयोरूचुर्वसूनि नि द्विता । वीरस्य पृतनाषहः ॥
6.45.e: Him in whose hands they say are stored all treasures from the days of old,  The Hero, conquering in the fight.

6.45.d: वि दृळ्हानि चिदद्रिवो जनानां शचीपते । वृह माया अनानत ॥
6.45.e: Lord of Strength, Caster of the Stone, destroy the firm forts built by men,  And foil their arts, unbending God!

6.45.d: तमु त्वा सत्य सोमपा इन्द्र वाजानां पते । अहूमहि श्रवस्यवः ॥
6.45.e: Thee, thee as such, O Lord of Power, O Indra, Soma-drinker, true,  We, fain for glory, have invoked.

6.45.d: तमु त्वा यः पुरासिथ यो वा नूनं हिते धने । हव्यः स श्रुधी हवम् ॥
6.45.e: Such as thou wast of old, and art now to be called on when the prize  lies ready, listen to our call.

6.45.d: धीभिरर्वद्भिरर्वतो वाजाँ इन्द्र श्रवाय्यान् । त्वया जेष्म हितं धनम् ॥
6.45.e: With hymns and coursers we will gain, Indra, through thee, both steeds and spoil  Most glorious, and the proffered prize.

6.45.d: अभूरु वीर गिर्वणो महाँ इन्द्र धने हिते । भरे वितन्तसाय्यः ॥
6.45.e: Thou, Indra, Lover of the Song, whom men must stir to help, hast been  Great in the contest for the prize.

6.45.d: या त ऊतिरमित्रहन्मक्षूजवस्तमासति । तया नो हिनुही रथम् ॥
6.45.e: Slayer of foes, whatever aid of thine imparts the swiftest course,  With that impel our car to speed.

6.45.d: स रथेन रथीतमोऽस्माकेनाभियुग्वना । जेषि जिष्णो हितं धनम् ॥
6.45.e: As skilfullest of those who drive the chariot, with our art and aim,  O Conqueror, win the proffered prize.

6.45.d: य एक इत्तमु ष्टुहि कृष्टीनां विचर्षणिः । पतिर्जज्ञे वृषक्रतुः ॥
6.45.e: Praise him who, Matchless and Alone, was born the Lord of living men,  Most active, with heroic soul.

6.45.d: यो गृणतामिदासिथापिरूती शिवः सखा । स त्वं न इन्द्र मृळय ॥
6.45.e: Thou who hast been the singers' Friend, a Friend auspicious with thine aid,  As such, O Indra, favour us.

6.45.d: धिष्व वज्रं गभस्त्यो रक्षोहत्याय वज्रिवः । सासहीष्ठा अभि स्पृधः ॥
6.45.e: Grasp in thine arms the thunderbolt, O Thunder-armed, to slay the fiends:  Mayst thou subdue the foemen's host.

6.45.d: प्रत्नं रयीणां युजं सखायं कीरिचोदनम् । ब्रह्मवाहस्तमं हुवे ॥
6.45.e: I call the ancient Friend, allied with wealth, who speeds the lowly man,  Him to whom chiefly prayer is brought.

6.45.d: स हि विश्वानि पार्थिवाँ एको वसूनि पत्यते । गिर्वणस्तमो अध्रिगुः ॥
6.45.e: For he alone is Lord of all the treasures of the earth: he speeds  Hither, chief Lover of the Song.

6.45.d: स नो नियुद्भिरा पृण कामं वाजेभिरश्विभिः । गोमद्भिर्गोपते धृषत् ॥
6.45.e: So with thy yoked teams satisfy our wish with power and wealth in steeds  And cattle, boldly, Lord of kine!

6.45.d: तद्वो गाय सुते सचा पुरुहूताय सत्वने । शं यद्गवे न शाकिने ॥
6.45.e: Sing this, what time the ' juice is pressed, to him your Hero, Much-invoked,  To please him as a mighty Steer.

6.45.d: न घा वसुर्नि यमते दानं वाजस्य गोमतः । यत्सीमुप श्रवद्गिरः ॥
6.45.e: He, Excellent, withholdeth not his gift of power and wealth in kine,  When he hath listened to our songs.

6.45.d: कुवित्सस्य प्र हि व्रजं गोमन्तं दस्युहा गमत् । शचीभिरप नो वरत् ॥
6.45.e: May he with might unclose for us the cow's stall, whosesoe’er it be,  To which the Dasyu-slayer goes.

6.45.d: इमा उ त्वा शतक्रतोऽभि प्र णोनुवुर्गिरः । इन्द्र वत्सं न मातरः ॥
6.45.e: O Indra Śatakratu, these our songs have called aloud to thee,  Like mother cows to meet their calves.

6.45.d: दूणाशं सख्यं तव गौरसि वीर गव्यते । अश्वो अश्वायते भव ॥
6.45.e: Hard is thy love to win: thou art a Steer to him who longs for steers:  Be to one craving steeds a Steed.

6.45.d: स मन्दस्वा ह्यन्धसो राधसे तन्वा महे । न स्तोतारं निदे करः ॥
6.45.e: Delight thee with the juice we pour for thine own great munificence:  Yield not thy singer to reproach.

6.45.d: इमा उ त्वा सुतेसुते नक्षन्ते गिर्वणो गिरः । वत्सं गावो न धेनवः ॥
6.45.e: These songs with every draught we pour come, Lover of the Song, to thee,  As milch-kine hasten to their young

6.45.d: पुरूतमं पुरूणां स्तोतॄणां विवाचि । वाजेभिर्वाजयताम् ॥
6.45.e: To thee most oft invoked, amid the many singers' rivalry  Who beg with all their might for wealth.

6.45.d: अस्माकमिन्द्र भूतु ते स्तोमो वाहिष्ठो अन्तमः । अस्मान्राये महे हिनु ॥
6.45.e: Nearest and most attractive may our laud, O Indra come to thee.  Urge thou us on to ample wealth.

6.45.d: अधि बृबुः पणीनां वर्षिष्ठे मूर्धन्नस्थात् । उरुः कक्षो न गाङ्ग्यः ॥
6.45.e: Brbu hath set himself above the Paṇis, o’er their highest head,  Like the wide bush on Gan!gā's bank.

6.45.d: यस्य वायोरिव द्रवद्भद्रा रातिः सहस्रिणी । सद्यो दानाय मंहते ॥
6.45.e: He whose good bounty, thousandfold, swift as the rushing of the wind,  Suddenly offers as a gift.

6.45.d: तत्सु नो विश्वे अर्य आ सदा गृणन्ति कारवः । बृबुं सहस्रदातमं सूरिं सहस्रसातमम् ॥
6.45.e: So all our singers ever praise the pious Brbu's noble deed,  Chief, best to give his thousands, best to give a thousand liberal gifts.

6.46.d: त्वामिद्धि हवामहे साता वाजस्य कारवः । त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं नरस्त्वां काष्ठास्वर्वतः ॥
6.46.e: THAT we may win us wealth and power we poets, verily, call on thee:  In war men call on thee, Indra, the hero's Lord, in the steed's race-course call on thee.

6.46.d: स त्वं नश्चित्र वज्रहस्त धृष्णुया महः स्तवानो अद्रिवः । गामश्वं रथ्यमिन्द्र सं किर सत्रा वाजं न जिग्युषे ॥
6.46.e: As such, O Wonderful, whose hand holds thunder, praised as mighty, Caster of the Stone!  Pour on us boldly, Indra, kine and chariotsteeds, ever to be the conqueror's strength.

6.46.d: यः सत्राहा विचर्षणिरिन्द्रं तं हूमहे वयम् । सहस्रमुष्क तुविनृम्ण सत्पते भवा समत्सु नो वृधे ॥
6.46.e: We call upon that Indra, who, most active, ever slays the foe:  Lord of the brave, Most Manly, with a thousand powers, help thou and prosper us in fight.

6.46.d: बाधसे जनान्वृषभेव मन्युना घृषौ मीळ्ह ऋचीषम । अस्माकं बोध्यविता महाधने तनूष्वप्सु सूर्ये ॥
6.46.e: Rcisama, thou forcest men as with a bull, with anger, in the furious fray.  Be thou our Helper in the mighty battle fought for sunlight, water, and for life.

6.46.d: इन्द्र ज्येष्ठं न आ भरँ ओजिष्ठं पपुरि श्रवः । येनेमे चित्र वज्रहस्त रोदसी ओभे सुशिप्र प्राः ॥
6.46.e: O Indra, bring us name and fame, enriching, mightiest, excellent,  Wherewith, O Wondrous God, fair-visored, thunder-armed, thou hast filled full this earth and heaven.

6.46.d: त्वामुग्रमवसे चर्षणीसहं राजन्देवेषु हूमहे । विश्वा सु नो विथुरा पिब्दना वसोऽमित्रान्त्सुषहान्कृधि ॥
6.46.e: We call on thee, O King, Mighty amid the Gods, Ruler of men, to succour us.  All that is weak in us, Excellent God, make firm: make our foes easy to subdue.

6.46.d: यदिन्द्र नाहुषीष्वाँ ओजो नृम्णं च कृष्टिषु । यद्वा पञ्च क्षितीनां द्युम्नमा भर सत्रा विश्वानि पौंस्या ॥
6.46.e: All strength and valour that is found, Indra, in tribes of Nahusas, and all the splendid fame that the Five Tribes enjoy  Bring, yea, all manly powers at once.

6.46.d: यद्वा तृक्षौ मघवन्द्रुह्यावा जने यत्पूरौ कच्च वृष्ण्यम् । अस्मभ्यं तद्रिरीहि सं नृषाह्येऽमित्रान्पृत्सु तुर्वणे ॥
6.46.e: Or, Maghavan, what vigorous strength in Trksi lay, in Druhyus or in Paru's folk,  Fully bestow on us, that, in the conquering fray, we may subdue our foes in fight.

6.46.d: इन्द्र त्रिधातु शरणं त्रिवरूथं स्वस्तिमत् । छर्दिर्यच्छ मघवद्भ्यश्च मह्यं च यावया दिद्युमेभ्यः ॥
6.46.e: O Indra, grant a happy home, a triple refuge triply strong.  Bestow a dwelling-place on the rich lords and me, and keep thy dart afar from these.

6.46.d: ये गव्यता मनसा शत्रुमादभुरभिप्रघ्नन्ति धृष्णुया । अध स्मा नो मघवन्निन्द्र गिर्वणस्तनूपा अन्तमो भव ॥
6.46.e: They who with minds intent on spoil subdue the foe, boldly attack and smite him down,—  From these, O Indra Maghavan who lovest song, be closest guardian of our lives.

6.46.d: अध स्मा नो वृधे भवेन्द्र नायमवा युधि । यदन्तरिक्षे पतयन्ति पर्णिनो दिद्यवस्तिग्ममूर्धानः ॥
6.46.e: And now, O Indra, strengthen us: come near and aid us in the fight,  What time the feathered shafts are flying in the air, the arrows with their sharpened points.

6.46.d: यत्र शूरासस्तन्वो वितन्वते प्रिया शर्म पितॄणाम् । अध स्मा यच्छ तन्वे३ तने च छर्दिरचित्तं यावय द्वेषः ॥
6.46.e: Give us, where heroes strain their bodies in the fight, the shelter that our fathers loved.  To us and to our sons give refuge: keep afar all unobserved hostility.

6.46.d: यदिन्द्र सर्गे अर्वतश्चोदयासे महाधने । असमने अध्वनि वृजिने पथि श्येनाँ इव श्रवस्यतः ॥
6.46.e: When, Indra, in the mighty fray thou urgest chargers to their speed,  On the uneven road and on a toilsome path, like falcons, eager for renown,

6.46.d: सिन्धूँरिव प्रवण आशुया यतो यदि क्लोशमनु ष्वणि । आ ये वयो न वर्वृतत्यामिषि गृभीता बाह्वोर्गवि ॥
6.46.e: Speeding like rivers rushing down a steep descent, responsive to the urging call,  That come like birds attracted to the bait, held in by reins in both the driver's hands.

6.47.d: स्वादुष्किलायं मधुमाँ उतायं तीव्रः किलायं रसवाँ उतायम् । उतो न्व१स्य पपिवांसमिन्द्रं न कश्चन सहत आहवेषु ॥
6.47.e: YEA, this is good to taste and full of. sweetness, verily it is strong and rich in flavour.  No one may conquer Indra in the battle when he hath drunken of the draught we offer.

6.47.d: अयं स्वादुरिह मदिष्ठ आस यस्येन्द्रो वृत्रहत्ये ममाद । पुरूणि यश्च्यौत्ना शम्बरस्य वि नवतिं नव च देह्यो३ हन् ॥
6.47.e: This sweet juice here had mightiest power to gladden: it boldened Indra when he siaughtered Vṛtra,  When he defeated Śambara's many onslaughts, and battered down his nineand ninety ramparts.

6.47.d: अयं मे पीत उदियर्ति वाचमयं मनीषामुशतीमजीगः । अयं षळुर्वीरमिमीत धीरो न याभ्यो भुवनं कच्चनारे ॥
6.47.e: This stirreth up my voice when I have drunk it: this hath aroused from sleep my yearning spirit.  This Sage hath measured out the six expanses from which no single creature is excluded.

6.47.d: अयं स यो वरिमाणं पृथिव्या वर्ष्माणं दिवो अकृणोदयं सः । अयं पीयूषं तिसृषु प्रवत्सु सोमो दाधारोर्व१न्तरिक्षम् ॥
6.47.e: This, even this, is he who hath created the breadth of earth, the lofty height of heaven.  He formed the nectar in three headlong rivers. Soma supports the wide mid-air above us.

6.47.d: अयं विदच्चित्रदृशीकमर्णः शुक्रसद्मनामुषसामनीके । अयं महान्महता स्कम्भनेनोद्द्यामस्तभ्नाद्वृषभो मरुत्वान् ॥
6.47.e: He found the wavy sea of brilliant colours in forefront of the Dawns who dwell in brightness.  This Mighty One, the Steer begirt by Maruts, hath propped the heavens up with a mighty pillar.

6.47.d: धृषत्पिब कलशे सोममिन्द्र वृत्रहा शूर समरे वसूनाम् । माध्यंदिने सवन आ वृषस्व रयिस्थानो रयिमस्मासु धेहि ॥
6.47.e: Drink Soma boldly from the beaker, Indra, in war for treasures, Hero, Vṛtra-slayer!  Fill thyself full at the mid-day libation, and give us wealth, thou Treasury of riches.

6.47.d: इन्द्र प्र णः पुरएतेव पश्य प्र नो नय प्रतरं वस्यो अच्छ । भवा सुपारो अतिपारयो नो भवा सुनीतिरुत वामनीतिः ॥
6.47.e: Look out for us, O Indra, as our Leader, and guide us on to gain yet goodlier treasure.  Excellent Guardian, bear us well through peril, and lead us on to wealth with careful guidance.

6.47.d: उरुं नो लोकमनु नेषि विद्वान्त्स्वर्वज्ज्योतिरभयं स्वस्ति । ऋष्वा त इन्द्र स्थविरस्य बाहू उप स्थेयाम शरणा बृहन्ता ॥
6.47.e: Lead us to ample room, O thou who knowest, to happiness, security, and sunlight.  High, Indra, are the arms of thee the Mighty: may we betake. us to their lofty shelter.

6.47.d: वरिष्ठे न इन्द्र वन्धुरे धा वहिष्ठयोः शतावन्नश्वयोरा । इषमा वक्षीषां वर्षिष्ठां मा नस्तारीन्मघवन्रायो अर्यः ॥
6.47.e: Set us on widest chariot-seat, O Indra, with two steeds best to draw, O Lord of Hundreds!  Bring us the best among all sorts of viands: let not the foe's wealth, Maghavan, subdue us.

6.47.d: इन्द्र मृळ मह्यं जीवातुमिच्छ चोदय धियमयसो न धाराम् । यत्किं चाहं त्वायुरिदं वदामि तज्जुषस्व कृधि मा देववन्तम् ॥
6.47.e: Be gracious, Indra, let my days be lengthened: sharpen my thought as ’twere a blade of iron  Approve whatever words I speak, dependent on thee, and grant me thy divine protection.

6.47.d: त्रातारमिन्द्रमवितारमिन्द्रं हवेहवे सुहवं शूरमिन्द्रम् । ह्वयामि शक्रं पुरुहूतमिन्द्रं स्वस्ति नो मघवा धात्विन्द्रः ॥
6.47.e: Indra the Rescuer, Indra the Helper, Hero who listens at each invocation,  Śakra I call, Indra invoked of many. May Indra Maghavan prosper and bless us.

6.47.d: इन्द्रः सुत्रामा स्ववाँ अवोभिः सुमृळीको भवतु विश्ववेदाः । बाधतां द्वेषो अभयं कृणोतु सुवीर्यस्य पतयः स्याम ॥
6.47.e: May helpful Indra as our good Protector, Lord of all treasures, favour us with succour,  Baffle our foes, and give us rest and safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigour.

6.47.d: तस्य वयं सुमतौ यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम । स सुत्रामा स्ववाँ इन्द्रो अस्मे आराच्चिद्द्वेषः सनुतर्युयोतु ॥
6.47.e: May we enjoy the grace of him the Holy, yea, may we dwell in his auspicious favour.  May helpful Indra as our good Preserver drive from us, even from afar, our foemen.

6.47.d: अव त्वे इन्द्र प्रवतो नोर्मिर्गिरो ब्रह्माणि नियुतो धवन्ते । उरू न राधः सवना पुरूण्यपो गा वज्रिन्युवसे समिन्दून् ॥
6.47.e: Like rivers rushing down a slope, O Indra, to thee haste songs and prayers and linked verses.  Thou gatherest, Thunderer! like widespread bounty, kine, water, drops, and manifold libations.

6.47.d: क ईं स्तवत्कः पृणात्को यजाते यदुग्रमिन्मघवा विश्वहावेत् । पादाविव प्रहरन्नन्यमन्यं कृणोति पूर्वमपरं शचीभिः ॥
6.47.e: Who lauds him, satisfies him, pays him worship? E’en the rich noble still hath found him mighty.  With power, as when one moves his feet alternate, he makes the last precede, the foremost follow.

6.47.d: शृण्वे वीर उग्रमुग्रं दमायन्नन्यमन्यमतिनेनीयमानः । एधमानद्विळुभयस्य राजा चोष्कूयते विश इन्द्रो मनुष्यान् ॥
6.47.e: Famed is the Hero as each strong man's tamer, ever advancing one and then another.  King of both worlds, hating the high and haughty, Indra protects the men who are his people.

6.47.d: परा पूर्वेषां सख्या वृणक्ति वितर्तुराणो अपरेभिरेति । अनानुभूतीरवधून्वानः पूर्वीरिन्द्रः शरदस्तर्तरीति ॥
6.47.e: He loves no more the men he loved aforetime: he turns and moves away allied with others.  Rejecting those who disregard his worship, Indra victorious lives through many autumns.

6.47.d: रूपंरूपं प्रतिरूपो बभूव तदस्य रूपं प्रतिचक्षणाय । इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥
6.47.e: In every figure he hath been the mode: this is his only form for us to look on.  Indra moves multiform by his illusions; for his Bay Steeds are yoked, ten times a hundred.

6.47.d: युजानो हरिता रथे भूरि त्वष्टेह राजति । को विश्वाहा द्विषतः पक्ष आसत उतासीनेषु सूरिषु ॥
6.47.e: Here Tvaṣṭar, yoking to the car the Bay Steeds, hath extended sway.  Who will for ever stand upon the foeman's side, even when our princes sit at ease?

6.47.d: अगव्यूति क्षेत्रमागन्म देवा उर्वी सती भूमिरंहूरणाभूत् । बृहस्पते प्र चिकित्सा गविष्टावित्था सते जरित्र इन्द्र पन्थाम् ॥
6.47.e: Gods, we have reached a country void of pasture the land, though spacious, was too small to hold us.  Bṛhaspati, provide in war for cattle; find a path, Indra, for this faithful singer.

6.47.d: दिवेदिवे सदृशीरन्यमर्धं कृष्णा असेधदप सद्मनो जाः । अहन्दासा वृषभो वस्नयन्तोदव्रजे वर्चिनं शम्बरं च ॥
6.47.e: Day after day far from their seat he drove them, alike, from place to place, those darksome creatures.  The Hero slew the meanly-huckstering Dāsas, Varcin and Śambara, where the waters gather.

6.47.d: प्रस्तोक इन्नु राधसस्त इन्द्र दश कोशयीर्दश वाजिनोऽदात् । दिवोदासादतिथिग्वस्य राधः शाम्बरं वसु प्रत्यग्रभीष्म ॥
6.47.e: Out of thy bounty, Indra, hath Prastoka bestowed ten coffers and ten mettled horses.  We have received in turn from Divodāsa Śambara's wealth, the gift of Atithigva.

6.47.d: दशाश्वान्दश कोशान्दश वस्त्राधिभोजना । दशो हिरण्यपिण्डान्दिवोदासादसानिषम् ॥
6.47.e: Ten horses and ten treasure-chests, ten garments as an added gift,  These and ten lumps of gold have I received from Divodāsa's hand.

6.47.d: दश रथान्प्रष्टिमतः शतं गा अथर्वभ्यः । अश्वथः पायवेऽदात् ॥
6.47.e: Ten cars with extra steed to each, for the Atharvans hundred cows,  Hath Asvatha to Payu given.

6.47.d: महि राधो विश्वजन्यं दधानान्भरद्वाजान्त्सार्ञ्जयो अभ्ययष्ट ॥
6.47.e: Thus Sṛñjaya's son honoured the Bharadvājas, recipients of all noble gifts and bounty.

6.47.d: वनस्पते वीड्वङ्गो हि भूया अस्मत्सखा प्रतरणः सुवीरः । गोभिः संनद्धो असि वीळयस्वास्थाता ते जयतु जेत्वानि ॥
6.47.e: Lord of the wood, be firm and strong in body: be, bearing us, a brave victorious hero  Show forth thy strength, compact with straps of leather, and let thy rider win all spoils of battle.

6.47.d: दिवस्पृथिव्याः पर्योज उद्भृतं वनस्पतिभ्यः पर्याभृतं सहः । अपामोज्मानं परि गोभिरावृतमिन्द्रस्य वज्रं हविषा रथं यज ॥
6.47.e: Its mighty strength was borrowed from the heaven and earth: its conquering force was brought from sovrans of the wood.  Honour with holy gifts the Car like Indra's bolt, the Car bound round with straps, the vigour of the floods.

6.47.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो मरुतामनीकं मित्रस्य गर्भो वरुणस्य नाभिः । सेमां नो हव्यदातिं जुषाणो देव रथ प्रति हव्या गृभाय ॥
6.47.e: Thou Bolt of Indra, Vanguard of the Maruts, close knit to Varuṇa and Child of Mitra,—  As such, accepting gifts which here we offer, receive, O Godlike Chariot, these oblations.

6.47.d: उप श्वासय पृथिवीमुत द्यां पुरुत्रा ते मनुतां विष्ठितं जगत् । स दुन्दुभे सजूरिन्द्रेण देवैर्दूराद्दवीयो अप सेध शत्रून् ॥
6.47.e: Send forth thy voice aloud through earth and heaven, and let the world in all its breadth regard thee;  O Drum, accordant with the Gods and Indra, drive thou afar, yea, very far, our foemen.

6.47.d: आ क्रन्दय बलमोजो न आ धा निः ष्टनिहि दुरिता बाधमानः । अप प्रोथ दुन्दुभे दुच्छुना इत इन्द्रस्य मुष्टिरसि वीळयस्व ॥
6.47.e: Thunder out strength and fill us full of vigour: yea, thunder forth and drive away all dangers.  Drive hence, O War-drum, drive away misfortune: thou art the Fist of Indra: show thy firmness.

6.47.d: आमूरज प्रत्यावर्तयेमाः केतुमद्दुन्दुभिर्वावदीति । समश्वपर्णाश्चरन्ति नो नरोऽस्माकमिन्द्र रथिनो जयन्तु ॥
6.47.e: Drive hither those, and these again bring hither: the War-drum speaks aloud as battle's signal.  Our heroes, winged with horses, come together. Let our car-warriors, Indra, be triumphant.

6.48.d: यज्ञायज्ञा वो अग्नये गिरागिरा च दक्षसे । प्रप्र वयममृतं जातवेदसं प्रियं मित्रं न शंसिषम् ॥
6.48.e: SING to your Agni with each song, at every sacrifice, for strength.  Come, let us praise the Wise and Everlasting God, even as a well-beloved Friend,

6.48.d: ऊर्जो नपातं स हिनायमस्मयुर्दाशेम हव्यदातये । भुवद्वाजेष्वविता भुवद्वृध उत त्राता तनूनाम् ॥
6.48.e: The Son of Strength; for is he not our gracious Lord? Let us serve him who bears our gifts.  In battle may he be our help and strengthener, yea, be the saviour of our lives.

6.48.d: वृषा ह्यग्ने अजरो महान्विभास्यर्चिषा । अजस्रेण शोचिषा शोशुचच्छुचे सुदीतिभिः सु दीदिहि ॥
6.48.e: Agni, thou beamest forth with light, great Hero, never changed by time.  Shining, pure Agni! with a light that never fades, beam with thy fair beams brilliantly.

6.48.d: महो देवान्यजसि यक्ष्यानुषक्तव क्रत्वोत दंसना । अर्वाचः सीं कृणुह्यग्नेऽवसे रास्व वाजोत वंस्व ॥
6.48.e: Thou worshippest great Gods: bring them without delay by wisdom and thy wondrous power.  O Agni, make them turn hither to succour us. Give strength, and win it for thyself.

6.48.d: यमापो अद्रयो वना गर्भमृतस्य पिप्रति । सहसा यो मथितो जायते नृभिः पृथिव्या अधि सानवि ॥
6.48.e: He whom floods, stones, and trees support, the offspring of eternal Law;  He who when rubbed with force is brought to life by men upon the lofty height of earth;

6.48.d: आ यः पप्रौ भानुना रोदसी उभे धूमेन धावते दिवि । तिरस्तमो ददृश ऊर्म्यास्वा श्यावास्वरुषो वृषा श्यावा अरुषो वृषा ॥
6.48.e: He who hath filled both worlds fult with his brilliant shine, who hastens with his smoke to heaven;  He made himself apparent through the gloom by night, the Red Bull in the darksome nights, the Red Bull in the darksome nights.

6.48.d: बृहद्भिरग्ने अर्चिभिः शुक्रेण देव शोचिषा । भरद्वाजे समिधानो यविष्ठ्य रेवन्नः शुक्र दीदिहि द्युमत्पावक दीदिहि ॥
6.48.e: O Agni, with thy lofty beams, with thy pure brilliancy, O God,  Kindled, Most Youthful One! by Bharadvāja's hand, shine on us, O pure God, with wealth, shine, Purifier! splendidly.

6.48.d: विश्वासां गृहपतिर्विशामसि त्वमग्ने मानुषीणाम् । शतं पूर्भिर्यविष्ठ पाह्यंहसः समेद्धारं शतं हिमाः स्तोतृभ्यो ये च ददति ॥
6.48.e: Thou art the Lord of house and home of all the tribes, O Agni, of all tribes of men.  Guard with a hundred forts thy kindler from distress, through hundred winters, Youngest God! and those who make thy singers rich.

6.48.d: त्वं नश्चित्र ऊत्या वसो राधांसि चोदय । अस्य रायस्त्वमग्ने रथीरसि विदा गाधं तुचे तु नः ॥
6.48.e: Wonderful, with thy favouring help, send us thy bounties, gracious Lord.  Thou art the Charioteer, Agni, of earthly wealth: find rest and safety for our seed.

6.48.d: पर्षि तोकं तनयं पर्तृभिष्ट्वमदब्धैरप्रयुत्वभिः । अग्ने हेळांसि दैव्या युयोधि नोऽदेवानि ह्वरांसि च ॥
6.48.e: With guards unfailing never negligent speed thou our children and our progeny.  Keep far from us, O Agni, all celestial wrath and wickedness of godless men.

6.48.d: आ सखायः सबर्दुघां धेनुमजध्वमुप नव्यसा वचः । सृजध्वमनपस्फुराम् ॥
6.48.e: Hither, O friends, with newest song drive her who freely pours her milk;  Loose her who never turns away;

6.48.d: या शर्धाय मारुताय स्वभानवे श्रवोऽमृत्यु धुक्षत । या मृळीके मरुतां तुराणां या सुम्नैरेवयावरी ॥
6.48.e: Who, for the host of Maruts bright with native sheen, hath shed immortal fame like milk;  Whom the impetuous Maruts look upon with love, who moves in splendour on their ways.

6.48.d: भरद्वाजायाव धुक्षत द्विता । धेनुं च विश्वदोहसमिषं च विश्वभोजसम् ॥
6.48.e: For Bharadvāja she poured down in days of old  The milch-cow yielding milk for all, and food that gives all nourishment.

6.48.d: तं व इन्द्रं न सुक्रतुं वरुणमिव मायिनम् । अर्यमणं न मन्द्रं सृप्रभोजसं विष्णुं न स्तुष आदिशे ॥
6.48.e: Your friend like Indra passing wise, with magic power like Varuṇa.  Like Aryaman joy-giving, bringing plenteous food like ViSnxu for my wish, I praise,

6.48.d: त्वेषं शर्धो न मारुतं तुविष्वण्यनर्वाणं पूषणं सं यथा शता । सं सहस्रा कारिषच्चर्षणिभ्य आँ आविर्गूळ्हा वसू करत्सुवेदा नो वसू करत् ॥
6.48.e: Bright as the host of Maruts mighty in their roar. May they bring Pūṣan free from foes;  May they bring hither hundreds, thousands for our men: may they bring hidden stores to light, and make wealth easy to be found.

6.48.d: आ मा पूषन्नुप द्रव शंसिषं नु ते अपिकर्ण आघृणे । अघा अर्यो अरातयः ॥
6.48.e: Haste to me, Pūṣan, in thine car, bright Deity: I fain would speak:  Most sinful is our foeman's hate.

6.48.d: मा काकम्बीरमुद्वृहो वनस्पतिमशस्तीर्वि हि नीनशः । मोत सूरो अह एवा चन ग्रीवा आदधते वेः ॥
6.48.e: Tear not up by the roots the Kakambira tree: destroy thou all malignity.  Let them not snare by day the neck of that Celestial Bird the Sun.

6.48.d: दृतेरिव तेऽवृकमस्तु सख्यम् । अच्छिद्रस्य दधन्वतः सुपूर्णस्य दधन्वतः ॥
6.48.e: Uninjured let thy friendship be, like the smooth surface of a skin,  A flawless skin, containing curds, full to the mouth, containing curds.

6.48.d: परो हि मर्त्यैरसि समो देवैरुत श्रिया । अभि ख्यः पूषन्पृतनासु नस्त्वमवा नूनं यथा पुरा ॥
6.48.e: For thou art high above mankind, in glory equal to the Gods.  Therefore, O Pūṣan, look upon us in the fight: now help us as in days of old.

6.48.d: वामी वामस्य धूतयः प्रणीतिरस्तु सूनृता । देवस्य वा मरुतो मर्त्यस्य वेजानस्य प्रयज्यवः ॥
6.48.e: May the kind excellence of him the Kind, loud Roarers! be our guide,  Be it the God's, O Maruts, or a mortal man's who worships, ye impetuous Ones!

6.48.d: सद्यश्चिद्यस्य चर्कृतिः परि द्यां देवो नैति सूर्यः । त्वेषं शवो दधिरे नाम यज्ञियं मरुतो वृत्रहं शवो ज्येष्ठं वृत्रहं शवः ॥
6.48.e: They whose high glory in a moment like the God, the Sun, goes round the space of heaven,  The Maruts have obtained bright strength, a sacred name, strength that destroys the Vṛtras, strength Vṛtra-destroying excellent.

6.48.d: सकृद्ध द्यौरजायत सकृद्भूमिरजायत । पृश्न्या दुग्धं सकृत्पयस्तदन्यो नानु जायते ॥
6.48.e: Once, only once, the heaven was made, once only once, the earth was formed-  Once, only Pṛśni's milk was shed: no second, after this, is born.

6.49.d: स्तुषे जनं सुव्रतं नव्यसीभिर्गीर्भिर्मित्रावरुणा सुम्नयन्ता । त आ गमन्तु त इह श्रुवन्तु सुक्षत्रासो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निः ॥
6.49.e: I LAUD with newest songs the Righteous People, Mitra and Varuṇa who make us happy.  Let them approach, here let them listen,Agni, Varuṇa, Mitra, Lords of fair dominion.

6.49.d: विशोविश ईड्यमध्वरेष्वदृप्तक्रतुमरतिं युवत्योः । दिवः शिशुं सहसः सूनुमग्निं यज्ञस्य केतुमरुषं यजध्यै ॥
6.49.e: Him, to be praised at each tribe's sacrifices, the Two young Matrons' sober-minded Herald,  The Son of Strength, the Child of Heaven, the signal of sacrifice, red Agni will I worship.

6.49.d: अरुषस्य दुहितरा विरूपे स्तृभिरन्या पिपिशे सूरो अन्या । मिथस्तुरा विचरन्ती पावके मन्म श्रुतं नक्षत ऋच्यमाने ॥
6.49.e: Unlike in form are the Red God's two Daughters: one is the Sun's, and stars bedeck the other.  Apart, the Sanctifiers, in succession, come to the famed hymn, praised in holy verses.

6.49.d: प्र वायुमच्छा बृहती मनीषा बृहद्रयिं विश्ववारं रथप्राम् । द्युतद्यामा नियुतः पत्यमानः कविः कविमियक्षसि प्रयज्यो ॥
6.49.e: I with a lofty song call hither Vāyu, all-bounteous, filler of his car, most wealthy.  Thou, Sage, with bright path, Lord of harnessed horses, impetuous, promptly honourest the prudent.

6.49.d: स मे वपुश्छदयदश्विनोर्यो रथो विरुक्मान्मनसा युजानः । येन नरा नासत्येषयध्यै वर्तिर्याथस्तनयाय त्मने च ॥
6.49.e: That chariot of the Aśvins, fair to look on, pleaseth me well, yoked with a thought, refulgent,  Wherewith, Nāsatyas, Chiefs, ye seek our dwelling, to give new strength to us and to our children.

6.49.d: पर्जन्यवाता वृषभा पृथिव्याः पुरीषाणि जिन्वतमप्यानि । सत्यश्रुतः कवयो यस्य गीर्भिर्जगतः स्थातर्जगदा कृणुध्वम् ॥
6.49.e: Bulls of the Earth, O Vāta and Parjanya, stir up for us the regions of the water.  Hearers of truth, ye, Sages, World-Supporters, increase his living wealth whose songs delight you.

6.49.d: पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः सरस्वती वीरपत्नी धियं धात् । ग्नाभिरच्छिद्रं शरणं सजोषा दुराधर्षं गृणते शर्म यंसत् ॥
6.49.e: So may Sarasvatī, the Hero's Consort, brisk with rare life, the lightning's Child, inspire us,  And, with the Dames accordant, give the singer a refuge unassailable and flawless.

6.49.d: पथस्पथः परिपतिं वचस्या कामेन कृतो अभ्यानळर्कम् । स नो रासच्छुरुधश्चन्द्राग्रा धियंधियं सीषधाति प्र पूषा ॥
6.49.e: I praise with eloquence him who guards all pathways. He, when his love impelled him, went to Arka.  May he vouchsafe us gear with gold to grace it: may Pūṣan make each prayer of ours efective.

6.49.d: प्रथमभाजं यशसं वयोधां सुपाणिं देवं सुगभस्तिमृभ्वम् । होता यक्षद्यजतं पस्त्यानामग्निस्त्वष्टारं सुहवं विभावा ॥
6.49.e: May Herald Agni, fulgent, bring for worship Tvaṣṭar adored, in homes and swift to listen,  Glorious, first to share, the life-bestower, the ever active God, fair-armed, fair-handed.

6.49.d: भुवनस्य पितरं गीर्भिराभी रुद्रं दिवा वर्धया रुद्रमक्तौ । बृहन्तमृष्वमजरं सुषुम्नमृधग्घुवेम कविनेषितासः ॥
6.49.e: Rudra by day, Rudra at night we honour with these our songs, the Universe's Father.  Him great and lofty, blissful, undecaying let us call specially as the Sage impels us.

6.49.d: आ युवानः कवयो यज्ञियासो मरुतो गन्त गृणतो वरस्याम् । अचित्रं चिद्धि जिन्वथा वृधन्त इत्था नक्षन्तो नरो अङ्गिरस्वत् ॥
6.49.e: Ye who are youthful, wise, and meet for worship, come, Martits, to the longing of the singer.  Coming, as erst to Aṅgiras, O Heroes, ye animate and quicken e’en the desert.

6.49.d: प्र वीराय प्र तवसे तुरायाजा यूथेव पशुरक्षिरस्तम् । स पिस्पृशति तन्वि श्रुतस्य स्तृभिर्न नाकं वचनस्य विपः ॥
6.49.e: Even as the herdsman driveth home his cattle, I urge my songs to him the strong swift Hero  May he, the glorious, lay upon his body the singer's hymns, as stars bedeck the heaven.

6.49.d: यो रजांसि विममे पार्थिवानि त्रिश्चिद्विष्णुर्मनवे बाधिताय । तस्य ते शर्मन्नुपदद्यमाने राया मदेम तन्वा३ तना च ॥
6.49.e: He who for man's behoof in his afiliction thrice measured out the earthly regions, Viṣṇu-  When one so great as thou affordeth shelter, may we with wealth and with ourselves be happy.

6.49.d: तन्नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यो अद्भिरर्कैस्तत्पर्वतस्तत्सविता चनो धात् । तदोषधीभिरभि रातिषाचो भगः पुरंधिर्जिन्वतु प्र राये ॥
6.49.e: Sweet be this song of mine to Ahibudhnya, Parvata, Savitar, with Floods and Lightnings;  Sweet, with the Plants, to Gods who seek oblations. May liberal Bhaga speed us on to riches.

6.49.d: नु नो रयिं रथ्यं चर्षणिप्रां पुरुवीरं मह ऋतस्य गोपाम् । क्षयं दाताजरं येन जनान्त्स्पृधो अदेवीरभि च क्रमाम विश आदेवीरभ्य१श्नवाम ॥
6.49.e: Give riches borne on cars, with many heroes, contenting men, the guard of mighty Order.  Give us a lasting home that we may battle with godless bands of men who fight against us, and meet with tribes to whom the Gods are gracious.

6.50.d: हुवे वो देवीमदितिं नमोभिर्मृळीकाय वरुणं मित्रमग्निम् । अभिक्षदामर्यमणं सुशेवं त्रातॄन्देवान्त्सवितारं भगं च ॥
6.50.e: I CALL with prayers on Aditi your Goddess, on Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa for favour,  On Aryaman who gives unasked, the gracious, on Gods who save, on Savitar and Bhaga.

6.50.d: सुज्योतिषः सूर्य दक्षपितॄननागास्त्वे सुमहो वीहि देवान् । द्विजन्मानो य ऋतसापः सत्याः स्वर्वन्तो यजता अग्निजिह्वाः ॥
6.50.e: Visit, to prove us free from sin, O Sūrya Lord of great might, the bright Gods sprung from Dakṣa,  Twice-born and true, observing sacred duties, Holy and full of light, whose tongue is Agni.

6.50.d: उत द्यावापृथिवी क्षत्रमुरु बृहद्रोदसी शरणं सुषुम्ने । महस्करथो वरिवो यथा नोऽस्मे क्षयाय धिषणे अनेहः ॥
6.50.e: And, O ye Heaven and Earth, a wide dominion, O ye most blissful Worlds, our lofty shelter,  Give ample room and freedom for our dwelling, a home, ye Hemispheres, which none may rival.

6.50.d: आ नो रुद्रस्य सूनवो नमन्तामद्या हूतासो वसवोऽधृष्टाः । यदीमर्भे महति वा हितासो बाधे मरुतो अह्वाम देवान् ॥
6.50.e: This day invited may the Sons of Rudra, resistless, excellent, stoop down to meet us;  For, when beset with slight or sore affliction, we ever call upon the Gods, the Maruts;

6.50.d: मिम्यक्ष येषु रोदसी नु देवी सिषक्ति पूषा अभ्यर्धयज्वा । श्रुत्वा हवं मरुतो यद्ध याथ भूमा रेजन्ते अध्वनि प्रविक्ते ॥
6.50.e: To whom the Goddess Rodasī clings closely, whom Pūṣan follows bringing ample bounty.  What time ye hear our call and come, O Maruts, upon your separate path all creatures tremble.

6.50.d: अभि त्यं वीरं गिर्वणसमर्चेन्द्रं ब्रह्मणा जरितर्नवेन । श्रवदिद्धवमुप च स्तवानो रासद्वाजाँ उप महो गृणानः ॥
6.50.e: With a new hymn extol, O thou who singest, the Lover of the Song, the Hero Indra.  May he, exalted, hear our invocation, and grant us mighty wealth and strength when lauded.

6.50.d: ओमानमापो मानुषीरमृक्तं धात तोकाय तनयाय शं योः । यूयं हि ष्ठा भिषजो मातृतमा विश्वस्य स्थातुर्जगतो जनित्रीः ॥
6.50.e: Give full protection, Friends of man, ye Waters, in peace and trouble, to our sons and grandsons.  For ye are our most motherly physicians, parents of all that standeth, all that moveth.

6.50.d: आ नो देवः सविता त्रायमाणो हिरण्यपाणिर्यजतो जगम्यात् । यो दत्रवाँ उषसो न प्रतीकं व्यूर्णुते दाशुषे वार्याणि ॥
6.50.e: May Savitar come hither and approach us, the God who rescues, Holy, goldenhanded,  The God who, bounteous as the face of Morning, discloses precious gifts for him who worships.

6.50.d: उत त्वं सूनो सहसो नो अद्या देवाँ अस्मिन्नध्वरे ववृत्याः । स्यामहं ते सदमिद्रातौ तव स्यामग्नेऽवसा सुवीरः ॥
6.50.e: And thou, O Son of Strength, do thou turn hither the Gods to-day to this our holy service.  May I for evermore enjoy thy bounty and, Agni, by thy grace be rich in heroes.

6.50.d: उत त्या मे हवमा जग्म्यातं नासत्या धीभिर्युवमङ्ग विप्रा । अत्रिं न महस्तमसोऽमुमुक्तं तूर्वतं नरा दुरितादभीके ॥
6.50.e: Come also to my call, O ye Nāsatyas, yea, verily, through my prayers, ye Holy Sages.  As from great darkness ye delivered Atri, protect us, Chiefs, from danger in the conflict.

6.50.d: ते नो रायो द्युमतो वाजवतो दातारो भूत नृवतः पुरुक्षोः । दशस्यन्तो दिव्याः पार्थिवासो गोजाता अप्या मृळता च देवाः ॥
6.50.e: O Gods, bestow upon us riches, splendid with strength and heroes, bringing food in plenty.  Be gracious, helpful Gods of earth, of heaven, born of the Cow, and dwellers in the waters.

6.50.d: ते नो रुद्रः सरस्वती सजोषा मीळ्हुष्मन्तो विष्णुर्मृळन्तु वायुः । ऋभुक्षा वाजो दैव्यो विधाता पर्जन्यावाता पिप्यतामिषं नः ॥
6.50.e: May Rudra and Sarasvatī, accordant, Viṣṇu and Vāyu, pour down gifts and bless us;  Ṛbhukṣan, Vāja, and divine Vidhatar, Parjanya, Vāta make our food abundant.

6.50.d: उत स्य देवः सविता भगो नोऽपां नपादवतु दानु पप्रिः । त्वष्टा देवेभिर्जनिभिः सजोषा द्यौर्देवेभिः पृथिवी समुद्रैः ॥
6.50.e: May this God Savitar, the Lord, the Offspring of Waters, pouring down his dew be gracious,  And, with the Gods and Dames accordant, Tvaṣṭar; Dyaus with the Gods and Prthivi with oceans.

6.50.d: उत नोऽहिर्बुध्न्यः शृणोत्वज एकपात्पृथिवी समुद्रः । विश्वे देवा ऋतावृधो हुवानाः स्तुता मन्त्राः कविशस्ता अवन्तु ॥
6.50.e: May Aja-Ekapād and Ahibudhnya, and Earth and Ocean hear our invocation;  All Gods who strengthen Law, invoked and lauded, and holy texts uttered by sages, help us.

6.50.d: एवा नपातो मम तस्य धीभिर्भरद्वाजा अभ्यर्चन्त्यर्कैः । ग्ना हुतासो वसवोऽधृष्टा विश्वे स्तुतासो भूता यजत्राः ॥
6.50.e: So with my thoughts and hymns of praise the children of Bharadvāja sing aloud to please you.  The Dames invoked, and the resistless Vasus, and all ye Holy Ones have been exalted.

6.51.d: उदु त्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोराँ एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धम् । ऋतस्य शुचि दर्शतमनीकं रुक्मो न दिव उदिता व्यद्यौत् ॥
6.51.e: THAT mighty eye of Varuṇa and Mitra, infallible and dear, is moving upward.  The pure and lovely face of holy Order hath shone like gold of heaven in its arising.

6.51.d: वेद यस्त्रीणि विदथान्येषां देवानां जन्म सनुतरा च विप्रः । ऋजु मर्तेषु वृजिना च पश्यन्नभि चष्टे सूरो अर्य एवान् ॥
6.51.e: The Sage who knows these Gods’ three ranks and orders, and all their generations near and distant,  Beholding good and evil acts of mortals, Sūra marks well the doing of the pious.

6.51.d: स्तुष उ वो मह ऋतस्य गोपानदितिं मित्रं वरुणं सुजातान् । अर्यमणं भगमदब्धधीतीनच्छा वोचे सधन्यः पावकान् ॥
6.51.e: I praise you Guards of mighty Law eternal, Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa, the noble,  Aryaman, Bhaga, all whose thoughts are faithful: hither I call the Bright who share in common.

6.51.d: रिशादसः सत्पतीँरदब्धान्महो राज्ञः सुवसनस्य दातॄन् । यूनः सुक्षत्रान्क्षयतो दिवो नॄनादित्यान्याम्यदितिं दुवोयु ॥
6.51.e: Lords of the brave, infallible, foe-destroyers, great Kings, bestowers of fair homes to dwell in,  Young, Heroes, ruling heaven with strong dominion, Ādityas, Aditi I seek with worship.

6.51.d: द्यौ३ष्पितः पृथिवि मातरध्रुगग्ने भ्रातर्वसवो मृळता नः । विश्व आदित्या अदिते सजोषा अस्मभ्यं शर्म बहुलं वि यन्त ॥
6.51.e: O Heaven our Father, Earth our guileless Mother, O Brother Agni, and ye Vasus, bless us.  Grant us, O Aditi and ye Ādityas, all of one mind, your manifold protection.

6.51.d: मा नो वृकाय वृक्ये समस्मा अघायते रीरधता यजत्राः । यूयं हि ष्ठा रथ्यो नस्तनूनां यूयं दक्षस्य वचसो बभूव ॥
6.51.e: Give us not up to any evil creature, as spoil to wolf or she-wolf, O ye Holy.  For ye are they who guide aright our bodies, ye are the rulers of our speech and vigour.

6.51.d: मा व एनो अन्यकृतं भुजेम मा तत्कर्म वसवो यच्चयध्वे । विश्वस्य हि क्षयथ विश्वदेवाः स्वयं रिपुस्तन्वं रीरिषीष्ट ॥
6.51.e: Let us not suffer for the sin of others, nor do the deed which ye, O Vasus, punish.  Ye, Universal Gods! are all-controllers: may he do harm unto himself who hates Me.

6.51.d: नम इदुग्रं नम आ विवासे नमो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्याम् । नमो देवेभ्यो नम ईश एषां कृतं चिदेनो नमसा विवासे ॥
6.51.e: Mighty is homage: I adopt and use it. Homage hath held in place the earth and heaven.  Homage to Gods! Homage commands and rules them. I banish even committed sin by homage

6.51.d: ऋतस्य वो रथ्यः पूतदक्षानृतस्य पस्त्यसदो अदब्धान् । ताँ आ नमोभिरुरुचक्षसो नॄन्विश्वान्व आ नमे महो यजत्राः ॥
6.51.e: You Furtherers of Law, pure in your spirit, infallible, dwellers in the home of Order,  To you all Heroes mighty and far-seeing I bow me down, O Holy Ones, with homage.

6.51.d: ते हि श्रेष्ठवर्चसस्त उ नस्तिरो विश्वानि दुरिता नयन्ति । सुक्षत्रासो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निर्ऋतधीतयो वक्मराजसत्याः ॥
6.51.e: For these are they who shine with noblest splendour; through all our troubles these conduct us safely-  Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, mighty Rulers, trueminded, faithful to the hymn's controllers.

6.51.d: ते न इन्द्रः पृथिवी क्षाम वर्धन्पूषा भगो अदितिः पञ्च जनाः । सुशर्माणः स्ववसः सुनीथा भवन्तु नः सुत्रात्रासः सुगोपाः ॥
6.51.e: May they, Earth, Aditi, Indra, Bhaga, Pūṣan increase our laud, increase the Fivefold people.  Giving good help, good refuge, goodly guidance, be they our good deliverers, good protectors.

6.51.d: नू सद्मानं दिव्यं नंशि देवा भारद्वाजः सुमतिं याति होता । आसानेभिर्यजमानो मियेधैर्देवानां जन्म वसूयुर्ववन्द ॥
6.51.e: Come now, O Gods, to your celestial station: the Bharadvājas' priest entreats your favour.  He, sacrificing, fain for wealth, hath honoured the Gods vath those who sit and share oblations.

6.51.d: अप त्यं वृजिनं रिपुं स्तेनमग्ने दुराध्यम् । दविष्ठमस्य सत्पते कृधी सुगम् ॥
6.51.e: Agni, drive thou the wicked foe, the evil-hearted thief away,  Far, far, Lord of the brave I and give us easy paths.

6.51.d: ग्रावाणः सोम नो हि कं सखित्वनाय वावशुः । जही न्य१त्रिणं पणिं वृको हि षः ॥
6.51.e: Soma, these pressing-stones have called aloud to win thee for our Friend.  Destroy the greedy Paṇi, for a wolf is he.

6.51.d: यूयं हि ष्ठा सुदानव इन्द्रज्येष्ठा अभिद्यवः । कर्ता नो अध्वन्ना सुगं गोपा अमा ॥
6.51.e: Ye, O most bountiful, are they who, led by Indra, seek the sky.  Give us good paths for travel: guard us ivell at home.

6.51.d: अपि पन्थामगन्महि स्वस्तिगामनेहसम् । येन विश्वाः परि द्विषो वृणक्ति विन्दते वसु ॥
6.51.e: Now have we entered on the road that leads to bliss, without a foe,  The road whereon a man escapes all enemies and gathers wealth.

6.52.d: न तद्दिवा न पृथिव्यानु मन्ये न यज्ञेन नोत शमीभिराभिः । उब्जन्तु तं सुभ्व१ः पर्वतासो नि हीयतामतियाजस्य यष्टा ॥
6.52.e: THIS I allow not in the earth or heaven, at sacrifice or in these holy duties.  May the huge mountains crush him down: degraded be Atiyaja's sacrificing patron.

6.52.d: अति वा यो मरुतो मन्यते नो ब्रह्म वा यः क्रियमाणं निनित्सात् । तपूंषि तस्मै वृजिनानि सन्तु ब्रह्मद्विषमभि तं शोचतु द्यौः ॥
6.52.e: Or he who holds us in contempt, O Maruts, or seeks to blame the prayer that we are making,  May agonies of burning be his portion. May the sky scorch the man who hates devotion.

6.52.d: किमङ्ग त्वा ब्रह्मणः सोम गोपां किमङ्ग त्वाहुरभिशस्तिपां नः । किमङ्ग नः पश्यसि निद्यमानान्ब्रह्मद्विषे तपुषिं हेतिमस्य ॥
6.52.e: Why then, O Soma, do they call thee keeper of prayer? Why then our guardian from reproaches?  Why then beholdest thou how men revile us? Cast thy hot dart at him who hates devotion.

6.52.d: अवन्तु मामुषसो जायमाना अवन्तु मा सिन्धवः पिन्वमानाः । अवन्तु मा पर्वतासो ध्रुवासोऽवन्तु मा पितरो देवहूतौ ॥
6.52.e: May Mornings as they spring to life, protect me, and may the Rivers as they swell preserve me.  My guardians be the firmly-seated mountains: the Fathers, when I call on Gods, defend me!

6.52.d: विश्वदानीं सुमनसः स्याम पश्येम नु सूर्यमुच्चरन्तम् । तथा करद्वसुपतिर्वसूनां देवाँ ओहानोऽवसागमिष्ठः ॥
6.52.e: Through all our days may we be healthy. minded, and look upon the Sun when he arises.  Grant this the Treasure-Lord of treasures, coming, observant, oftenest of Gods, with succour!

6.52.d: इन्द्रो नेदिष्ठमवसागमिष्ठः सरस्वती सिन्धुभिः पिन्वमाना । पर्जन्यो न ओषधीभिर्मयोभुरग्निः सुशंसः सुहवः पितेव ॥
6.52.e: Most near, most oft comes Indra with protection, and she Sarasvatī, who swells with rivers -  Parjanya, bringing health with herbs, and Agni, well lauded swift to listen, like a father.

6.52.d: विश्वे देवास आ गत शृणुता म इमं हवम् । एदं बर्हिर्नि षीदत ॥
6.52.e: Hear this mine invocation; come hither, O Universal Gods,  Be seated on this holy grass.

6.52.d: यो वो देवा घृतस्नुना हव्येन प्रतिभूषति । तं विश्व उप गच्छथ ॥
6.52.e: To him who comes to meet you, Gods, with offerings bathed in holy oil-  Approach ye, one and all, to him.

6.52.d: उप नः सूनवो गिरः शृण्वन्त्वमृतस्य ये । सुमृळीका भवन्तु नः ॥
6.52.e: All Sons of Immortality shall listen to the songs we sing,  And be exceeding good to us.

6.52.d: विश्वे देवा ऋतावृध ऋतुभिर्हवनश्रुतः । जुषन्तां युज्यं पयः ॥
6.52.e: May all the Gods who strengthen Law, with Ṛtus, listening to our call,  Be pleased with theit appropriate draught.

6.52.d: स्तोत्रमिन्द्रो मरुद्गणस्त्वष्टृमान्मित्रो अर्यमा । इमा हव्या जुषन्त नः ॥
6.52.e: May Indra, with the Marut host, with Tvaṣṭar, Mitra, Aryaman,  Accept the laud and these our gifts.

6.52.d: इमं नो अग्ने अध्वरं होतर्वयुनशो यज । चिकित्वान्दैव्यं जनम् ॥
6.52.e: O Agni, Priest, as rules ordain, offer this sacrifice of ours,  Remembering the Heavenly Folk.

6.52.d: विश्वे देवाः शृणुतेमं हवं मे ये अन्तरिक्षे य उप द्यवि ष्ठ । ये अग्निजिह्वा उत वा यजत्रा आसद्यास्मिन्बर्हिषि मादयध्वम् ॥
6.52.e: Listen, All-Gods, to this mine invocation, Ye who inhabit heaven, and air's midregions,  All ye, O Holy Ones, whose tongue is Agni, seated upon this sacred grass, be joyful.

6.52.d: विश्वे देवा मम शृण्वन्तु यज्ञिया उभे रोदसी अपां नपाच्च मन्म । मा वो वचांसि परिचक्ष्याणि वोचं सुम्नेष्विद्वो अन्तमा मदेम ॥
6.52.e: May the All-Gods who claim our worship hear my thought; may the two World-halves hear it, and the Waters’ Child.  Let me not utter words that ye may disregard. Closely allied with you may we rejoice in bliss.

6.52.d: ये के च ज्मा महिनो अहिमाया दिवो जज्ञिरे अपां सधस्थे । ते अस्मभ्यमिषये विश्वमायुः क्षप उस्रा वरिवस्यन्तु देवाः ॥
6.52.e: And those who, Mighty, with the wiles of serpents, were born on earth, in heaven, where waters gather-  May they vouchsafe us life of full duration. May the Gods kindly give us nights and mornings.

6.52.d: अग्नीपर्जन्याववतं धियं मेऽस्मिन्हवे सुहवा सुष्टुतिं नः । इळामन्यो जनयद्गर्भमन्यः प्रजावतीरिष आ धत्तमस्मे ॥
6.52.e: At this my call, O Agni and Parjanya, help, swift to hear, my thought and our laudation.  One generates holy food, the other offspring, so grant us food enough with store of children.

6.52.d: स्तीर्णे बर्हिषि समिधाने अग्नौ सूक्तेन महा नमसा विवासे । अस्मिन्नो अद्य विदथे यजत्रा विश्वे देवा हविषि मादयध्वम् ॥
6.52.e: When holy grass is strewn and fire enkindled, with hymn and lowly homage I invite you.  All-Gods, to day in this our great assembly rejoice, ye Holy, in the gifts we offer.

6.53.d: वयमु त्वा पथस्पते रथं न वाजसातये । धिये पूषन्नयुज्महि ॥
6.53.e: LORD of the path, O Pūṣan, we have yoked and bound thee to our hymn,  Even as a car, to win the prize.

6.53.d: अभि नो नर्यं वसु वीरं प्रयतदक्षिणम् । वामं गृहपतिं नय ॥
6.53.e: Bring us the wealth that men require, a manly master of a house,  Free-handed with the liberal meed.

6.53.d: अदित्सन्तं चिदाघृणे पूषन्दानाय चोदय । पणेश्चिद्वि म्रदा मनः ॥
6.53.e: Even him who would not give, do thou,  O glowing Pūṣan, urge to give,  And make the niggard's soul grow soft.

6.53.d: वि पथो वाजसातये चिनुहि वि मृधो जहि । साधन्तामुग्र नो धियः ॥
6.53.e: Clear paths that we may win the prize; scatter our enemies afar.  Strong God, be all our thoughts fulfilled.

6.53.d: परि तृन्धि पणीनामारया हृदया कवे । अथेमस्मभ्यं रन्धय ॥
6.53.e: Penetrate with an awl, O Sage, the hearts of avaricious churls,  And make them subject to our will.

6.53.d: वि पूषन्नारया तुद पणेरिच्छ हृदि प्रियम् । अथेमस्मभ्यं रन्धय ॥
6.53.e: Thrust with thine awl, O Pūṣan: seek that which the niggard's heart holds dear,  And make him subject to our will.

6.53.d: आ रिख किकिरा कृणु पणीनां हृदया कवे । अथेमस्मभ्यं रन्धय ॥
6.53.e: Tear up and read in pieces, Sage, the hearts of avaricious churls,  And make them subject to our will.

6.53.d: यां पूषन्ब्रह्मचोदनीमारां बिभर्ष्याघृणे । तया समस्य हृदयमा रिख किकिरा कृणु ॥
6.53.e: Thou, glowing Pūṣan, carriest an awl that urges men to prayer;  Therewith do thou tear up and rend to shreds the heart of every one.

6.53.d: या ते अष्ट्रा गोओपशाघृणे पशुसाधनी । तस्यास्ते सुम्नमीमहे ॥
6.53.e: Thou bearest, glowing Lord! a goad with horny point that guides the cows  Thence do we seek thy gift of bliss.

6.53.d: उत नो गोषणिं धियमश्वसां वाजसामुत । नृवत्कृणुहि वीतये ॥
6.53.e: And make this hymn of ours produce kine, horses, and a store of wealth  For our delight and use as men.

6.54.d: सं पूषन्विदुषा नय यो अञ्जसानुशासति । य एवेदमिति ब्रवत् ॥
6.54.e: O PUSAN, bring us to the man who knows, who shall direct us straight,  And say unto us, It is here.

6.54.d: समु पूष्णा गमेमहि यो गृहाँ अभिशासति । इम एवेति च ब्रवत् ॥
6.54.e: May we go forth with Pūṣan who shall point the houses out to us,  And say to us, These same are they.

6.54.d: पूष्णश्चक्रं न रिष्यति न कोशोऽव पद्यते । नो अस्य व्यथते पविः ॥
6.54.e: Unharmed is Pūṣan's chariot wheel; the box ne’er falleth to the ground,  Nor doth the loosened felIy shake.

6.54.d: यो अस्मै हविषाविधन्न तं पूषापि मृष्यते । प्रथमो विन्दते वसु ॥
6.54.e: Pūṣan forgetteth not the man who serveth him with offered gift:  That man is first to gather wealth.

6.54.d: पूषा गा अन्वेतु नः पूषा रक्षत्वर्वतः । पूषा वाजं सनोतु नः ॥
6.54.e: May Pūṣan follow near our kine; may Pūṣan keep our horses safe:  May Pūṣan gather gear for us.

6.54.d: पूषन्ननु प्र गा इहि यजमानस्य सुन्वतः । अस्माकं स्तुवतामुत ॥
6.54.e: Follow the kine of him who pours libations out and worships thee;  And ours who sing thee songs of praise.

6.54.d: माकिर्नेशन्माकीं रिषन्माकीं सं शारि केवटे । अथारिष्टाभिरा गहि ॥
6.54.e: Let none be lost, none injured, none sink in a pit and break a limb.  Return with these all safe and sound.

6.54.d: शृण्वन्तं पूषणं वयमिर्यमनष्टवेदसम् । ईशानं राय ईमहे ॥
6.54.e: Pūṣan who listens to our prayers, the Strong whose wealth is never lost,  The Lord of riches, we implore.

6.54.d: पूषन्तव व्रते वयं न रिष्येम कदा चन । स्तोतारस्त इह स्मसि ॥
6.54.e: Secure in thy protecting care, O Pūṣan, never may we fail.  We here are they who sing thy praise.

6.54.d: परि पूषा परस्ताद्धस्तं दधातु दक्षिणम् । पुनर्नो नष्टमाजतु ॥
6.54.e: From out the distance, far and wide, may Pūṣan stretch his right hand forth,  And drive our lost again to us.

6.55.d: एहि वां विमुचो नपादाघृणे सं सचावहै । रथीर्ऋतस्य नो भव ॥
6.55.e: SON of Deliverance, come, bright God!  Let us twain go together: be our charioteer of sacrifice.

6.55.d: रथीतमं कपर्दिनमीशानं राधसो महः । रायः सखायमीमहे ॥
6.55.e: We pray for wealth to thee most skilled of charioteers, with braided hair,  Lord of great riches, and our Friend.

6.55.d: रायो धारास्याघृणे वसो राशिरजाश्व । धीवतोधीवतः सखा ॥
6.55.e: Bright God whose steeds are goats, thou art a stream of wealth, a treasure-heap,  The Friend of every pious man.

6.55.d: पूषणं न्व१जाश्वमुप स्तोषाम वाजिनम् । स्वसुर्यो जार उच्यते ॥
6.55.e: Pūṣan, who driveth goats for steeds, the strong and Mighty, who is called  His Sister's lover, will we laud.

6.55.d: मातुर्दिधिषुमब्रवं स्वसुर्जारः शृणोतु नः । भ्रातेन्द्रस्य सखा मम ॥
6.55.e: His Mother's suitor I address. May he who loves his Sister hear,  Brother of Indra, and my Friend.

6.55.d: आजासः पूषणं रथे निशृम्भास्ते जनश्रियम् । देवं वहन्तु बिभ्रतः ॥
6.55.e: May the sure-footed goats come nigh, conveying Pūṣan on his car,  The God who visiteth mankind.

6.56.d: य एनमादिदेशति करम्भादिति पूषणम् । न तेन देव आदिशे ॥
6.56.e: WHOSO remembers Pūṣan as cater of mingled curd and meal  Need think no more upon the God.

6.56.d: उत घा स रथीतमः सख्या सत्पतिर्युजा । इन्द्रो वृत्राणि जिघ्नते ॥
6.56.e: And he is best of charioteers. Indra, the hero's Lord, allied  With him as Friend, destroys the foes.

6.56.d: उतादः परुषे गवि सूरश्चक्रं हिरण्ययम् । न्यैरयद्रथीतमः ॥
6.56.e: And there the best of charioteers hath guided through the speckled cloud  The golden wheel of Sūra's car.

6.56.d: यदद्य त्वा पुरुष्टुत ब्रवाम दस्र मन्तुमः । तत्सु नो मन्म साधय ॥
6.56.e: Whate’er we speak this day to thee, Wise, Wondrous God whom many praise,  Give thou fulfilment of our thought.

6.56.d: इमं च नो गवेषणं सातये सीषधो गणम् । आरात्पूषन्नसि श्रुतः ॥
6.56.e: Lead on this company of ours, that longs for kine, to win the spoil:  Thou, Pūṣan, art renowned afar.

6.56.d: आ ते स्वस्तिमीमह आरेअघामुपावसुम् । अद्या च सर्वतातये श्वश्च सर्वतातये ॥
6.56.e: Prosperity we crave from thee, afar from sin and near to wealth,  Tending to perfect happiness both for to. morrow and to-day.

6.57.d: इन्द्रा नु पूषणा वयं सख्याय स्वस्तये । हुवेम वाजसातये ॥
6.57.e: INDRA and Pūṣan will we call for friend ship and prosperity  And for the winning of the spoil.

6.57.d: सोममन्य उपासदत्पातवे चम्वोः सुतम् । करम्भमन्य इच्छति ॥
6.57.e: One by the Soma sits to drink juice which the mortar hath expressed:  The other longs for curd and meal.

6.57.d: अजा अन्यस्य वह्नयो हरी अन्यस्य सम्भृता । ताभ्यां वृत्राणि जिघ्नते ॥
6.57.e: Goats are the team that draws the one: the other hath Bay Steeds at hand;  With both of these he slays the fiends.

6.57.d: यदिन्द्रो अनयद्रितो महीरपो वृषन्तमः । तत्र पूषाभवत्सचा ॥
6.57.e: When Indra, wondrous strong, brought down the streams, the mighty waterfloods,  Pūṣan was standing by his side.

6.57.d: तां पूष्णः सुमतिं वयं वृक्षस्य प्र वयामिव । इन्द्रस्य चा रभामहे ॥
6.57.e: To this, to Pūṣan's favouring love, and Indra's, may we closely cling,  As to a tree's extended bough.

6.57.d: उत्पूषणं युवामहेऽभीशूँरिव सारथिः । मह्या इन्द्रं स्वस्तये ॥
6.57.e: As one who drives a car draws in his reins, may we draw Pūṣan near,  And Indra, for our great success.

6.58.d: शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि । विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥
6.58.e: LIKE heaven art thou: one form is bright, one holy, like Day and Night dissimilar in colour.  All magic powers thou aidest, self-depen. dent! Auspicious be thy bounty here, O Pūṣan.

6.58.d: अजाश्वः पशुपा वाजपस्त्यो धियंजिन्वो भुवने विश्वे अर्पितः । अष्ट्रां पूषा शिथिरामुद्वरीवृजत्संचक्षाणो भुवना देव ईयते ॥
6.58.e: Goat-borne, the guard of cattle, he whose home is strength, inspirer of the hymn, set over all the world;  Brandishing here and there his lightly. moving goad, beholding every creature, Pūṣan, God, goes forth.

6.58.d: यास्ते पूषन्नावो अन्तः समुद्रे हिरण्ययीरन्तरिक्षे चरन्ति । ताभिर्यासि दूत्यां सूर्यस्य कामेन कृत श्रव इच्छमानः ॥
6.58.e: O Pūṣan, with thy golden ships that travel across the ocean, in the air's mid-region,  Thou goest on an embassy to Sūrya, subdued by love, desirous of the glory.

6.58.d: पूषा सुबन्धुर्दिव आ पृथिव्या इळस्पतिर्मघवा दस्मवर्चाः । यं देवासो अददुः सूर्यायै कामेन कृतं तवसं स्वञ्चम् ॥
6.58.e: Near kinsman of the heaven and earth is Pūṣan, liberal, Lord of food, of wondrous iustre,  Whom strong and vigorous and swiftlymoving, subdued by love, the Deities gave to Sūrya.

6.59.d: प्र नु वोचा सुतेषु वां वीर्या३ यानि चक्रथुः । हतासो वां पितरो देवशत्रव इन्द्राग्नी जीवथो युवम् ॥
6.59.e: I WILL declare, while juices flow, the manly deeds that ye have done:  Your Fathers, enemies of Gods, were smitten down, and, Indra-Agni, ye survive.

6.59.d: बळित्था महिमा वामिन्द्राग्नी पनिष्ठ आ । समानो वां जनिता भ्रातरा युवं यमाविहेहमातरा ॥
6.59.e: Thus, Indra-Agnip verily your greatness merits loftiest praise,  Sprung from one common Father, brothers, twins are ye; your Mother is in every place.

6.59.d: ओकिवांसा सुते सचाँ अश्वा सप्ती इवादने । इन्द्रा न्व१ग्नी अवसेह वज्रिणा वयं देवा हवामहे ॥
6.59.e: These who delight in flowing juice, like fellow horses at their food,  Indra and Agni, Gods armed with the thunderbolt, we call this day to come with help.

6.59.d: य इन्द्राग्नी सुतेषु वां स्तवत्तेष्वृतावृधा । जोषवाकं वदतः पज्रहोषिणा न देवा भसथश्चन ॥
6.59.e: Indra and Agni, Friends of Law, served with rich gifts, your speech is kind  To him who praises you while these libations flow: that man, O Gods, ye ne’er consume.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी को अस्य वां देवौ मर्तश्चिकेतति । विषूचो अश्वान्युयुजान ईयत एकः समान आ रथे ॥
6.59.e: What mortal understands, O Gods, Indra and Agni, this your way?  One of you, yoking Steeds that move to every side, advances in your common car.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी अपादियं पूर्वागात्पद्वतीभ्यः । हित्वी शिरो जिह्वया वावदच्चरत्त्रिंशत्पदा न्यक्रमीत् ॥
6.59.e: First, Indra-Agni, hath this Maid come footless unto those with feet.  Stretching her head and speaking loudly with her tongue, she hath gone downward thirty steps.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी आ हि तन्वते नरो धन्वानि बाह्वोः । मा नो अस्मिन्महाधने परा वर्क्तं गविष्टिषु ॥
6.59.e: E’en now, O Indra-Agni, men hold in their arms and stretch their bows.  Desert us not in this great fray, in battles for the sake of kine.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी तपन्ति माघा अर्यो अरातयः । अप द्वेषांस्या कृतं युयुतं सूर्यादधि ॥
6.59.e: The foeman's sinful enmities, Indra and Agni, vex me sore.  Drive those who hate me far away, and keep them distant from the Sun.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी युवोरपि वसु दिव्यानि पार्थिवा । आ न इह प्र यच्छतं रयिं विश्वायुपोषसम् ॥
6.59.e: Indra and Agni, yours are all the treasures of the heavens and earth.  Here give ye us the opulence that prospers every living man.

6.59.d: इन्द्राग्नी उक्थवाहसा स्तोमेभिर्हवनश्रुता । विश्वाभिर्गीर्भिरा गतमस्य सोमस्य पीतये ॥
6.59.e: O Indra-Agni, who accept the laud, and hear us for our praise,  Come near us, drawn by all our songs, to drink of this our Soma juice.

6.60.d: श्नथद्वृत्रमुत सनोति वाजमिन्द्रा यो अग्नी सहुरी सपर्यात् । इरज्यन्ता वसव्यस्य भूरेः सहस्तमा सहसा वाजयन्ता ॥
6.60.e: HE slays the foe and wins the spoil who worships Indra and Agni, strong and mighty Heroes,  Who rule as Sovrans over ample riches, victorious, showing forth their power in conquest.

6.60.d: ता योधिष्टमभि गा इन्द्र नूनमपः स्वरुषसो अग्न ऊळ्हाः । दिशः स्वरुषस इन्द्र चित्रा अपो गा अग्ने युवसे नियुत्वान् ॥
6.60.e: So battle now, O Indra and thou, Agni, for cows and waters, sunlight, stolen Mornings.  Team-borne, thou makest kine thine own, O Agni: thou, Indra, light, Dawns, regions, wondrous waters.

6.60.d: आ वृत्रहणा वृत्रहभिः शुष्मैरिन्द्र यातं नमोभिरग्ने अर्वाक् । युवं राधोभिरकवेभिरिन्द्राग्ने अस्मे भवतमुत्तमेभिः ॥
6.60.e: With Vṛtra-slaying might, Indra and Agni, come, drawn by homage, O ye Vṛtra-slayers.  Indra and Agni, show yourselves among us with your supreme and unrestricted bounties.

6.60.d: ता हुवे ययोरिदं पप्ने विश्वं पुरा कृतम् । इन्द्राग्नी न मर्धतः ॥
6.60.e: I call the Twain whose deeds of old have all been famed in ancient days  O Indra-Agni, harm us not.

6.60.d: उग्रा विघनिना मृध इन्द्राग्नी हवामहे । ता नो मृळात ईदृशे ॥
6.60.e: The Strong, the scatterers of the foe, Indra and Agni, we invoke;  May they be kind to one like me.

6.60.d: हतो वृत्राण्यार्या हतो दासानि सत्पती । हतो विश्वा अप द्विषः ॥
6.60.e: They slay our Ārya foes, these Lords of heroes, slay our Dasyu foes  And drive our enemies away.

6.60.d: इन्द्राग्नी युवामिमे३ऽभि स्तोमा अनूषत । पिबतं शम्भुवा सुतम् ॥
6.60.e: Indra and Agni, these our songs of praise have sounded forth to you:  Ye who bring blessings! drink the juice.

6.60.d: या वां सन्ति पुरुस्पृहो नियुतो दाशुषे नरा । इन्द्राग्नी ताभिरा गतम् ॥
6.60.e: Come, Indra-Agni, with those teams, desired of many, which ye have,  O Heroes, for the worshipper.

6.60.d: ताभिरा गच्छतं नरोपेदं सवनं सुतम् । इन्द्राग्नी सोमपीतये ॥
6.60.e: With those to this libation poured, ye Heroes, Indra-Agni, come:  Come ye to drink the Soma juice.

6.60.d: तमीळिष्व यो अर्चिषा वना विश्वा परिष्वजत् । कृष्णा कृणोति जिह्वया ॥
6.60.e: Glorify him who compasses all forests with his glowing flame,  And leaves them blackened with his tongue.

6.60.d: य इद्ध आविवासति सुम्नमिन्द्रस्य मर्त्यः । द्युम्नाय सुतरा अपः ॥
6.60.e: He who gains Indra's bliss with fire enkindled finds an easy way  Over the floods to happiness.

6.60.d: ता नो वाजवतीरिष आशून्पिपृतमर्वतः । इन्द्रमग्निं च वोळ्हवे ॥
6.60.e: Give us fleet coursers to convey Indra and Agni, and bestow  Abundant strengthening food on us.

6.60.d: उभा वामिन्द्राग्नी आहुवध्या उभा राधसः सह मादयध्यै । उभा दाताराविषां रयीणामुभा वाजस्य सातये हुवे वाम् ॥
6.60.e: Indra and Agni, I will call you hither and make you joyful with the gifts I offer.  Ye Twain are givers both of food and riches: to win me strength and vigour I invoke you.

6.60.d: आ नो गव्येभिरश्व्यैर्वसव्यै३रुप गच्छतम् । सखायौ देवौ सख्याय शम्भुवेन्द्राग्नी ता हवामहे ॥
6.60.e: Come unto us with riches, come with wealth in horses and in kine.  Indra and Agni, we invoke you both, the Gods, as Friends for friendship, bringing bliss.

6.60.d: इन्द्राग्नी शृणुतं हवं यजमानस्य सुन्वतः । वीतं हव्यान्या गतं पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ॥
6.60.e: Indra and Agni, hear his call who worships. with libations poured.  Come and enjoy the offerings, drink the sweetly-flavoured Soma juice.

6.61.d: इयमददाद्रभसमृणच्युतं दिवोदासं वध्र्यश्वाय दाशुषे । या शश्वन्तमाचखादावसं पणिं ता ते दात्राणि तविषा सरस्वति ॥
6.61.e: To Vadhryasva when. be worshipped her with gifts she gave fierce Divodāsa, canceller of debts.  Consumer of the churlish niggard, one and all, thine, O Sarasvatī, are these effectual boons.

6.61.d: इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः । पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवासेम धीतिभिः ॥
6.61.e: She with her might, like one who digs for lotus-stems, hath burst with her strong waves the ridges of the hills.  Let us invite with songs and holy hymns for help Sarasvatī who slayeth the Paravatas.

6.61.d: सरस्वति देवनिदो नि बर्हय प्रजां विश्वस्य बृसयस्य मायिनः । उत क्षितिभ्योऽवनीरविन्दो विषमेभ्यो अस्रवो वाजिनीवति ॥
6.61.e: Thou castest down, Sarasvatī, those who scorned the Gods, the brood of every Bṛsaya skilled in magic arts.  Thou hast discovered rivers for the tribes of men, and, rich in wealth! made poison flow away from them.

6.61.d: प्र णो देवी सरस्वती वाजेभिर्वाजिनीवती । धीनामवित्र्यवतु ॥
6.61.e: May the divine Sarasvatī, rich in her wealth, protect us well,  Furthering all our thoughts with might

6.61.d: यस्त्वा देवि सरस्वत्युपब्रूते धने हिते । इन्द्रं न वृत्रतूर्ये ॥
6.61.e: Whoso, divine Sarasvatī, invokes thee where the prize is set,  Like Indra when he smites the foe.

6.61.d: त्वं देवि सरस्वत्यवा वाजेषु वाजिनि । रदा पूषेव नः सनिम् ॥
6.61.e: Aid us, divine Sarasvad, thou who art strong in wealth and power  Like Pūṣan, give us opulence.

6.61.d: उत स्या नः सरस्वती घोरा हिरण्यवर्तनिः । वृत्रघ्नी वष्टि सुष्टुतिम् ॥
6.61.e: Yea, this divine Sarasvatī, terrible with her golden path,  Foe-slayer, claims our eulogy.
Whose limitless unbroken flood, swift-moving with a rapid rush,  Comes onward with tempestuous roar.

6.61.d: सा नो विश्वा अति द्विषः स्वसॄरन्या ऋतावरी । अतन्नहेव सूर्यः ॥
6.61.e: She hath spread us beyond all foes, beyond her Sisters, Holy One,  As Sūrya spreadeth out the days.

6.61.d: उत नः प्रिया प्रियासु सप्तस्वसा सुजुष्टा । सरस्वती स्तोम्या भूत् ॥
6.61.e: Yea, she most dear amid dear stream, Seven-sistered, graciously inclined,  Sarasvatī hath earned our praise.

6.61.d: आपप्रुषी पार्थिवान्युरु रजो अन्तरिक्षम् । सरस्वती निदस्पातु ॥
6.61.e: Guard us from hate Sarasvatī, she who hath filled the realms of earth,  And that wide tract, the firmament!

6.61.d: त्रिषधस्था सप्तधातुः पञ्च जाता वर्धयन्ती । वाजेवाजे हव्या भूत् ॥
6.61.e: Seven-sistered, sprung from threefold source, the Five Tribes' prosperer, she must be  Invoked in every deed of might.

6.61.d: प्र या महिम्ना महिनासु चेकिते द्युम्नेभिरन्या अपसामपस्तमा । रथ इव बृहती विभ्वने कृतोपस्तुत्या चिकितुषा सरस्वती ॥
6.61.e: Marked out by majesty among the Mighty Ones, in glory swifter than the other rapid Streams,  Created vast for victory like a chariot, Sarasvatī must be extolled by every sage.

6.61.d: सरस्वत्यभि नो नेषि वस्यो माप स्फरीः पयसा मा न आ धक् । जुषस्व नः सख्या वेश्या च मा त्वत्क्षेत्राण्यरणानि गन्म ॥
6.61.e: Guide us, Sarasvatī, to glorious treasure: refuse us not thy milk, nor spurn us from thee.  Gladly accept our friendship and obedience: let us not go from thee to distant countries.

6.62.d: स्तुषे नरा दिवो अस्य प्रसन्ताश्विना हुवे जरमाणो अर्कैः । या सद्य उस्रा व्युषि ज्मो अन्तान्युयूषतः पर्युरू वरांसि ॥
6.62.e: I LAUD the Heroes Twain, this heaven's Controllers: singing with songs of praise I call the Aśvins,  Fain in a moment, when the morns are breaking, to part the earth's ends and the spacious regions.

6.62.d: ता यज्ञमा शुचिभिश्चक्रमाणा रथस्य भानुं रुरुचू रजोभिः । पुरू वरांस्यमिता मिमानापो धन्वान्यति याथो अज्रान् ॥
6.62.e: Moving to sacrifice through realms of lustre they light the radiance of the car that bears them.  Traversing many wide unmeasured spaces, over the wastes ye pass, and fields, and waters.

6.62.d: ता ह त्यद्वर्तिर्यदरध्रमुग्रेत्था धिय ऊहथुः शश्वदश्वैः । मनोजवेभिरिषिरैः शयध्यै परि व्यथिर्दाशुषो मर्त्यस्य ॥
6.62.e: Ye to that bounteous path of yours, ye mighty, have ever borne away our thoughts with horses,  Mind-swift and full of vigour, that the trouble of man who offers gifts might cease and slumber.

6.62.d: ता नव्यसो जरमाणस्य मन्मोप भूषतो युयुजानसप्ती । शुभं पृक्षमिषमूर्जं वहन्ता होता यक्षत्प्रत्नो अध्रुग्युवाना ॥
6.62.e: So ye, when ye have yoked your chariothorses, come to the hymn of the most recent singer.  Our true and ancient Herald Priest shall bring you, the Youthful, bearing splendour, food, and vigour.

6.62.d: ता वल्गू दस्रा पुरुशाकतमा प्रत्ना नव्यसा वचसा विवासे । या शंसते स्तुवते शम्भविष्ठा बभूवतुर्गृणते चित्रराती ॥
6.62.e: With newest hymn I call those Wonder-Workers, ancient and brilliant, and exceeding mighty,  Bringers of bliss to him who lauds and praises, bestowing varied bounties on the singer.

6.62.d: ता भुज्युं विभिरद्भ्यः समुद्रात्तुग्रस्य सूनुमूहथू रजोभिः । अरेणुभिर्योजनेभिर्भुजन्ता पतत्रिभिरर्णसो निरुपस्थात् ॥
6.62.e: So ye, with birds, out of the sea and waters bore Bhujyu, son of Tugra, through the regions.  Speeding with winged steeds through dustless spaces, out of the bosom of the flood they bore him.

6.62.d: वि जयुषा रथ्या यातमद्रिं श्रुतं हवं वृषणा वध्रिमत्याः । दशस्यन्ता शयवे पिप्यथुर्गामिति च्यवाना सुमतिं भुरण्यू ॥
6.62.e: Victors, car-borne, ye rent the rock asunder: Bulls, heard the calling of the eunuch's consort.  Bounteous, ye filled the cow with milk for Śayu: thus, swift and zealous Ones, ye showed your favour.

6.62.d: यद्रोदसी प्रदिवो अस्ति भूमा हेळो देवानामुत मर्त्यत्रा । तदादित्या वसवो रुद्रियासो रक्षोयुजे तपुरघं दधात ॥
6.62.e: Whate’er from olden time, Heaven, Earth! existeth great object of the wrath of Gods and mortals,  Make that, Ādityas, Vasus, sons of Rudra, an evil brand to one allied with demons.

6.62.d: य ईं राजानावृतुथा विदधद्रजसो मित्रो वरुणश्चिकेतत् । गम्भीराय रक्षसे हेतिमस्य द्रोघाय चिद्वचस आनवाय ॥
6.62.e: May he who knows, as Varuṇa and Mitra, air's realm, appointing both the Kings in season,  Against the secret fiend cast forth his weapon, against the lying words that strangers utter.

6.62.d: अन्तरैश्चक्रैस्तनयाय वर्तिर्द्युमता यातं नृवता रथेन । सनुत्येन त्यजसा मर्त्यस्य वनुष्यतामपि शीर्षा ववृक्तम् ॥
6.62.e: Come to our home with friendly wheels, for offipring; come on your radiant chariot rich in heroes.  Strike off, ye Twain, the heads of our assailants who with man's treacherous attack approach us.

6.62.d: आ परमाभिरुत मध्यमाभिर्नियुद्भिर्यातमवमाभिरर्वाक् । दृळ्हस्य चिद्गोमतो वि व्रजस्य दुरो वर्तं गृणते चित्रराती ॥
6.62.e: Come hitherward to us with teams of horses, the highest and the midmost and the lowest.  Bountiful Lords, throw open to the singer doors e’en of the firm-closed stall of cattle.

6.63.d: क्व१ त्या वल्गू पुरुहूताद्य दूतो न स्तोमोऽविदन्नमस्वान् । आ यो अर्वाङ्नासत्या ववर्त प्रेष्ठा ह्यसथो अस्य मन्मन् ॥
6.63.e: WHERE hath the hymn with reverence, like an envoy, found both fair Gods to-day, invoked of many-  Hymn that hath brought the two Nāsatyas hither? To this man's thought be ye, both Gods, most friendly.

6.63.d: अरं मे गन्तं हवनायास्मै गृणाना यथा पिबाथो अन्धः । परि ह त्यद्वर्तिर्याथो रिषो न यत्परो नान्तरस्तुतुर्यात् ॥
6.63.e: Come readily to this mine invocation, lauded with songs, that ye may drink the juices.  Compass this house to keep it from the foeman, that none may force it, either near or distant.

6.63.d: अकारि वामन्धसो वरीमन्नस्तारि बर्हिः सुप्रायणतमम् । उत्तानहस्तो युवयुर्ववन्दा वां नक्षन्तो अद्रय आञ्जन् ॥
6.63.e: Juice in wide room hath been prepared to feast you: for you the grass is strewn, most soft to tread on.  With lifted hands your servant hath adored you. Yearningfor you the press-stones shed the liquid.

6.63.d: ऊर्ध्वो वामग्निरध्वरेष्वस्थात्प्र रातिरेति जूर्णिनी घृताची । प्र होता गूर्तमना उराणोऽयुक्त यो नासत्या हवीमन् ॥
6.63.e: Agni uplifts him at your sacrifices: forth goes the oblation dropping oil and glowing.  Up stands the grateful-minded priest, elected, appointed to invoke the two Nāsatyas.

6.63.d: अधि श्रिये दुहिता सूर्यस्य रथं तस्थौ पुरुभुजा शतोतिम् । प्र मायाभिर्मायिना भूतमत्र नरा नृतू जनिमन्यज्ञियानाम् ॥
6.63.e: Lords of great wealth! for glory, Sūrya's Daughter mounted your car that brings a hundred succours.  Famed for your magic arts were ye, magicians! amid the race of Gods, ye dancing Heroes!

6.63.d: युवं श्रीभिर्दर्शताभिराभिः शुभे पुष्टिमूहथुः सूर्यायाः । प्र वां वयो वपुषेऽनु पप्तन्नक्षद्वाणी सुष्टुता धिष्ण्या वाम् ॥
6.63.e: Ye Twain, with these your glories fair to look on, brought, to win victory, rich gifts for Sūrya.  After you flew your birds, marvels of beauty: dear to our hearts! the song, well lauded, reached you.

6.63.d: आ वां वयोऽश्वासो वहिष्ठा अभि प्रयो नासत्या वहन्तु । प्र वां रथो मनोजवा असर्जीषः पृक्ष इषिधो अनु पूर्वीः ॥
6.63.e: May your winged coursers, best to draw. Nāsatyas! convey you to the object of your wishes.  Swift as the thought, your car hath been sent onward to food of many a sort and dainty viands.

6.63.d: पुरु हि वां पुरुभुजा देष्णं धेनुं न इषं पिन्वतमसक्राम् । स्तुतश्च वां माध्वी सुष्टुतिश्च रसाश्च ये वामनु रातिमग्मन् ॥
6.63.e: Lords of great wealth, manifold is your bounty: ye filled our cow with food that never faileth.  Lovers of sweetness! yours are praise and singers, and poured libations which have sought your favour.

6.63.d: उत म ऋज्रे पुरयस्य रघ्वी सुमीळ्हे शतं पेरुके च पक्वा । शाण्डो दाद्धिरणिनः स्मद्दिष्टीन्दश वशासो अभिषाच ऋष्वान् ॥
6.63.e: Mine were two mares of Puraya, brown, swift-footed; a hundred with Sumidha, food with Peruk  Sanda gave ten gold-decked and well-trained horses, tame and obedient and of lofty stature.

6.63.d: सं वां शता नासत्या सहस्राश्वानां पुरुपन्था गिरे दात् । भरद्वाजाय वीर नू गिरे दाद्धता रक्षांसि पुरुदंससा स्युः ॥
6.63.e: Nāsatyas! Purupanthas offered hundreds, thousands of steeds to him who sang your praises,  Gave, Heroes! to the singer Bharadvāja. Ye-Wonder-Workers, let the fiends be slaughtered.
May I with princes share your bliss in freedom.

6.64.d: उदु श्रिय उषसो रोचमाना अस्थुरपां नोर्मयो रुशन्तः । कृणोति विश्वा सुपथा सुगान्यभूदु वस्वी दक्षिणा मघोनी ॥
6.64.e: THE radiant Dawns have risen up for glory, in their white splendour like the waves of waters.  She maketh paths all easy, fair to travel, and, rich, hath shown herself benign and friendly.

6.64.d: भद्रा ददृक्ष उर्विया वि भास्युत्ते शोचिर्भानवो द्यामपप्तन् । आविर्वक्षः कृणुषे शुम्भमानोषो देवि रोचमाना महोभिः ॥
6.64.e: We see that thou art good: far shines thy lustre; thy beams, thy splendours have flown up to heaven.  Decking thyself, thou makest bare thy bosom, shining in majesty, thou Goddess Morning.

6.64.d: वहन्ति सीमरुणासो रुशन्तो गावः सुभगामुर्विया प्रथानाम् । अपेजते शूरो अस्तेव शत्रून्बाधते तमो अजिरो न वोळ्हा ॥
6.64.e: Red are the kine and luminous that bear her the Blessed One who spreadeth through the distance.  The foes she chaseth like a valiant archer, like a swift warrior she repelleth darkness.

6.64.d: सुगोत ते सुपथा पर्वतेष्ववाते अपस्तरसि स्वभानो । सा न आ वह पृथुयामन्नृष्वे रयिं दिवो दुहितरिषयध्यै ॥
6.64.e: Thy ways are easy on the hills: thou passest Invincible! Se1f-luminous! through waters.  So lofty Goddess with thine ample pathway, Daughter of Heaven, bring wealth to give us comfort.

6.64.d: सा वह योक्षभिरवातोषो वरं वहसि जोषमनु । त्वं दिवो दुहितर्या ह देवी पूर्वहूतौ मंहना दर्शता भूः ॥
6.64.e: Dawn, bring me wealth: untroubled, with thine oxen thou bearest riches at thy will and pleasure;  Thou who, a Goddess, Child of Heaven, hast shown thee lovely through bounty when we called thee early.

6.64.d: उत्ते वयश्चिद्वसतेरपप्तन्नरश्च ये पितुभाजो व्युष्टौ । अमा सते वहसि भूरि वाममुषो देवि दाशुषे मर्त्याय ॥
6.64.e: As the birds fly forth from their restingplaces, so men with store of food rise at thy dawning.  Yea, to the liberal mortal who rernaineth at home, O Goddess Dawn, much good thou bringest.

6.65.d: एषा स्या नो दुहिता दिवोजाः क्षितीरुच्छन्ती मानुषीरजीगः । या भानुना रुशता राम्यास्वज्ञायि तिरस्तमसश्चिदक्तून् ॥
6.65.e: SHEDDING her light on human habitations this Child of Heaven hath called us from our slumber;  She who at night-time with her argent lustre hath shown herself e’en through the shades of darkness.

6.65.d: वि तद्ययुररुणयुग्भिरश्वैश्चित्रं भान्त्युषसश्चन्द्ररथाः । अग्रं यज्ञस्य बृहतो नयन्तीर्वि ता बाधन्ते तम ऊर्म्यायाः ॥
6.65.e: All this with red-rayed steeds have they divided: the Dawns on bright cars shine in wondrous fashion.  They, bringing near the stately rite's commencement, drive far away the night's surrounding shadows.

6.65.d: श्रवो वाजमिषमूर्जं वहन्तीर्नि दाशुष उषसो मर्त्याय । मघोनीर्वीरवत्पत्यमाना अवो धात विधते रत्नमद्य ॥
6.65.e: Dawns, bringing hither, to the man who worships, glory and power and might and food and vigour,  Opulent, with imperial sway like heroes, favour your servant and this day enrich him.

6.65.d: इदा हि वो विधते रत्नमस्तीदा वीराय दाशुष उषासः । इदा विप्राय जरते यदुक्था नि ष्म मावते वहथा पुरा चित् ॥
6.65.e: Now is there treasure for the man who serves you, now for the hero, Dawns! who brings oblation;  Now for the singer when he sings the praise-song. Even to one like me ye brought aforetime.

6.65.d: इदा हि त उषो अद्रिसानो गोत्रा गवामङ्गिरसो गृणन्ति । व्य१र्केण बिभिदुर्ब्रह्मणा च सत्या नृणामभवद्देवहूतिः ॥
6.65.e: O Dawn who standest on the mountain ridges, Aṅgirases now praise thy stalls of cattle.  With prayer and holy hymn they burst them open: the heroes' calling on the Gods was fruitful.

6.65.d: उच्छा दिवो दुहितः प्रत्नवन्नो भरद्वाजवद्विधते मघोनि । सुवीरं रयिं गृणते रिरीह्युरुगायमधि धेहि श्रवो नः ॥
6.65.e: Shine on us as of old, thou Child of Heaven,on him, rich Maid! who serves like Bharadvāja.  Give to the singer wealth with noble heroes, and upon us bestow wide-spreading glory.

6.66.d: वपुर्नु तच्चिकितुषे चिदस्तु समानं नाम धेनु पत्यमानम् । मर्तेष्वन्यद्दोहसे पीपाय सकृच्छुक्रं दुदुहे पृश्निरूधः ॥
6.66.e: E'EN to the wise let that be still a wonder to which the general name of Cow is given.  The one hath swelled among mankind for milking: Pṛśni hath drained but once her fair bright udder.

6.66.d: ये अग्नयो न शोशुचन्निधाना द्विर्यत्त्रिर्मरुतो वावृधन्त । अरेणवो हिरण्ययास एषां साकं नृम्णैः पौंस्येभिश्च भूवन् ॥
6.66.e: They who like kindled flames of fire are glowing,. the Maruts, twice and thrice have waxen mighty.  Golden and dustless were their cars, invested with their great strength and their heroic vigour.

6.66.d: रुद्रस्य ये मीळ्हुषः सन्ति पुत्रा याँश्चो नु दाधृविर्भरध्यै । विदे हि माता महो मही षा सेत्पृश्निः सुभ्वे३ गर्भमाधात् ॥
6.66.e: They who are Sons of the rain-pouring Rudra, whom the long-lasting One had power to foster:  The Mighty Ones whose germ great Mother Pṛśni is known to have received for man's advantage.

6.66.d: न य ईषन्ते जनुषोऽया न्व१न्तः सन्तोऽवद्यानि पुनानाः । निर्यद्दुह्रे शुचयोऽनु जोषमनु श्रिया तन्वमुक्षमाणाः ॥
6.66.e: They shrink not from the birth; in this same manner still resting there they purge away reproaches.  When they have streamed forth, brilliant, at their pleasure, with their own splendour they bedew their bodies.

6.66.d: मक्षू न येषु दोहसे चिदया आ नाम धृष्णु मारुतं दधानाः । न ये स्तौना अयासो मह्ना नू चित्सुदानुरव यासदुग्रान् ॥
6.66.e: Even those who bear the brave bold name of Maruts, whom not the active quickly wins for milking.  Even the liberal wards not off those fierce ones, those who are light and agile in their greatness.

6.66.d: त इदुग्राः शवसा धृष्णुषेणा उभे युजन्त रोदसी सुमेके । अध स्मैषु रोदसी स्वशोचिरामवत्सु तस्थौ न रोकः ॥
6.66.e: When, strong in strength and armed with potent weapons, they had united wellformed earth and heaven,  Rodasl stood among these furious Heroes like splendour shining with her native brightness.

6.66.d: अनेनो वो मरुतो यामो अस्त्वनश्वश्चिद्यमजत्यरथीः । अनवसो अनभीशू रजस्तूर्वि रोदसी पथ्या याति साधन् ॥
6.66.e: No team of goats shall draw your car, O Maruts, no horse no charioteer be he who drives it.  Halting not, reinless, through the air it travels, speeding alone its paths through earth and heaven.

6.66.d: नास्य वर्ता न तरुता न्वस्ति मरुतो यमवथ वाजसातौ । तोके वा गोषु तनये यमप्सु स व्रजं दर्ता पार्ये अध द्योः ॥
6.66.e: None may obstruct, none overtake, O Maruts, him whom ye succour in the strife of battle  For sons and progeny, for kine and waters: he bursts the cow-stall on the day of trial.

6.66.d: प्र चित्रमर्कं गृणते तुराय मारुताय स्वतवसे भरध्वम् । ये सहांसि सहसा सहन्ते रेजते अग्ने पृथिवी मखेभ्यः ॥
6.66.e: Bring a bright hymn to praise the band of Maruts, the Singers, rapid, strong in native vigour,  Who conquer mighty strength with strength more mighty: earth shakes in terror at their wars, O Agni.

6.66.d: त्विषीमन्तो अध्वरस्येव दिद्युत्तृषुच्यवसो जुह्वो३ नाग्नेः । अर्चत्रयो धुनयो न वीरा भ्राजज्जन्मानो मरुतो अधृष्टाः ॥
6.66.e: Bright like the flashing flames of sacrifices, like tongues of fire impetuous in their onset,  Chanting their psalm, singing aloud, like heroes, splendid from birth, invincible, the Maruts.

6.66.d: तं वृधन्तं मारुतं भ्राजदृष्टिं रुद्रस्य सूनुं हवसा विवासे । दिवः शर्धाय शुचयो मनीषा गिरयो नाप उग्रा अस्पृध्रन् ॥
6.66.e: That swelling band I call with invocation, the brood of Rudra, armed with glittering lances.  Pure hymns are meet for that celestial army: like floods and mountains have the Strong Ones battled.
